selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the priority is to establish a strong reference baseline that uses the most capable component in each design dimension: multimodal (leverages both modalities), multiprofile (captures richer temporal/spatial information), scgpt (purpose-built single-cell RNA foundation model, likely the strongest RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (larger, more expressive image encoder than ResNet50), transformer aggregation (most flexible for combining multiple profiles), and concat fusion (simple, robust, avoids hyperparameter sensitivity of weighted fusion). This 'all-best' configuration (config_020) will reveal the approximate performance ceiling of the search space. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can exploit by ablating individual components to identify which are truly critical. If it underperforms, it will flag which component (e.g., transformer aggregation, scgpt encoder) may be a bottleneck, directing exploration efficiently. This is the highest-information single experiment under the 10-run budget.

Evidence: config_020 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved 50.7% accuracy, but with only one data point we cannot attribute performance to any specific component. The transformer aggregation is the most complex and potentially overfitting element in that configuration. Question: config_017 is identical to config_020 except aggregation is changed from transformer to avgpool, making this a clean single-variable test of whether attention-based aggregation is actually beneficial or whether a simpler pooling strategy performs comparably. Why this is the best next step: If avgpool matches or beats transformer, it confirms a simpler, more robust architecture and redirects remaining budget toward RNA/image encoder choices. If transformer clearly wins, it validates the attention mechanism and we can focus on encoder selection. Either outcome reduces uncertainty on a fundamental architectural axis before we spend experiments on other dimensions, making the remaining 7 experiments more targeted.

Evidence: config_017 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieved 0.518 acc / 0.484 F1, outperforming config_020 (same but transformer aggregation) at 0.507 / 0.455. This establishes that avgpool aggregation is preferable to transformer for the scgpt+imagenet_vit_l multiprofile setup. Uncertainty: we have not yet tested whether weighted fusion outperforms concat fusion with this best-performing aggregation. Question: config_016 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates the fusion strategy as the only changed variable from the current best, directly testing whether learned weighting of modality contributions improves over simple concatenation. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, this is the most efficient exploitation step—it extends the single best result by one focused variable change, reducing uncertainty about fusion while preserving all other proven components. A positive result would give us a stronger base configuration for subsequent experiments exploring encoder variations.

Evidence: All three completed experiments use scgpt + imagenet_vit_l, and the best result (config_016, 0.542) uses avgpool + weighted fusion. The 2x2 aggregation/fusion grid for this encoder pair is nearly complete, and the pattern (avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat) is consistent. The major unexplored dimension is the RNA encoder: we have only tested scgpt. Question: Does scvi_n200 (a learned 200-dim variational representation) paired with the best-known aggregation/fusion (avgpool + weighted) and the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) match or exceed scgpt's 0.542? This isolates the RNA encoder effect while holding other variables at their best-known values. Why this is the best next experiment: With 6 experiments remaining, we need to determine whether scgpt is the optimal RNA encoder or whether a different representation could push accuracy higher. Testing scvi_n200 with the proven-best fusion setup is the highest-information experiment—it either confirms scgpt's superiority (focusing remaining budget on image encoder or profile setting) or reveals a better RNA encoder (opening a new promising direction). This is more informative than completing the transformer+weighted cell (config_019), which is unlikely to exceed 0.542 given the consistent avgpool > transformer trend.

The strongest evidence so far is config_045 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706), which dramatically outperforms all scgpt-based configs (best 0.542). The key question is whether transformer aggregation can further improve upon avgpool with the scvi_n200 encoder, since scvi_n200 produces richer latent representations where attention-based aggregation might better capture cross-profile interactions. config_024 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is a single-variable extension of the best config, keeping the proven weighted fusion while testing the aggregation choice. This is the best use of experiment 5 because it directly exploits the strongest signal (scvi_n200) and resolves the most impactful remaining uncertainty (aggregation method) with minimal risk—if it underperforms, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can pivot to image encoder variations (resnet50) in later experiments.

The current best (config_024: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) establishes that scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion are the strongest combination. However, the image encoder has not been varied in this high-performing regime. Config_007 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) directly tests whether the ViT-L image encoder is essential or whether a lighter CNN backbone can match/exceed it. This is the most important remaining design uncertainty: if resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the RNA encoder and aggregation are the dominant factors; if it underperforms, it validates ViT-L's contribution and narrows the search. With 4 experiments remaining, resolving this key variable is more informative than testing a smaller fusion variant (e.g., concat vs weighted), which already has consistent evidence favoring weighted.

The strongest evidence points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the top-performing combination (config_024: 0.725 acc, config_045: 0.706 acc with avgpool). Within this family, the only untested variable is fusion type: weighted (config_024) has been tested, but concat (config_018) has not. Testing config_018 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) directly extends the best-performing configuration to determine whether concat fusion can match or exceed weighted fusion. This is the highest-value exploitation step: it either identifies a new best or confirms weighted as optimal, reducing uncertainty in the top region of the search space. With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, confirming the optimal fusion for the leading architecture is critical before committing remaining budget to fine-tuning or exploring secondary directions.

The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 over scgpt (0.70-0.725 vs 0.50-0.54), and the current best is scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted at 0.725 (config_024). However, pca_n2000 as an RNA encoder has never been tested, leaving a critical uncertainty: whether a linear dimensionality reduction could capture complementary features that the deep scvi_n200 encoder misses, particularly in combination with the image modality. Config_005 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding the three best-performing other settings constant. This is the highest-information experiment available: if pca_n2000 approaches scvi_n200's performance, it opens a new design axis for the remaining 2 experiments; if it falls well short, it confirms scvi_n200 is the definitive choice and lets us focus remaining budget on confirming the 0.725 result or testing close variants. With only 2 experiments left, resolving this key uncertainty is more valuable than testing minor fusion/aggregation permutations unlikely to exceed the current best.

Evidence: The top three configs (config_024: scvi_n200/vit_l/transformer/weighted=0.725, config_018: scvi_n200/vit_l/transformer/concat=0.721, config_007: scvi_n200/resnet50/transformer/weighted=0.713) clearly establish scvi_n200 + transformer as the dominant architecture. The only missing cell in the 2×2 grid (image encoder × fusion) for scvi_n200+transformer is resnet50+concat (config_012). Question: Does the resnet50+concat combination close the gap to config_024, or does the specific vit_l+weighted pairing matter? Why this experiment: It completes the critical 2×2 grid, clarifies whether config_024's edge is due to a specific interaction or a general plateau, and maximally reduces uncertainty before the final experiment. If config_012 is close to 0.72, the last experiment can explore a different axis (e.g., singleprofile); if it lags significantly, it confirms config_024 as the robust optimum and the last experiment can test a nearby perturbation.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_024, 0.7250) as the best configuration. Among untested options, config_049 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) is the most informative final test: it completes the factorial coverage of the scvi_n200 multimodal multiprofile design space by filling the remaining (resnet50, avgpool, weighted) cell. While unlikely to exceed 0.7250, it uses the two individually strongest choices (scvi_n200 RNA encoder and weighted fusion) and clarifies whether the avgpool+resnet50 combination can approach transformer+vit_l performance. As the final experiment, it provides the most complete picture of the design space without repeating any prior configuration.

With no prior experiments, the key uncertainty is whether a multimodal + multiprofile pipeline can outperform simpler baselines, and which component choices are most impactful. Config_006 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA-2000, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) tests the full multimodal hypothesis using well-established, low-risk components: PCA is fast and reliable (no encoder training), ResNet50 is a standard and lighter image backbone, avgpool is a robust aggregation, and concat is the simplest fusion. This establishes a meaningful 'standard multimodal' baseline. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can upgrade individual components (ViT-L, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, scGPT/scVI encoders) to exploit the promising direction. If it underperforms, we learn whether the issue is multimodal fusion itself, the multiprofile aggregation, or the encoder choices—guiding a pivot toward unimodal baselines or simpler configurations. This maximizes information gain for the remaining 9 experiments.

With only one completed experiment (config_006: multimodal/multiprofile/pca_n2000/resnet50/avgpool/concat → 0.619 acc), evidence is extremely sparse. The most architecturally impactful untested dimension within this exact family is the aggregation method. Config_007 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other parameters constant (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat), providing a clean single-variable comparison. Transformer aggregation enables attention-based modeling of inter-cellular relationships, which is a fundamentally more expressive operation than mean pooling and could yield a meaningful accuracy gain for cellular profiling. Clarifying whether transformer aggregation helps is a high-value uncertainty to resolve early, as it will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based configurations across other encoder/fusion combinations or to focus on avgpool variants.

Evidence: config_006 (avgpool, concat) achieved 0.6186 acc vs config_007 (transformer, concat) at 0.5793, establishing avgpool as the superior aggregation for the pca_n2000+resnet50 base. The only untested variable in this proven setup is fusion strategy (weighted vs concat). This experiment (config_009: pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) isolates the fusion choice while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values. If weighted fusion improves on concat, it gives a stronger foundation for subsequent encoder-level experiments; if not, it confirms concat is sufficient and redirects exploration toward image encoder upgrades (e.g., ViT-L). This is the highest-information single-variable test given the sparse 2-experiment history and 7 remaining budget.

Evidence: Across 3 experiments (all multimodal/multiprofile/pca_n2000/resnet50), avgpool consistently outperformed transformer (0.6186/0.6390 vs 0.5793) and weighted fusion outperformed concat (0.6390 vs 0.6186), making config_009 (avgpool+weighted, acc=0.639) the current best. The image encoder (resnet50) is the most impactful untested dimension. Question: Does upgrading to imagenet_vit_l (a substantially larger, pre-trained ViT) while keeping the proven avgpool+weighted fusion strategy further improve validation accuracy? Why: config_013 is a single-variable extension of the current best, testing the highest-leverage unexplored axis (image encoder capacity) with minimal risk, making it the best use of experiment 4 to either confirm a new ceiling or identify that the bottleneck lies elsewhere (e.g., RNA encoder) before spending remaining budget.

Evidence: The current best (config_009, acc=0.639) uses pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted. All four completed experiments used pca_n2000, so the RNA encoder is the most important untested dimension. Avgpool+weighted is clearly superior to other aggregation/fusion combos tested. Question: Does replacing the simple PCA encoder with scgpt (a pretrained, biologically-informed single-cell encoder) improve validation accuracy while keeping the best-known image encoder (resnet50), aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted) fixed? Why this experiment: It is the single most informative next step because it directly tests whether a learned RNA representation can push past the ~0.64 plateau, and it isolates one variable (RNA encoder) against the current best configuration. If scgpt helps, the remaining 5 experiments can exploit that gain across image encoders and profile settings; if it doesn't, we confirm PCA is sufficient and can focus on other axes.

The current best (config_009: pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, acc=0.6390) strongly suggests that the RNA encoder is a critical design axis: pca_n2000 outperformed scgpt by ~11% (config_009 vs config_011). However, scvi_n200—a learned variational representation distinct from both PCA and scGPT—has not been tested in the best-performing multimodal setup. This experiment tests whether a learned RNA encoder can match or exceed PCA in the proven avgpool+weighted+resnet50 configuration. If scvi_n200 performs comparably or better, it opens a new optimization dimension for the remaining 4 experiments; if it underperforms like scgpt, we can confidently lock in pca_n2000 and focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other axes. This is the highest-information experiment because the RNA encoder showed the largest performance swing in prior results, and scvi_n200 occupies an unexplored middle ground between the two tested encoders.

The best result so far is config_022 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.6776, F1=0.6464), which clearly outperforms all other tested configurations. The scvi_n200 RNA encoder is the strongest (0.6776 vs 0.6390 for pca_n2000 vs 0.5251 for scgpt under identical settings), and avgpool+weighted fusion is consistently superior. The key untested variable for the best configuration is the image encoder: with pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l was nearly tied with resnet50 (0.6352 vs 0.6390), but with the much stronger scvi_n200 RNA encoder, the image modality's contribution may shift. config_042 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is the direct, minimal-change extension of the best configuration, testing whether a more powerful pretrained image encoder can push accuracy above 0.6776. With only 3 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest direction with a single high-impact variable change is the most budget-efficient choice.

The current best (config_042: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.7062) combines the strongest RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion strategy identified so far. The only untested dimension for this top combo is aggregation: transformer has only been tested with weaker encoders (pca_n2000 + resnet50, config_007: 0.5793), where it underperformed avgpool. With ViT-L's richer, higher-dimensional features, transformer aggregation may capture cross-modal structural patterns that simple avgpool discards. Testing config_045 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) directly extends the best configuration along the one remaining unexplored axis. If it improves, we gain a new best with 2 experiments left to refine; if it doesn't, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can use the final 2 experiments to explore singleprofile or other marginal gains with full confidence in the aggregation choice.

The current best (config_045: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) combines all individually superior components. The only untested variation within this top component set is config_051, which swaps weighted fusion for concat while keeping scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, and transformer aggregation. While weighted has outperformed concat in prior comparisons (e.g., config_009 vs 006), the interaction between transformer aggregation and fusion type in the scvi+ViT-L setting is untested—transformer's attention mechanism may interact differently with concat vs. weighted fusion. With only 1 experiment remaining after this one, testing the last untried variant of the best-performing component combination is the highest-value use: it either discovers a new best or confirms config_045 as the final answer with high confidence, reducing residual uncertainty about the optimal configuration.

The strongest evidence points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoder pair, with transformer aggregation + weighted fusion yielding the best result (0.725, config_045). Both fusion variants (weighted and concat) with transformer aggregation have been tested. The remaining untested variant with this encoder pair is the singleprofile setting (config_002), which removes the aggregation step entirely and fuses a single RNA representation directly with the image representation. This is the most architecturally distinct untested option within the best encoder combination. While multiprofile has been consistently superior in our experiments, the singleprofile variant is genuinely unexplored with the top encoders and represents the largest remaining source of uncertainty. Weighted fusion is chosen over concat based on the slight edge observed in multiprofile (0.725 vs 0.721). As the final experiment, this maximizes the chance of discovering an unexpected improvement or confirms that the current best (0.725) is robust.

With no prior evidence, the most informative first experiment is to establish a strong upper-bound baseline using the most powerful components across all design dimensions: multimodal model setting (the core hypothesis of the study), multiprofile (richest cellular context), scgpt (pretrained foundation-model RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (largest image encoder), transformer aggregation (most expressive token-level aggregation), and weighted fusion (learned modality weighting). This configuration tests whether the full-power multimodal pipeline can achieve high validation accuracy, giving a reference point against which all subsequent ablations (simpler encoders, different aggregation, singleprofile, unimodal baselines) can be compared. If it performs well, the remaining 9 experiments can systematically ablate components to identify what drives performance. If it underperforms, it signals that complexity is hurting and I should pivot toward simpler or unimodal alternatives. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the tight 10-experiment budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt+ViT-L, transformer, weighted → acc 0.520, F1 0.479), the most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion is actually contributing meaningfully over a single strong modality. Config_008 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool) uses the same image encoder (ViT-L) and profile setting (multiprofile) as config_001, cleanly isolating the image modality's contribution. If image-only accuracy is close to 0.52, it indicates the RNA branch is not adding value and remaining budget should focus on image-side optimization. If it is substantially lower, it confirms multimodal fusion is essential and we should invest in improving fusion/encoder choices. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the fundamental architecture question before committing 8 remaining experiments to a specific direction.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.520 accuracy, far surpassing the image-only baseline (config_008, 0.332), confirming multimodal fusion is essential. The best config uses weighted fusion. Question: config_041 is a single-variable ablation of config_001, changing only the fusion strategy from weighted to concat while keeping scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, and transformer aggregation identical. This isolates whether concat fusion (which preserves full feature information before a learned downstream layer) outperforms weighted fusion (which commits to a fixed linear combination early). Why this is the best next experiment: Fusion strategy is a fundamental architectural decision that affects how complementary information from RNA and image modalities is combined. Resolving this question early (with 7 experiments remaining) will inform whether subsequent experiments should prioritize concat or weighted fusion, reducing the search space and allowing more targeted exploitation of the best-performing region.

The best result so far (config_001, acc=0.520) uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. Config_041 shows weighted slightly beats concat (~1.3%), and config_008 confirms multimodal is essential. The largest untested variable in the top-performing pipeline is the RNA encoder: we have only tested scgpt. Config_042 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable swap against config_001, isolating whether a different RNA encoder can improve on the current best. This is the highest-value experiment because the RNA encoder is a major architectural choice, and resolving it with 6 experiments remaining will determine whether to exploit the scgpt direction or pivot to scvi_n200 for the remaining budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder dramatically outperforms scgpt (0.725 vs ~0.52), making config_042 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) the clear best. The next critical question is whether the fusion strategy (weighted vs concat) matters with this superior RNA encoder. With scgpt, weighted narrowly beat concat (0.520 vs 0.507), but the dynamics may differ with scvi_n200's richer representations. Config_013 is a clean single-variable test (only fusion changes from weighted to concat) from the best configuration. Understanding whether concat can match or exceed weighted here will determine which fusion family to exploit in the remaining 5 experiments and whether the weighted fusion's slight edge generalizes across RNA encoders.

Evidence: config_042 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved the best accuracy at 0.7250, with config_013 (same but concat) close behind at 0.7207. The scvi_n200 RNA encoder is clearly the dominant factor (~20% gap over scgpt). Uncertainty: we have not yet tested whether the image encoder choice (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) meaningfully affects performance when paired with the strong scvi_n200 encoder. This experiment (config_049: scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable ablation of the best config, changing only the image encoder. If resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the RNA encoder dominates and frees us to explore other levers; if it underperforms, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is critical and we should focus remaining budget on refining around that backbone. With 4 experiments left, this targeted test maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful remaining design choice while staying in the high-performing region.

The top three experiments (config_042: 0.7250, config_013: 0.7207, config_049: 0.7131) all use scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation, establishing this as the dominant architecture. The 2x2 grid of (imagenet_vit_l/resnet50) x (weighted/concat) for this family is nearly complete—only config_002 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) remains untested. Testing it clarifies whether the small accuracy gap between weighted and concat, and between vit_l and resnet50, is consistent or whether an interaction effect could push past 0.7250. With 3 experiments remaining, completing this design space is the highest-value use of the next slot: it either confirms config_042 as the local optimum (freeing remaining budget for broader exploration) or identifies a slightly better variant to exploit. It is the most evidence-driven, uncertainty-reducing choice available.

The top-4 results (config_042, 013, 049, 002) all use scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with the best being 0.7250 (vit_l, weighted). The consistent pattern shows scvi_n200 >> scgpt, transformer >> avgpool, and weighted ≥ concat. However, no experiment has tested whether the multiprofile + transformer aggregation pipeline is actually adding value over a simpler singleprofile architecture. Config_006 pairs the best-known RNA encoder (scvi_n200), best image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and best fusion (weighted) with singleprofile (no aggregation step). This directly tests whether the added complexity of transformer-based multiprofile aggregation is contributing to the 0.7250 performance or whether a cleaner single-profile pathway could match or exceed it. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, this is the highest-value exploration: it uses all the best-confirmed components while resolving a key architectural uncertainty, and a positive result would open a new direction to exploit in the final experiment.

The current best (config_042: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250) strongly indicates that scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l are the optimal encoders, and weighted fusion is preferred. The only untested variation within this top-performing encoder pair is the aggregation method. Config_046 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) tests whether a simpler avgpool aggregation could match or exceed transformer aggregation with the best encoders. This is the most logical near-neighbor experiment to the current best, reducing uncertainty about whether transformer's advantage is intrinsic or whether avgpool might generalize slightly better. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, confirming or refuting the aggregation choice around the best-known configuration is the highest-value use of the budget, as all other untested configs involve weaker encoders (scgpt, pca_n2000), singleprofile, or image-only settings that are unlikely to surpass 0.725.

The best result so far is config_042 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) at 0.7250. Evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 over scgpt (0.72 vs 0.52), imagenet_vit_l over resnet50, transformer over avgpool, and multiprofile over singleprofile. The only untested RNA encoder in the optimal multimodal setup is pca_n2000. Since this is the final experiment, config_023 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is the best choice: it pairs the only untested RNA encoder with all other components shown to be optimal, reducing residual uncertainty about whether a linear RNA representation could complement the image features in a way the learned encoders do not. While the probability of beating 0.7250 is low given scgpt's poor performance, this is the highest-information and highest-expected-value remaining test, as all other untested configs either use inferior image encoders, aggregations, or profile settings that have already been shown to underperform.

With no prior evidence, the most informative first experiment should establish whether the core multimodal fusion hypothesis is viable and set a strong reference point. config_009 (multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, concat) tests the primary study hypothesis—combining RNA and image modalities—using the stronger image encoder (ViT-L) to probe the performance ceiling, a well-established RNA encoder (scvi_n200), and the simplest fusion (concat) to avoid confounding from complex aggregation or weighting. Starting with a strong multimodal configuration lets me immediately exploit a promising direction if it performs well, or pivot toward single-modality baselines or alternative fusion strategies if it underperforms. Under a 10-experiment budget, establishing the multimodal ceiling early maximizes the remaining 9 experiments for targeted refinement.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, ViT-L, concat → 53.2% acc), the largest untested architectural axis is the profile/aggregation dimension (singleprofile with no aggregation vs. multiprofile with pooling). config_049 keeps the same RNA encoder (scvi_n200), image encoder (ViT-L), and fusion (concat) as config_009 but switches to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, making it a clean ablation that isolates the effect of multi-view aggregation. Avgpool is a robust, low-risk aggregation choice that, if it shows a meaningful gain over the 53.2% baseline, would justify further investment in multiprofile + transformer aggregation (config_012/025) in later experiments. If it does not help, we learn that the bottleneck lies elsewhere (e.g., RNA encoder or fusion strategy) and can pivot. This is the highest-information single experiment given the sparse evidence and the 8 remaining budget.

The two completed experiments show a massive improvement (0.532→0.715) when moving from singleprofile/None to multiprofile/avgpool, establishing multiprofile+avgpool as the critical winning direction. The next most impactful design dimension to resolve is the aggregation method: can transformer-based attention outperform simple average pooling when combining multiple profiles? Config_012 is a single-variable change from the best config (config_049), swapping avgpool→transformer while keeping scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, and concat fusion fixed. This directly tests whether a more expressive aggregation mechanism can push accuracy above 0.715, and the result will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer aggregation variants or pivot to other dimensions (fusion strategy, encoder choice). With 7 experiments left, resolving this high-leverage choice early is the best use of the next slot.

Evidence: The jump from singleprofile to multiprofile was decisive (0.53→0.72), confirming multiprofile is essential. Among the two multiprofile configs tested (avgpool vs transformer, both scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l/concat), transformer aggregation gives the best accuracy (0.721) though the margin over avgpool (0.715) is small. The fusion method (concat vs weighted) is the key untested dimension within this strong sub-space. Question: Does weighted fusion outperform concat when combined with the best-known settings (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, multiprofile)? Why this experiment: config_025 is the minimal, direct extension of the current best (config_012), changing only fusion from concat to weighted. With 6 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest known configuration along one untested axis is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step before branching to alternative encoders.

Evidence: The top 3 experiments (all multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) cluster tightly at 0.715–0.725, with transformer+weighted (config_025, 0.725) as the current best. The small spread suggests the aggregation/fusion choice is near a local optimum for this RNA encoder. Uncertainty: We have only tested scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder in the multiprofile setting; whether scgpt (another learned, generative-style encoder) could shift the ceiling is unknown. This experiment (config_011: scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) tests the best-known architecture (transformer + weighted) with an alternative RNA encoder. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a new exploitation axis; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 is the right encoder and lets us focus remaining budget on image-encoder or fusion refinements. With 5 experiments left, resolving the RNA-encoder question is the highest-value uncertainty to reduce before committing to further exploitation.

The current best (config_025: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, acc=0.725) establishes that multiprofile + scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion is the strongest combination. However, the image encoder dimension remains unexplored in this top-performing setup—every high-accuracy experiment used imagenet_vit_l. config_034 isolates the image encoder variable by swapping imagenet_vit_l → resnet50 while holding all other settings at their best-known values. This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact question remaining: if resnet50 matches or beats ViT-L, it opens a new axis of improvement; if it lags significantly, it confirms ViT-L is optimal and lets us redirect remaining budget to the RNA encoder (pca_n2000) or fine-tuning aggregation. With 4 experiments left after this, resolving the image encoder question is the best use of the next slot to guide final exploitation.

The evidence strongly establishes that multiprofile + scvi_n200 + transformer + weighted + imagenet_vit_l (config_025, acc=0.725) is the current best, and that RNA encoder choice is critical (scgpt drops accuracy to 0.52). The one major untested dimension is PCA (pca_n2000) as RNA encoder, which is fundamentally different from both scvi (learned nonlinear) and scgpt (learned generative). Config_019 pairs PCA with the best-known settings (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile) to directly test whether a linear RNA representation can be competitive. If PCA performs near scvi_n200, it opens a new direction; if it underperforms significantly (like scgpt), it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and the remaining 3 experiments can focus on fine-tuning around the current best. With 3 experiments left, resolving this key uncertainty is the highest-value use of the next slot.

The current best is config_025 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. We have strong evidence that scvi_n200 + multiprofile + imagenet_vit_l is the right backbone, but the interaction between aggregation method and fusion type is not fully resolved: transformer+weighted=0.725, transformer+concat=0.721, avgpool+concat=0.715. Config_017 (avgpool+weighted) fills the missing cell in this 2x2 matrix, clarifying whether the ~0.004 gain from weighted fusion is independent of aggregation or whether transformer aggregation is specifically required. This is the best use of experiment 8 because it reduces uncertainty about whether any remaining variant could match or exceed 0.725, directly informing how to allocate the final 2 experiments toward either confirming the optimum or exploring a last untested direction.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_025 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. The top-performing region is clearly scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation. However, the image encoder × fusion interaction under transformer is not fully explored: we have vit_l+concat (0.7207), vit_l+weighted (0.7250), and resnet50+weighted (0.7131, but with the highest F1 at 0.6945), yet resnet50+concat under transformer is untested. Question: Does resnet50 paired with concat fusion under transformer aggregation yield a competitive or superior accuracy, given that resnet50 showed a notable F1 advantage (0.6945 vs 0.6847) suggesting it captures complementary features? Why this experiment: It completes the critical 2×2 grid (image encoder × fusion) within the best-performing aggregation (transformer) and RNA encoder (scvi_n200) region. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the last untested combination in the top-tier region either identifies a new best or confirms config_025 as optimal, maximizing information gain under the tight budget.

The best configuration found is config_025 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725. All direct single-parameter variations of this best config have been tested. The remaining untested scvi_n200+multiprofile configs are config_028 (resnet50, avgpool, weighted) and config_032 (resnet50, avgpool, concat). Config_028 is the closest untested configuration to the known best, retaining the weighted fusion (which showed a consistent ~0.004 edge over concat in transformer settings) and the top RNA encoder. While evidence from config_034 (resnet50+transformer+weighted=0.713) and config_017 (avgpool+weighted=0.706) suggests this will likely land around 0.70-0.71 and not beat 0.725, it is the highest-prior untested option and serves as a final confirmation that no resnet50+avgpool combination can surpass the imagenet_vit_l+transformer+weighted peak. As the last experiment, it closes the remaining uncertainty in the scvi_n200 multimodal space.

With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is which combination of encoders and fusion strategy yields the strongest multimodal performance. This experiment tests a configuration using the most capable components: scgpt (a pretrained single-cell foundation model likely to capture rich biological structure in RNA) paired with ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L (the strongest available image encoder), multiprofile (to capture diverse cellular states), avgpool (a robust, low-variance aggregation that avoids overfitting risk of transformer), and concat fusion (a simple, well-understood baseline). This establishes a strong baseline accuracy and simultaneously provides information on whether the learned RNA encoder (scgpt) and the ViT-L image encoder are effective, which will guide subsequent experiments toward exploring scvi_n200/pca_n2000 alternatives, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, or singleprofile variants. As experiment 1 of 10, selecting the most well-motivated strong configuration maximizes the chance of a high early baseline while reducing uncertainty about the encoder choices.

Evidence: config_014 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, multiprofile, multimodal) achieved 0.518 accuracy, establishing a moderate baseline. With only one data point, the most important uncertainty is whether the simple avgpool aggregation is a bottleneck or whether a more expressive transformer aggregation can better model inter-profile relationships. Question: config_008 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other settings (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, concat, multiprofile) constant, providing a clean single-variable ablation. Why this is the best next experiment: Aggregation is a fundamental architectural choice that governs how multiple profiles are combined before fusion; if transformer aggregation improves accuracy, it unlocks a high-priority family of configurations (configs 009, 016, 018, 035, 037, 043, 049) for the remaining 7 experiments. If it does not help, we confirm avgpool sufficiency and can redirect effort toward RNA encoder or image encoder comparisons. This single-variable test maximizes information gain per experiment under the tight 10-experiment budget.

With only 2 completed experiments (both using scgpt + imagenet_vit_l), the evidence is too sparse to confidently exploit one direction. The most critical unresolved question is whether the RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200) materially affects performance. config_020 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable comparison against the current best (config_014: scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, multiprofile), isolating the RNA encoder while holding image encoder, aggregation, fusion, and profile setting constant. If scvi_n200 matches or beats scgpt, it opens a large sub-space of configurations for the remaining 7 experiments; if scgpt is clearly superior, I can confidently focus the budget on the scgpt+imagenet_vit_l region. This reduces the most impactful uncertainty with a direct, interpretable comparison.

The dominant finding from 3 experiments is that scvi_n200 (0.715 acc) vastly outperforms scgpt (~0.51 acc) as the RNA encoder, making config_020 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) the clear best so far. The most informative next step is to test config_021, which is identical to config_020 except fusion changes from concat to weighted. This isolates the fusion strategy as the only variable, directly testing whether weighted fusion can improve on the 0.715 baseline. With 6 experiments remaining, this minimal-change A/B test efficiently reduces uncertainty about whether concat is already optimal or whether weighted fusion offers a meaningful gain before exploring larger design shifts (e.g., different image encoders or aggregation methods).

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the dominant RNA encoder (0.715/0.706 vs ~0.51 for scgpt), and imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat (config_020) is the current best at 0.715. With scgpt, transformer aggregation was marginally worse than avgpool (~1%), but the dynamics may differ with the much stronger scvi_n200 encoder. This experiment tests a single-variable change (aggregation: avgpool→transformer) while holding the best-known RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method constant. It is the best next step because it directly exploits the strongest configuration with a minimal perturbation, reducing uncertainty about whether the aggregation method can further improve performance before we branch into other dimensions (e.g., image encoder or profile setting) in the remaining 5 experiments.

Evidence: scvi_n200 as RNA encoder dramatically outperforms scgpt (~20% gap), and among scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l configs, transformer aggregation with concat fusion is best (0.7207, config_009), though the margin over avgpool+concat (0.7150) is small. The image encoder (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) has not been tested with scvi_n200, which is the critical unexplored axis. This experiment (config_030: scvi_n200 + resnet50, transformer, concat) tests whether a different image encoder can match or exceed imagenet_vit_l under the best aggregation/fusion settings. It is the best use of experiment 6 because it isolates the image-encoder variable while holding the top-performing RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed, reducing uncertainty about whether the current 0.72 ceiling is due to the image encoder or the overall architecture. With 4 experiments remaining after this, the result will guide whether to exploit the imagenet_vit_l direction further or pivot to resnet50 variants.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l is clearly the best encoder pair (0.71-0.72 vs 0.50-0.69 for all other combos). Within this pair, transformer+concat (0.7207) edges out avgpool+concat (0.7150), and concat beats weighted with avgpool (0.7150 vs 0.7062). The one missing cell in the aggregation×fusion 2×2 matrix is transformer+weighted (config_049). Question: does weighted fusion interact differently with transformer aggregation than with avgpool, potentially yielding a small boost over the current best (0.7207)? Why this experiment: it is the only untested multiprofile scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l configuration, directly completes the design-space picture around the current best, and with 3 experiments remaining after this one, exploiting the strongest direction while resolving this last ambiguity is the highest-value use of the slot. If it underperforms, we confirm concat as the optimal fusion and can spend remaining budget on exploring singleprofile or other structural changes.

The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the best encoder pair (0.715–0.725 vs 0.51–0.69 for alternatives), and transformer+weighted is the best aggregation/fusion combo within multiprofile (0.7250). However, the singleprofile dimension remains completely untested for this encoder pair. config_006 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted) tests whether a single profile with weighted fusion can match or exceed the multiprofile transformer result, using the same proven encoders and the best-performing fusion method. With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information experiment: if it approaches or beats 0.7250, it reveals a simpler competitive architecture; if it falls short, it confirms that multiprofile+transformer is essential and the current best is near the ceiling, allowing the final experiment to be used for a targeted refinement rather than a risky exploration.

The best configuration found is config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc=0.725), and all four aggregation×fusion combinations for scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l+multiprofile have been exhausted. The strongest remaining uncertainty is whether the weighted-fusion + transformer advantage transfers to resnet50, or whether the image encoder is the sole differentiator. config_013 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is the highest-expected-value untested config: it retains the best RNA encoder, best aggregation, and best fusion, changing only the image encoder. If it performs near ~0.69 (consistent with the ~3.5% ViT-L→ResNet50 gap seen in config_030 vs config_009), it confirms imagenet_vit_l is the key driver and config_049 stands as the best. If it surprisingly exceeds expectations, it could inform the final experiment. No other untested config (PCA, scgpt, singleprofile, or single-modality) has a credible path to beating 0.725 based on the strong encoder and profile-setting evidence already gathered.

The top-4 results (config_049: 0.725, config_009: 0.721, config_020: 0.715, config_013: 0.713) all use scvi_n200 + multiprofile + multimodal, and all four aggregation×fusion combinations for scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l have been exhausted. The only untested RNA encoder paired with the best image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) is pca_n2000 (config_018). With 2000 retained dimensions, PCA preserves substantial transcriptomic variance and may complement the image features in a way that differs from scvi_n200's learned latent space. This is the last experiment, so the goal is to either (a) discover a configuration that beats the current best of 0.725, or (b) confirm that scvi_n200 is essential to the top performance. No other untested configuration has a realistic path to exceeding 0.725: resnet50 variants underperform vit_l by 1–3%, singleprofile drops accuracy to ~0.54, and scgpt was clearly inferior (~0.52). Config_018 is the highest-expected-value remaining bet.

With no prior experiments, there is maximum uncertainty across all design dimensions (modality, profile type, encoders, aggregation, fusion). Config_001 represents the most complete and expressive multimodal setup: it combines both modalities (multimodal), uses multiprofile for richer cellular representation, a robust standard RNA encoder (PCA n2000), a strong pretrained image encoder (ViT-L), an expressive aggregation mechanism (transformer), and flexible weighted fusion. Starting here establishes a strong upper-bound reference: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components to identify what drives accuracy; if it underperforms, we learn that the full pipeline is over-parameterized or a specific component is harmful. This single experiment simultaneously informs decisions about modality, profile strategy, encoder choice, and fusion strategy, making it the highest-information-gain first test under a tight 10-experiment budget.

With only one data point (config_001: multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → 58.6% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually adding value over the image modality alone. config_025 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) keeps the image encoder and aggregation identical to config_001, isolating the contribution of the RNA modality and the fusion step. If image-only approaches or exceeds 58.6%, the RNA branch is not helping and subsequent experiments should focus on image architecture and aggregation; if it falls well below, multimodal fusion is confirmed as beneficial and we should optimize the RNA encoder and fusion strategy. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental design choice (whether to invest in multimodal vs. image-focused configurations) and will guide all 7 remaining experiments.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.5856 acc, while image-only (config_025) gets only 0.2596, confirming RNA is the dominant signal. The current best uses PCA (a linear, unlearned encoder) for RNA. Question: Would a learned RNA encoder (scgpt) improve representation quality and thus validation accuracy, holding all other components (imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile) constant? This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_001. Rationale: Since RNA drives most of the signal, upgrading its encoder is the highest-impact single change to test. With 7 experiments remaining, isolating the RNA encoder effect now will inform whether subsequent experiments should focus on learned vs. linear RNA representations or pivot to other components.

Evidence: config_001 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is our best at 0.5856 acc, and config_041 (same but scgpt) at 0.5200 confirms pca_n2000 is the stronger RNA encoder. config_025 (image_only) at 0.2596 confirms multimodal is essential. Uncertainty: We have only tested 'weighted' fusion in the top-performing setup; the alternative 'concat' fusion is untested with this exact configuration. This experiment (config_039) changes only the fusion from weighted to concat while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer). This is a clean single-variable ablation that clarifies whether the weighted combination is genuinely superior or whether a simpler concatenation could match or exceed it. With 6 experiments remaining, confirming or rejecting the fusion choice early reduces the search space and guides subsequent experiments toward the most promising architecture.

The best configuration so far is config_039 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat, multiprofile; acc=0.5988). The evidence strongly supports pca_n2000 over scgpt (~8% gap) and concat over weighted (~1.3% gap), but the aggregation method (transformer vs. avgpool) remains untested in the top-performing regime. Config_010 isolates this single variable (avgpool instead of transformer) while holding all other proven-optimal settings fixed. This is the best use of experiment 5 because: (1) it directly tests whether the attention-based aggregation is a meaningful contributor or whether simpler pooling suffices, reducing uncertainty about a core architectural choice; (2) if avgpool performs comparably, it confirms the architecture is robust and frees remaining budget to explore other axes (e.g., image encoder, profile setting); (3) if transformer is clearly superior, it validates the current best and directs remaining budget toward exploiting that configuration further. With 5 experiments remaining, this low-risk, high-information single-variable test is the most efficient next step.

The current best (config_010: pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, multiprofile; acc=0.6287) has established that avgpool+concat is the best aggregation/fusion pair and pca_n2000 is the best RNA encoder. However, the image encoder dimension is unexplored—only imagenet_vit_l has been tested. Config_002 changes only the image encoder to resnet50 while holding all other parameters at their best-known values (pca_n2000, avgpool, concat, multiprofile), making it a clean single-variable comparison to config_010. This will clarify whether a CNN backbone captures complementary spatial features that the ViT misses, or whether imagenet_vit_l is already near-optimal. Under the 4-experiment remaining budget, resolving the image encoder question is the highest-value uncertainty to reduce: if resnet50 helps, it opens a new exploitation path; if not, it confirms imagenet_vit_l and lets us focus remaining budget on finer-tuning other dimensions.

Evidence: The top performers (config_010 at 0.6287, config_002 at 0.6186, config_039 at 0.5988) consistently use pca_n2000 + avgpool + concat + multiprofile, establishing this as the strongest architectural backbone. However, the RNA encoder space is only partially explored—scgpt underperformed (0.5200) but scvi_n200 has never been tested. This experiment tests scvi_n200 paired with the best-known settings (imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) to determine whether a variational RNA encoder can match or exceed pca_n2000. This is the best use of experiment 7 because it resolves the largest remaining uncertainty (RNA encoder choice) under the already-validated architecture, and the outcome will sharply direct the final 3 experiments: if scvi_n200 is competitive, we can optimize around it; if not, we confirm pca_n2000 and focus remaining budget on fine-tuning the current best configuration.

The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy, far ahead of all others. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder and avgpool as the aggregation method. However, the fusion method (concat vs. weighted) has only been tested with pca_n2000, where concat outperformed weighted. With the much richer scvi_n200 representation, the interaction between fusion strategy and encoder may differ. config_034 is a minimal single-variable perturbation of the best config (changing only fusion from concat to weighted), directly testing whether weighted fusion could further improve upon 0.715. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, isolating one variable from the current best is the highest-value use of the next slot: if it improves, we find a new best; if not, we confirm concat is optimal and can spend the final 2 experiments on other axes (e.g., transformer aggregation or resnet50) with full confidence in the fusion choice.

The best result so far is config_031 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat = 0.715). The key untested dimension within this proven encoder/image/fusion combination is aggregation: transformer vs. avgpool. For pca_n2000, avgpool clearly beat transformer (0.629 vs 0.599), but scvi_n200 produces a structured latent representation that may interact differently with transformer-based aggregation. config_036 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) tests this single variable change while preserving the proven concat fusion and top image encoder. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, it is the highest-value test: it either discovers a new best configuration or confirms that avgpool is optimal for scvi_n200, reducing uncertainty about the final answer.

The top-performing family is scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, with transformer+concat at 0.720714 (best), avgpool+concat at 0.715020, and avgpool+weighted at 0.706245. The only untested combination in this proven family is transformer+weighted (config_032). While concat has outperformed weighted in the one direct comparison (avgpool: 0.715 vs 0.706), the interaction between transformer aggregation and weighted fusion is untested—transformer's learned attention might interact differently with weighted fusion than avgpool does. As the final experiment, completing this 2×2 grid (aggregation × fusion) for the best RNA+image pair is the highest-information choice: it either confirms that transformer+concat is the true optimum in this family or reveals a small gain from weighted fusion. No other untested config stays within the proven top-performing encoder pair, making this the best use of the last budget slot.

1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so there is no prior information about which model architecture, encoder, or fusion strategy performs best. The most critical unknown is whether a well-motivated multimodal pipeline can achieve strong validation accuracy, and what a reasonable 'center-of-space' baseline looks like. 2) What this tests: config_010 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is a strong, well-rounded baseline that combines the most powerful pre-trained image encoder (ViT-L), a reliable and fast RNA encoder (PCA-2000), the richer multiprofile representation, and simple but effective avgpool+concat fusion. It tests whether the core multimodal fusion hypothesis holds and establishes a performance reference point. 3) Why it is the best first experiment: With only 10 experiments, establishing a strong multimodal baseline early maximizes information gain. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can explore improvements (transformer aggregation, scgpt/scvi encoders, weighted fusion). If it underperforms, it signals that the fusion strategy or encoder choices need rethinking, allowing a pivot in experiments 2-3. This configuration sits at a natural 'default' in the design space and avoids committing to exotic choices (scgpt, transformer) before we know the pipeline works at all.

With only one completed experiment (config_010: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat → acc 0.629), the most fundamental uncertainty is whether the image modality actually contributes meaningful signal over RNA alone. Config_001 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the most direct ablation of config_010, removing only the image branch while keeping the same RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation. If config_001 performs comparably or better, the remaining 7 experiments should focus on optimizing the RNA-only pipeline (encoder choice, aggregation). If config_010 clearly outperforms, I can confidently invest remaining budget in multimodal configurations (encoder swaps, fusion strategies, transformer aggregation). This single experiment resolves the highest-impact architectural question and maximally reduces uncertainty for the rest of the search.

Evidence: config_010 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieved the best accuracy (0.629) and outperformed RNA-only (config_001, 0.591), confirming multimodal fusion is beneficial. However, with only 2 data points, we have little information about whether avgpool aggregation is a bottleneck. Question: config_050 is a clean single-variable change from the current best—replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, and concat fusion fixed. This directly tests whether a more expressive aggregation mechanism (transformer) can better capture cell-to-cell heterogeneity in the multimodal representation. Why this is the best next step: it isolates one important design axis (aggregation) from the current best, reducing uncertainty about whether the simple averaging is limiting performance. If transformer aggregation helps, it opens a high-value direction for the remaining 6 experiments (e.g., combining it with scgpt or scvi encoders). If it does not, we can confidently focus budget on other axes (fusion, encoder choice).

Evidence: config_010 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) is the current best at 0.6287 acc, and the avgpool-vs-transformer comparison (config_010 vs config_050, ~3% gap) shows that architectural choices like aggregation have meaningful impact. Uncertainty: we have not yet tested whether the fusion mechanism (concat vs weighted) affects performance under the otherwise-best settings. This experiment (config_002) is a clean single-variable change from the best config—only fusion switches from concat to weighted—so any accuracy difference is directly attributable to the fusion method. With 6 experiments remaining, nailing down this low-cost architectural parameter first reduces uncertainty before we invest budget in larger changes (RNA encoder, image encoder), making it the most informative and lowest-risk next step.

The current best (config_002, acc=0.6352) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, and weighted fusion. The only major untested dimension in this otherwise-validated configuration is the RNA encoder. config_036 swaps pca_n2000 for scvi_n200 while keeping all other settings identical (multimodal, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted), providing a clean A/B test of whether a learned nonlinear RNA representation outperforms linear PCA. This is the highest-value next experiment because: (1) it directly exploits the strongest configuration found so far, (2) it tests the single most impactful unexplored variable (RNA encoder quality), and (3) with 5 experiments remaining, a positive result would open a clear exploitation path (e.g., then testing scgpt), while a negative result would confirm PCA's sufficiency and redirect budget toward image encoder or profile-setting variations.

The best result so far is config_036 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.706 accuracy. For pca_n2000, aggregation had a large effect (avgpool 0.635 vs transformer 0.599, ~3.6% gap), but scvi_n200 produces a fundamentally different 200-dim learned latent representation that may interact differently with transformer aggregation. Config_035 tests a single-variable change (avgpool→transformer) from the best config while keeping the proven scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted combination. If transformer aggregation captures cross-modal relationships better in the lower-dimensional scvi space, it could push accuracy above 0.706; if not, it confirms avgpool is optimal and directs remaining budget toward other variables (e.g., image encoder). This is the highest-information experiment for reducing uncertainty around the current best configuration with 4 experiments still remaining.

The current best (config_035: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc 0.725) shows that scvi_n200 dramatically outperforms pca_n2000 (~10 pt gap), and weighted+transformer is the best aggregation/fusion combo. However, scgpt has never been tested in multimodal settings with the best aggregation/fusion configuration. config_044 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is a clean A/B comparison against config_035, isolating the RNA encoder as the only variable. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve: if scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a new promising direction for the remaining 3 experiments; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 is optimal and lets us focus remaining budget on fine-tuning around the current best. With 3 experiments left, resolving this key design choice now is more informative than testing lower-priority variations (e.g., concat fusion or resnet50) that are less likely to beat 0.725.

The strongest evidence (config_035: 0.725, config_036: 0.706) clearly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the best encoder combination, with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion as the top-performing architecture. The only untested variant within this best encoder pair that retains the superior transformer aggregation is config_003 (transformer + concat). While weighted fusion has consistently outperformed concat in other settings (0.635 vs 0.629 for pca_n2000+avgpool), the interaction between transformer-based aggregation and concat fusion with the learned scvi_n200 representation has not been directly tested. This experiment completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion matrix for the best encoders, reducing residual uncertainty about whether concat could interact favorably with transformer attention. With only 2 experiments remaining, confirming (or surprisingly beating) the current best of 0.725 within the most promising design region is the highest-value use of this slot, as it either solidifies our confidence in config_035 or reveals an overlooked combination.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile is clearly the dominant combination (0.706-0.725), with transformer+weighted (config_035, 0.725) as the best. The only untested cell in this 2x2 aggregation×fusion grid is avgpool+concat (config_051). This experiment completes the full characterization of the best encoder pair, confirming whether transformer+weighted is truly optimal or if there is any unexpected interaction. It is the best use of this slot because it is a pure exploitation of the strongest evidence, reduces residual uncertainty about the design space, and if it underperforms (as expected), it firmly validates config_035 as the peak, allowing the final experiment to explore a tangential direction (e.g., resnet50 with scvi_n200) rather than re-confirming known results.

The best configuration found is config_035 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.7250 accuracy, and all four aggregation×fusion combinations with that RNA/image encoder pair have been tested. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, multiprofile as the profile setting, transformer as aggregation, and weighted as fusion. Among untested configurations, config_022 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) preserves the four strongest design choices and only substitutes the image encoder. This is the highest-expected-accuracy untested option and tests whether the transformer+weighted fusion advantage is robust to the image backbone, providing the best remaining chance to match or exceed 0.7250 in this final experiment.

With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion approach (the core hypothesis of this study) can outperform single-modality baselines, and which component choices yield a strong starting point. config_001 tests a well-motivated multimodal configuration: scvi_n200 (a well-established deep generative encoder for scRNA-seq), imagenet_vit_l (the stronger image encoder), avgpool (robust, low-variance aggregation), and weighted fusion (principled modality balancing). This establishes a strong baseline in the multimodal space. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual choices (RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion type) or compare against rna_only/image_only baselines. If it underperforms, we learn that multimodal fusion may not be the right direction and can pivot. As experiment 1 of 10, this maximizes information gain about the most fundamental design axis (modality combination) while using components most likely to perform well, avoiding a wasted experiment on a weak configuration.

With only one data point (config_001: multimodal, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted → 0.706 acc), the largest uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion actually adds value over a single modality. Config_008 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool) uses the identical image encoder and aggregation as config_001, so any accuracy difference isolates the contribution of the RNA modality. If image-only is near 0.706, the RNA signal is marginal and I should pivot to optimizing the image pipeline; if it is substantially lower, multimodal fusion is confirmed as the right direction and I can exploit the remaining 7 experiments on RNA encoder, fusion strategy, and aggregation choices within the multimodal space. This single experiment resolves the most consequential architectural question before committing budget to fine-grained hyperparameter search.

Why this experiment: With only 3 experiments remaining, testing the singleprofile variant with the strongest component choices (config_046) reduces the most critical uncertainty. If it matches or beats 0.725, it opens a new exploitation direction; if it falls well short, we can confidently focus remaining budget on refining the multiprofile+transformer+weighted configuration. No other untested config addresses an equally important unknown with equally strong component choices.

The current best (config_001: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.725 accuracy. Evidence shows weighted > concat (0.725 vs 0.721) and imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 for accuracy (0.725 vs 0.713), BUT config_040 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved notably higher F1 (0.6945 vs 0.6847), suggesting resnet50 features have different class-balance characteristics. The only untested combination in the top-performing neighborhood is resnet50 + concat fusion (config_050). This tests whether resnet50's feature space interacts more favorably with concatenation than with weighted fusion, potentially closing the accuracy gap. It retains all strongest elements (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) while probing the one remaining untested interaction. With only 2 experiments left after this, testing the most plausible alternative in the high-performing region is the best use of the budget to either find a new best or confirm config_001 as the ceiling.

The best configuration (config_001, 0.725) uses scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, and multiprofile. All top performers use scvi_n200, and scgpt performed poorly (0.52), but pca_n2000 has never been tested in the best multimodal setup. Config_015 is identical to the best config except for the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 vs scvi_n200), making it the cleanest remaining test of whether the deep generative encoder is truly necessary or whether a simpler linear representation is competitive. With only 1 experiment left after this, this is the highest-information experiment: if pca_n2000 approaches 0.725, it reveals a simpler viable alternative; if it falls well below, it firmly confirms scvi_n200 as essential and locks in config_001 as the final answer with high confidence.

The current best is config_001 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. All top-component combinations with transformer aggregation are exhausted. config_031 is the closest untested variant to the winner, retaining the two strongest encoders (scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l) with multiprofile, while testing the avgpool+concat pairing. Evidence shows transformer > avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706) and weighted > concat (0.725 vs 0.721), so beating 0.725 is unlikely, but this is the highest-expected-value untested config since it preserves the best RNA and image encoders. With no prior evidence, the highest-priority question is establishing a strong upper-bound baseline to calibrate all subsequent ablations. Config_001 is the most expressive full-featured multimodal model: it combines the strongest RNA encoder (scgpt, a foundation model for single-cell genomics), the strongest image encoder (ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L), multiprofile (maximum input information), transformer aggregation (most flexible cross-profile interaction), and concat fusion (a standard, well-understood baseline). Testing this first gives a performance ceiling against which I can systematically ablate each component (modality, encoder choice, profile setting, aggregation, fusion) in the remaining 9 experiments. If it performs well, I can exploit the direction; if it underperforms, it signals overfitting or component mismatch, redirecting the search. This single experiment reduces the most uncertainty about the overall architecture ceiling and sets a clear reference point for all follow-up comparisons.

The only completed experiment (config_001, multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/concat) achieved 50.7% accuracy, which is moderate and does not yet tell us whether the image modality is contributing positively or negatively. The most fundamental uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion is actually beneficial over RNA-only modeling. config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) is a clean single-variable ablation of config_001—only the image modality is removed while all other settings (profile, RNA encoder, aggregation) remain identical. If rna_only matches or exceeds 50.7%, it signals that the image branch is not adding value and I should redirect the remaining 8 experiments toward RNA-encoder and aggregation choices. If it falls well below, the multimodal direction is validated and I can exploit it by varying encoders and fusion. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the highest-leverage design axis before committing the remaining budget.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) scored 0.507 acc / 0.455 F1, while config_002 (RNA-only, scgpt, transformer) scored 0.514 acc / 0.498 F1. The multimodal model underperforms its RNA-only counterpart, suggesting the concat fusion may be forcing equal-weight integration of potentially noisy image features. Question: config_026 isolates a single change—switching fusion from concat to weighted—while keeping scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, and transformer aggregation identical to config_001. This tests whether learned modality weighting can recover the performance gap and determine if the image modality is salvageable. Why this is the best next step: With 7 experiments remaining, we need to resolve whether the multimodal pipeline is worth further investment or whether we should pivot to RNA-only improvements. A single-variable change (fusion only) gives the cleanest causal signal about the integration strategy, directly informing whether subsequent experiments should explore other image encoders/aggregations or focus on the RNA side.

Evidence: config_026 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the best at 0.520 acc, beating config_001 (same but concat) at 0.507, confirming weighted fusion is superior. However, we have only tested transformer aggregation with weighted fusion; we don't know whether the transformer aggregation is actually contributing beyond the fusion strategy itself. Question: config_016 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates the aggregation method while holding the best fusion constant. Why: With 6 experiments left, clarifying whether transformer vs avgpool matters is a high-value ablation. If avgpool+weighted matches transformer+weighted, it frees us to explore other dimensions (image encoder, RNA encoder) without the transformer's complexity. If transformer is clearly superior, we've confirmed it and can focus optimization on other axes. This reduces uncertainty about a core architectural choice before committing remaining budget to more specific variations.

The best result so far (config_016, acc=0.542) uses multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/avgpool/weighted, showing that avgpool+weighted substantially outperforms transformer+concat (0.542 vs 0.507) and transformer+weighted (0.520). The key uncertainty is whether this avgpool+weighted advantage is specific to imagenet_vit_l or generalizes across image encoders. Config_008 is a single-variable change (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) from the best config, directly testing robustness of the aggregation/fusion finding. If it performs comparably, we confirm avgpool+weighted is the critical design choice and can then pivot to RNA encoder variations; if it degrades, we confirm ViT-L is essential and should focus remaining budget on RNA encoder and profile setting. With 5 experiments left, this clean ablation maximizes information gain per experiment.

The best result so far is config_016 (acc=0.542) using scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted + multiprofile. The aggregation (avgpool > transformer) and fusion (weighted > concat) choices are now well-supported. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the RNA encoder (scgpt vs scvi_n200) is a critical design choice. config_011 tests scvi_n200 in the exact best-known architecture (multimodal, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted), directly clarifying whether a different learned RNA encoder can match or exceed scgpt. This is the highest-value experiment because: (1) it isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding all other parameters at their best-known values, (2) if scvi_n200 performs comparably, it opens a new exploration axis; if not, it confirms scgpt's importance and lets us focus remaining budget on other refinements, and (3) with 4 experiments left, reducing uncertainty about this core component is more valuable than testing marginal variations.

The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder produces a massive jump (config_011: 0.706 acc) over scgpt (~0.54 acc), making it the critical design choice. Config_011 uses avgpool aggregation, which was also best for scgpt (0.542 vs 0.520 for transformer). However, the interaction between aggregation method and encoder richness is untested: a transformer aggregator may better exploit the richer, learned latent representations from scvi_n200 compared to the simpler scgpt embeddings. Config_013 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile, multimodal) is a single-parameter exploitation of the best config, testing whether transformer aggregation can push accuracy above 0.706. This is the highest-value next step because it keeps all proven winning components while probing the one dimension where encoder-dependent interaction is uncertain, and with only 3 experiments remaining, a focused exploitation around the current best is the best use of budget.

The current best is config_013 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) at 0.725 accuracy, with scvi_n200 as the dominant factor and transformer > avgpool aggregation. Evidence: The top-performing family is scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, where imagenet_vit_l+weighted=0.725, imagenet_vit_l+concat=0.721, and resnet50+weighted=0.713. The only untested cell in this 2x2 grid (image encoder × fusion) is resnet50+concat. Question: Does resnet50 with concat fusion in the transformer-aggregation setting reach competitive accuracy (~0.71-0.72), completing the full characterization of the best design space?
