Config_012 fills the last gap in the most promising family, ensuring the reported best (config_013) is not an artifact of an untested nearby variant, and provides a complete, defensible picture of the optimal architecture for the study conclusion.

With no prior evidence, the most important uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion (RNA + image) provides any benefit over single-modality approaches, and what a reasonable baseline accuracy looks like. Config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the simplest and most interpretable multimodal configuration: it uses a fast linear RNA representation (PCA), a standard pretrained CNN (ResNet50), and the most basic fusion (concatenation). This establishes a clear baseline that isolates the core question—does combining modalities help at all?—without confounding from complex encoders, multiprofile aggregation, or learned fusion weights. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can systematically upgrade individual components (e.g., scGPT for RNA, ViT for image, weighted fusion). If it underperforms, the result tells us the bottleneck is in representation quality or fusion strategy, guiding more targeted exploration. As experiment 1 of 10, this maximizes information per trial by anchoring the search space with a well-understood reference point.

The only completed experiment (config_001: pca_n2000, resnet50, concat, singleprofile, multimodal) yielded ~52.7% accuracy, a weak baseline. The most impactful single-variable question is whether replacing the linear PCA RNA encoder (pca_n2000) with a learned, context-aware encoder (scgpt) substantially improves representation quality. config_043 changes only the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scgpt) while holding image encoder (resnet50), fusion (concat), and profile setting (singleprofile) identical to config_001, giving a clean A/B comparison. This is the best use of experiment 2 because: (1) the RNA encoder is likely the most informative modality for cellular profiling, so its quality is the highest-leverage design choice; (2) a single-variable change from the baseline isolates the effect of the encoder upgrade; and (3) with 8 experiments remaining, establishing whether scgpt is meaningfully better than PCA early will guide whether to invest subsequent experiments in scgpt-based multimodal/multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: config_001 (pca_n2000 + resnet50 + concat, singleprofile) achieved 0.527 acc, while config_043 (scgpt + resnet50 + concat) dropped to 0.427, strongly indicating pca_n2000 is the superior RNA encoder. The only major untested variable in the best config's neighborhood is the image encoder. Question: Does upgrading from resnet50 to the much stronger imagenet_vit_l improve multimodal accuracy? config_047 is an exact single-variable swap from config_001 (only image_encoder changes: resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l; all else identical: multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, None aggregation, concat fusion). This clean A/B test isolates the image encoder effect, which is likely the highest-leverage remaining design choice. If it helps, subsequent experiments can stack it with multiprofile/aggregation or weighted fusion; if it doesn't, we rule out that direction and focus on fusion or profile settings. With 7 experiments left, establishing whether the stronger image encoder pays off is the most information-dense next step.

Evidence: Across 3 experiments, pca_n2000 is clearly the best RNA encoder (0.527 vs 0.427 for scgpt), and imagenet_vit_l is the best image encoder (0.535 vs 0.527 for resnet50). All tested configs used singleprofile with concat fusion. The largest unexplored structural dimension is multiprofile, which could capture richer cellular heterogeneity. Question: Does adding multiprofile with simple avgpool aggregation improve accuracy over the best singleprofile setup (config_047, 0.535)? Why this config: config_049 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + multiprofile + concat) isolates the multiprofile effect by keeping the best-known RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method while introducing only the profile change and the simplest aggregation. This controlled test reduces uncertainty about whether multiprofile is a promising direction before investing further experiments in more complex aggregation (transformer) or fusion (weighted) variants. With 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether multiprofile helps is the highest-value next step.

The strongest evidence from 4 experiments is that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation is the dominant factor (config_049: 0.629 vs best singleprofile: 0.535), and pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l is the best encoder combination. The only untested dimension on the current best config (config_049) is the fusion method (concat vs weighted). Config_009 is identical to config_049 except for weighted fusion, making it a minimal, targeted extension that directly tests whether learned fusion weights can improve upon simple concatenation. This is the highest-value next experiment because it exploits the strongest direction with the smallest possible change, reducing uncertainty about the fusion mechanism while preserving all other proven-good settings. With 5 experiments remaining, this low-risk exploitation maximizes the chance of pushing accuracy above 0.629 before exploring larger structural changes (e.g., transformer aggregation or scvi_n200).

The best result so far is config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6352 accuracy. The key evidence shows multiprofile >> singleprofile (~0.10 gain), weighted > concat (small gain), and pca_n2000 > scgpt. Config_037 changes only the aggregation to transformer while keeping all other hyperparameters at their best-known values. With 4 experiments remaining, this low-risk exploitation step either finds a new best or confirms avgpool is near-optimal, freeing remaining budget for RNA encoder exploration (e.g., scvi_n200).

Config_032 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) isolates this one variable while preserving all proven-optimal settings. Config_019 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates this single change. If it improves, it opens a new optimization axis; if it doesn't, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can direct the final 2 experiments toward other levers. The current best (config_019: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → 0.725) sits at the apparent optimum across all four design dimensions. The current best (config_019, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + multimodal + transformer + weighted. The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoders, and multiprofile as superior to singleprofile. Within this best-encoder space, we have tested transformer/weighted (0.725), transformer/concat (0.721), and avgpool/weighted (0.706). Config_018 (avgpool/concat) is the only untested aggregation-fusion combination in this top-tier encoder space. While it is unlikely to surpass the current best (since both avgpool and concat are individually suboptimal), it is the most logical exploitation choice: it maintains the two most impactful design decisions (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) and completes the factorial exploration of the remaining axes. As the final experiment, it provides the cleanest confirmation of the interaction structure between aggregation and fusion within the best-encoder regime, and has the highest expected accuracy among all remaining untested configurations that preserve the proven encoder choices.

With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether a well-motivated multimodal configuration can achieve strong validation accuracy, and which component choices matter most. config_009 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, weighted fusion) tests a strong, standard multimodal setup: a learned RNA encoder (scgpt) that should capture nonlinear biological signal better than PCA, a well-validated image encoder (resnet50), and a simple robust weighted fusion. This is the best first experiment because it establishes a high-quality reference point in the multimodal space with minimal architectural complexity (singleprofile, no aggregation step), making it easier to diagnose which axis to push next (multiprofile, transformer aggregation, ViT-L image encoder, concat fusion, scvi_n200) if performance is promising, or to identify a weak modality if it underperforms.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt+resnet50, weighted fusion → 42.1% accuracy), the critical uncertainty is how much each modality contributes individually. Config_028 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image branch using the exact same image encoder and profile setting as config_009, enabling a direct comparison. If image-only accuracy is near 42%, RNA adds little and the fusion strategy is the bottleneck; if it is substantially lower, RNA is a meaningful contributor and we should focus on improving RNA encoding or fusion. Resolving this modality-contribution question early is essential for allocating the remaining 8 experiments efficiently toward the right design dimensions (fusion, multiprofile, encoder upgrades) rather than chasing a modality that may be underperforming.

Evidence: config_009 (multimodal, scgpt+resnet50, weighted fusion) achieved 0.421 acc, while config_028 (image_only, resnet50) achieved only 0.208 acc — a 21-point gap showing RNA is critical. However, we cannot yet decompose how much of the 0.421 comes from RNA alone versus the multimodal combination. If RNA alone approaches ~0.40+, the image modality adds little and remaining budget should target RNA encoder/architecture improvements. If RNA alone is much lower (~0.20-0.30), the multimodal fusion is genuinely synergistic and we should prioritize multiprofile aggregation and fusion strategy experiments. With only 2 data points, this decomposition is the highest-information experiment to guide the remaining 7 trials efficiently.

Evidence: config_009 (multimodal, scgpt+resnet50, weighted) achieves 0.4214, while RNA-only scgpt (config_038) achieves 0.4106 and image-only resnet50 (config_028) is very weak at 0.2079. This shows RNA is the dominant signal and the image modality contributes only ~1% via resnet50. Question: Is the weak image contribution due to a suboptimal image encoder? config_002 swaps resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l while keeping everything else identical to config_009 (scgpt, singleprofile, weighted fusion), making it a clean single-variable test. Why this is the best next experiment: With 6 experiments remaining, isolating the image encoder variable is the highest-information experiment—if imagenet_vit_l substantially boosts image signal, the multimodal model could see a meaningful accuracy gain; if not, we can confidently rule out image encoder quality as the bottleneck and redirect remaining budget toward multiprofile aggregation or RNA encoder alternatives.

All four completed experiments used singleprofile, so the impact of multiprofile aggregation is the largest unexplored design dimension. Our best results (config_009: 0.4214, config_002: 0.4224) both use scgpt + weighted fusion in multimodal mode, with only a marginal difference between resnet50 and imagenet_vit_l. This isolates the effect of multi-profile aggregation and tells us whether capturing multiple spatial profiles can push accuracy beyond the ~0.42 plateau. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving whether multiprofile is a productive direction is critical before committing further budget to more complex variants (transformer aggregation, different encoders).

The best result so far is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.5251 accuracy, showing a large jump over singleprofile configs (~0.42). The current best (config_019, acc=0.5251) uses multimodal + multiprofile + scgpt + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted. The current best is config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.542). The best result (config_046, acc=0.706) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. The only untested variation within this strongest base is the fusion strategy. With no prior evidence, I need to establish a strong baseline while testing the core multimodal hypothesis. config_012 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) combines the strongest available image encoder (ViT-L pretrained on ImageNet) with a robust, low-variance RNA representation (PCA-2000), standard average pooling for multi-profile aggregation, and weighted fusion to allow learned modality balancing. Evidence: config_012 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.635 val accuracy, giving a single baseline. Uncertainty: with only one data point, I cannot tell whether the simple avgpool aggregation is a bottleneck or whether a more expressive transformer aggregation would better capture cross-modal interactions. This experiment (config_015) is a clean single-variable A/B test: it changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other settings identical to config_012. If transformer aggregation improves accuracy, it signals that the fusion architecture has headroom and justifies exploring transformer-based variants with other encoders/fusions in remaining budget. If it does not help, I can rule out the transformer dimension and focus exploitation on RNA/image encoder and fusion choices. Evidence: config_012 (avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.635 accuracy, significantly outperforming config_015 (transformer, weighted) at 0.586, establishing avgpool as the superior aggregation. Both used weighted fusion, so the fusion strategy (weighted vs concat) remains untested. Question: config_004 is identical to our best (config_012) except fusion changes from weighted to concat, isolating the effect of fusion strategy while holding the proven avgpool aggregation, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder constant. Why: This is the cleanest single-variable exploitation of our current best result. Fusion strategy is a fundamental architectural choice that could meaningfully shift accuracy, and resolving it early (with 7 experiments left) lets us lock in the better fusion for all subsequent exploration of RNA encoders (scvi_n200, scgpt), image encoders (resnet50), and profile settings. Testing concat now maximizes information gain per experiment.

Evidence: All three completed experiments share pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile, with avgpool+weighted (config_012, acc=0.635) clearly outperforming transformer+weighted (config_015, acc=0.586) and avgpool+concat (config_004, acc=0.629). The RNA encoder dimension is completely untested. Question: Does a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) improve over PCA in the proven architecture (avgpool + weighted + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile)? Why: config_027 is a clean single-variable swap from the current best (only RNA encoder changes from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200), directly testing whether a biologically-informed latent representation can push accuracy beyond 0.635. With 6 experiments remaining, resolving the RNA encoder question early is critical because it determines whether subsequent experiments should explore scvi/scgpt variants or stay with PCA and vary other axes.

The strongest evidence so far is that switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (config_027 vs config_012) yielded a ~7-point accuracy gain (0.635→0.706) with all other settings held constant, making scvi_n200 the clear best RNA encoder. The image encoder dimension (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) is completely untested across all 4 experiments. Config_035 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable test that changes only the image encoder from the best configuration (config_027). This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-potential-impact axis remaining: a different backbone architecture could shift accuracy substantially in either direction. With 5 experiments left, resolving whether resnet50 or imagenet_vit_l pairs better with scvi_n200 is critical before committing remaining budget to fine-tuning aggregation/fusion choices. If resnet50 matches or beats imagenet_vit_l, it opens a new promising branch; if not, we can confidently exploit the imagenet_vit_l + scvi_n200 combination in subsequent experiments.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted (config_027) is the clear best at 0.7062, with scvi_n200 outperforming pca_n2000 by ~7 points and imagenet_vit_l outperforming resnet50 by ~3 points. However, we have zero information about scgpt as an RNA encoder. Question: Does scgpt, paired with the best-known image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted), match or exceed scvi_n200? Why: With 4 experiments remaining after this one, testing the one unexplored RNA encoder under otherwise optimal settings is the highest-information experiment. If scgpt is competitive, it opens new combinations; if it lags significantly, we confirm scvi_n200 is optimal and can spend remaining budget on fine-grained fusion/aggregation variants around the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l core.

The best result so far is config_027 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.7062). The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation could outperform avgpool when paired with the richer, nonlinear scvi_n200 embeddings. With pca_n2000, transformer was notably worse (0.5856 vs 0.6352), but PCA produces linear projections that may not benefit from attention-based token weighting, whereas scvi_n200 yields learned latent representations where attention could selectively emphasize informative dimensions. This experiment tests that hypothesis directly. If transformer helps, it could push accuracy above 0.7062; if not, it confirms avgpool as optimal and frees the remaining 3 experiments to exploit the confirmed best architecture with other variations (e.g., fusion strategy via config_020, or singleprofile settings). This is the highest-information experiment that extends the strongest finding.

The evidence strongly points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the best encoder pair (config_022: 0.725, config_027: 0.706), and transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706). Weighted fusion has been preferred over concat in prior comparisons (0.635 vs 0.629 with pca_n2000), but that gap was small and tested under different conditions. Config_050 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) is the only untested variant in the top-performing family. Testing it clarifies whether concat fusion could match or exceed weighted when paired with transformer aggregation and the strongest encoders. With only 2 experiments remaining after this, confirming the optimal fusion method within the best family is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve before committing final experiments to fine-tuning or confirming the overall best configuration.

Evidence: The best configuration so far (config_022, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted in a multiprofile setting. All 8 completed experiments are multiprofile, so the single-profile architecture (no aggregation step) remains entirely untested with the top two encoders. Question: config_019 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted) tests whether removing the multi-profile aggregation pipeline and relying on a single profile with the best RNA and image encoders can match or exceed the 0.725 ceiling, or whether the aggregation step is essential. Why this is the best use: With only 1 experiment remaining after this one, I need the highest-ceiling untested direction. The single-profile architecture is the most structurally different untested option that still uses the two clearly superior encoders (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l). If it outperforms 0.725, it becomes the new best; if it underperforms, it confirms the multiprofile+transformer pipeline is the right architecture, allowing the final experiment to focus on a fine-tuned variant of the current best. This maximizes information gain under the tight budget.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l is clearly the best encoder pair (0.725, 0.721, 0.706 across tested combos), and transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool by ~0.02. The current best is config_022 (transformer+weighted, 0.725). Question: config_020 (avgpool+concat) is the only untested aggregation×fusion combination for this top encoder pair, completing the 2×2 grid. While transformer+weighted is the current best, testing avgpool+concat clarifies whether the concat fusion's slight edge in some settings (config_050 vs config_022 gap is only 0.004) might interact differently with avgpool. This is the best use of the final experiment because it closes the last gap in the design space for the dominant encoder pair, and no other untested configuration (resnet50 variants, scgpt, pca, singleprofile) has realistic potential to exceed 0.725 given the strong evidence favoring scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong reference point for the multimodal pipeline. config_016 combines the most powerful and well-motivated components: multimodal (the study's focus), multiprofile (richer cellular state), scgpt (learned biologically-informed RNA representation), imagenet_vit_l (strongest available image encoder), transformer aggregation (most expressive for multiprofile), and concat fusion (simple, robust baseline). This 'strong prior' configuration tests whether the full multimodal architecture can achieve high accuracy, establishing an upper-bound reference. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components to identify what matters most; if it underperforms, the result flags which dimension to investigate. With 9 experiments remaining, this single informative baseline is the highest-value first move.

With only one completed experiment (config_016: multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat → 50.7% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually adding value over the image modality alone. The 50.7% accuracy is modest and the F1 (0.455) is notably lower, raising the possibility that the RNA branch is not contributing meaningfully or is introducing noise. config_024 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) is the closest single-modality counterpart to config_016, sharing the same image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation. Comparing the two will directly tell us whether the RNA encoder (scgpt) and fusion step are helping or hurting. This baseline is essential before committing remaining budget to multimodal optimization; if image-only matches or exceeds 50.7%, the search should pivot toward image-focused configurations, saving experiments from being wasted on multimodal variants that may not outperform a simpler model.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved 0.507 accuracy, far exceeding the image-only baseline (config_024, 0.260), confirming that the multimodal setup with scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer is the strongest direction. Question: Does changing the fusion strategy from concat to weighted (config_036) improve upon the best result while keeping all other hyperparameters identical? This is a clean single-variable ablation of the fusion mechanism. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest evidence with a minimal, interpretable change is the highest-value next step. If weighted fusion helps, it opens a clear optimization axis; if not, it rules out fusion as the next lever and directs attention to RNA encoder or aggregation changes. This avoids over-exploring untested modalities (e.g., RNA-only) that, while scientifically informative, are less likely to yield the best config within the remaining budget.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_036 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.520 acc / 0.479 F1, confirming that multimodal + weighted fusion + ViT-L image encoder is the strongest combination. The RNA encoder axis (scgpt vs scvi_n200 vs pca) remains unexplored under this optimal setting. Question: config_039 swaps scgpt for scvi_n200 while holding all other proven-best components constant (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile), directly testing whether a VAE-based RNA representation can match or exceed the generative scgpt encoder in a multimodal context. Why this is the best next experiment: With 6 experiments remaining, testing the RNA encoder under the current best architecture is the highest-information move—it either reveals a better RNA representation to exploit in subsequent runs or confirms scgpt as the optimal choice, narrowing the search space significantly for the remaining budget.

The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder drives a massive accuracy jump (0.725 in config_039 vs ~0.51-0.52 for scgpt configs), making it the clear backbone. The best config (config_039) uses weighted fusion; the only other scgpt comparison (config_016 vs config_036) showed weighted slightly beating concat, but that was with a weaker RNA encoder. Config_028 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) isolates the fusion method while holding all other components at the best-known values. This tells us whether weighted fusion provides a genuine advantage over concat when the RNA representation is already strong, or whether the ~0.01 gap seen with scgpt was noise. With 5 experiments remaining, understanding which components are truly load-bearing is critical before committing budget to further modifications. If concat matches weighted, it simplifies the search space; if weighted clearly wins, it confirms config_039's fusion choice and we can focus remaining experiments on other axes (aggregation, image encoder).

The current best (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The dominant factor identified so far is the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs scgpt gives ~20% gain), while fusion (weighted vs concat) shows only a ~0.4% difference. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation performs comparably with the strong scvi_n200 encoder. Config_021 changes exactly one variable from the best (transformer → avgpool, keeping weighted fusion), directly testing whether aggregation architecture matters. This is the best use of experiment 6 because: (1) it is a clean single-variable ablation of the current best, (2) if avgpool matches transformer, it confirms the model is not aggregation-limited and remaining budget can focus on other axes (e.g., image encoder or profile setting); if it falls short, it confirms transformer is essential and we should exploit that. With only 4 experiments left, resolving this uncertainty efficiently is critical.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder (~0.72 vs ~0.51 for scgpt), and with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer, weighted fusion (0.725) marginally edges out concat (0.721). The image encoder choice is the largest untested axis under the scvi_n200 regime — all strong results so far use imagenet_vit_l, but we have no direct comparison with resnet50. Question: Does swapping imagenet_vit_l for resnet50 (config_042: scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) maintain or improve performance? This is a clean single-variable ablation against the current best (config_039). Why this is the best use of experiment 7: It directly tests whether the image encoder contributes meaningfully when the RNA encoder is already strong, reducing uncertainty about a key design choice. With 3 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out resnet50 early lets us either exploit a broader set of resnet50 configs or lock in imagenet_vit_l and focus remaining budget on subtler refinements (e.g., singleprofile, aggregation variants).

The current best (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + weighted. All top results confirm multiprofile+transformer is strong, but the singleprofile architecture with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l remains completely untested. Config_007 (singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted) isolates the single most important unexplored architectural dimension—whether multiprofile+transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler single-profile path with the same strong encoders could match or exceed 0.725. This resolves high uncertainty with the best-known component choices. If it underperforms, it confirms the multiprofile+transformer design and lets the final 2 experiments focus on fine-tuning within that space; if it performs comparably or better, it opens a new promising direction. With only 2 experiments remaining, reducing this architectural uncertainty is the highest-value use of the next slot.

Evidence: The top-4 experiments (config_039: 0.725, config_028: 0.721, config_042: 0.713, config_021: 0.706) establish that scvi_n200 + multiprofile + multimodal is the dominant setting, with imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 and transformer > avgpool, and weighted ≈ concat (small ~0.004 gap). Question: config_018 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) completes the 2×2 factorial on image_encoder × fusion under the best aggregation, which is the only cell not yet tested. This clarifies whether the small weighted-over-concat and vit_l-over-resnet50 advantages are purely additive or show interaction effects. Why best use: With only 1 experiment remaining after this, completing the factorial gives the clearest picture of the design space, ensuring the final experiment (if needed) targets a genuine gap rather than a redundant confirmation. It is the most informative remaining scvi_n200 + transformer configuration and the logical extension of the systematic exploration already underway.

Evidence: config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) achieved the best accuracy at 0.7250, and all top-5 results share multiprofile + transformer aggregation + weighted/concat fusion with scvi_n200. The only untested configuration that pairs the four best-validated settings (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) with an alternative RNA encoder is config_041 (pca_n2000). This experiment directly tests whether a simpler linear RNA representation can match or exceed the deep scvi_n200 encoder in the otherwise-optimal pipeline. As the final experiment, it provides a clean ablation (only RNA encoder differs from config_039), confirming whether scvi_n200's ~0.20 accuracy advantage over scgpt is specific to learned representations or generalizable to any non-trivial RNA encoding. This is the highest-value remaining test because it either discovers a competitive alternative or definitively closes the search by validating the best configuration found.

With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal (RNA + image) combination provides a meaningful accuracy advantage, and which core architectural choices are most impactful. Config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) tests the central multimodal hypothesis using well-established, robust components: PCA-2000 as a simple but effective RNA representation, ViT-L as the strongest available image encoder, transformer aggregation to capture cross-profile interactions, and weighted fusion to let the model learn modality importance. This provides a strong reference baseline: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can refine by swapping in more sophisticated RNA encoders (scgpt, scvi_n200) or different fusion strategies; if it underperforms, the result helps diagnose whether the bottleneck lies in the RNA encoding, image encoding, or fusion mechanism. As the first of 10 experiments, establishing this multimodal baseline is the highest-information-gain choice before committing budget to single-modality comparisons or fine-grained ablations.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted → 0.5856 acc), the largest source of uncertainty is the RNA encoder choice, as it determines the quality of the single-cell representation fed into the multimodal model. config_012 is identical to config_009 in every setting except rna_encoder is changed from pca_n2000 (linear, 2000-dim) to scgpt (generative pretrained transformer for scRNA-seq), making this a clean single-variable A/B test. scgpt captures non-linear biological structure that PCA cannot, and if it yields a meaningful accuracy gain, it opens a rich sub-space of scgpt-based multimodal configurations to exploit in later experiments; if it does not improve, we can confidently rule out the RNA encoder as a bottleneck and redirect remaining budget toward fusion, aggregation, or image-encoder variations. Under an 8-experiment remaining budget, resolving this high-impact uncertainty early is the most information-efficient use of experiment 2.

The two completed experiments show that pca_n2000 (0.5856) substantially outperforms scgpt (0.5199) as the RNA encoder within the multimodal/multiprofile/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/weighted setup. The current best config (config_009) uses weighted fusion. The key remaining uncertainty within this promising configuration space is whether concat fusion could outperform weighted fusion while keeping all other components identical. config_013 is a clean single-variable change (fusion: weighted → concat) from the best config, directly testing this important design dimension. It is the best use of experiment 3 because it either confirms weighted fusion as optimal (consolidating our exploitation direction) or discovers a better fusion strategy that would unlock further improvements in the remaining 7 experiments.

Evidence: All three completed experiments use transformer aggregation, so we have no information on whether this structural choice is actually beneficial. The best config (config_013: pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat, acc=0.599) establishes pca_n2000 >> scgpt and concat ≥ weighted as the current best settings. Question: Does transformer aggregation meaningfully outperform simpler avgpool aggregation when paired with the best-known RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and fusion (concat)? This is the single most important untested structural variable in the current best configuration. Why this experiment: It isolates one variable (aggregation) from the current best config, directly tests whether the added complexity of a transformer is justified, and with 6 experiments remaining, resolving this question early prevents us from wasting budget on transformer-based variants if a simpler aggregation is equally effective or superior.

The best result so far is config_024 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.6287 acc. Evidence from completed experiments strongly supports pca_n2000 over scgpt (+6.6%), avgpool over transformer (+3.0%), and concat over weighted (+1.3%). The one major variable not yet tested with this winning combination is the image encoder—we have only used imagenet_vit_l. Config_022 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable swap from the current best, directly testing whether resnet50 can match or exceed imagenet_vit_l. This is the highest-information experiment: if resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the architecture is robust to encoder choice and we can focus remaining budget on other axes; if it underperforms, we lock in imagenet_vit_l and redirect exploration. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving this key uncertainty early is the best use of the next slot.

Evidence: The top-3 results (config_024: 0.6287, config_022: 0.6186, config_013: 0.5988) consistently show that avgpool aggregation + concat fusion is the strongest combination, and pca_n2000 with imagenet_vit_l is the best RNA+image pairing tested. However, scvi_n200 (a learned RNA encoder) has never been tested in this optimal aggregation/fusion/image setting. This experiment (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) directly tests whether a learned encoder can match or exceed PCA in the best-known structural configuration. It is the highest-value next test because: (1) it isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding all other factors at their empirically best values, (2) if scvi_n200 performs comparably or better, it opens a new exploitation direction for the remaining 4 experiments, and (3) if it underperforms, it confirms PCA is the ceiling for RNA encoding and lets us focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other aspects. This is a clean, high-information experiment that reduces uncertainty about the most impactful untested design choice.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 is a dramatically better RNA encoder than pca_n2000 or scgpt (0.7150 vs ~0.62 vs ~0.52), and avgpool+concat is the best aggregation/fusion combination. The only untested high-impact variable in the scvi_n200 context is the image encoder: we've only tested scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l. With pca_n2000, vit_l and resnet50 were close (0.6287 vs 0.6186), so it's unclear whether vit_l's advantage persists or reverses when paired with the richer scvi_n200 representations. Config_015 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + concat) directly tests this. If resnet50 matches or beats vit_l, it broadens the search; if vit_l is clearly superior, we can confidently lock in the image encoder and spend remaining budget on finer refinements (e.g., fusion weighting or profile setting). This is the highest-information experiment for the 3 remaining slots.

The current best (config_049, acc=0.715) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat. The strongest untested dimension for this top combination is aggregation: transformer has not yet been paired with scvi_n200. While transformer was slightly worse than avgpool for pca_n2000 (0.599 vs 0.629), scvi_n200 produces a richer, non-linear latent representation where transformer's ability to model cell-cell interactions could yield a meaningful gain. This experiment isolates a single variable (aggregation) from the proven-best configuration, keeping concat fusion and imagenet_vit_l fixed. If it beats 0.715, we have a new champion; if not, we confirm avgpool is optimal for scvi_n200 and can spend the remaining 2 experiments on other directions (e.g., weighted fusion or singleprofile). This is the highest-information, lowest-risk extension of the current best with 2 experiments left in budget.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + concat as the winning combination (config_007: 0.7207, config_049: 0.7150). The only untested cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for this top encoder pair is transformer + weighted (config_017). While concat has outperformed weighted in prior tests (config_013 vs config_009), the interaction between transformer aggregation and weighted fusion with the strongest encoders is untested and could theoretically yield a small gain over 0.7207. Testing this completes the design space for the best configuration family, reduces residual uncertainty about the fusion choice under transformer aggregation, and is the most logical exploitation step given only 1 experiment remains after this one.

The current best is config_017 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.7250). The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l as the superior encoders, with transformer+weighted as the best aggregation/fusion pair. The only untested cell in this top-performing 2×2 grid (aggregation × fusion) is avgpool + weighted (config_020). We know avgpool+concat gives 0.715 and weighted fusion adds ~0.004–0.005 over concat in the transformer row, so avgpool+weighted is expected around 0.719–0.721. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, this is the last logical exploitation step in the most promising subspace, completing the full characterization and confirming whether the transformer aggregation advantage holds across fusion strategies. No other untested config (scgpt, resnet50, singleprofile, unimodal) has a realistic chance of exceeding the current best, making this the highest-value final experiment.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a high-ceiling baseline using the most sophisticated components across all design axes: multimodal (both modalities), multiprofile (richer cellular context), scgpt (learned, biologically-informed RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (large pretrained image encoder), transformer aggregation (attention-based profile pooling), and weighted fusion (learned modality combination). This configuration tests whether the full pipeline can achieve strong validation accuracy and provides a reference upper bound. Subsequent experiments can then ablate individual components (e.g., swap scgpt→pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l→resnet50, transformer→avgpool) to identify which design choices drive performance, making this the most informative first probe under the 10-experiment budget.

We have only one data point (config_002: multimodal, pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → 58.6% acc). The most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion is actually adding value over a single modality. Config_013 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) is the cleanest ablation of config_002: it removes the RNA modality while keeping the same image encoder and aggregation. If image-only approaches ~58%, the RNA branch isn't contributing and we should focus on image-centric or lighter multimodal configs; if it's substantially lower, the RNA signal is essential and we should explore RNA encoder variants (scgpt, scvi) and fusion strategies. Establishing this single-modality floor with 8 experiments remaining is the highest-information experiment before committing to a multimodal optimization trajectory.

Evidence: config_002 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.586 accuracy, while image-only config_013 (same image encoder, transformer) achieves only 0.260, indicating RNA features are the dominant driver of performance. Question: config_002 uses PCA (a linear projection) for RNA; config_019 swaps in scgpt (a learned, non-linear RNA encoder) while keeping all other settings identical (imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile). This isolates whether a more expressive RNA representation can push accuracy beyond 0.586. Why this is best: with 7 experiments remaining, testing the highest-impact single variable (RNA encoder quality, given RNA's clear dominance) around the current best configuration is the most informative exploitation step. A positive result would open a promising direction for further tuning; a null result would confirm PCA is sufficient and redirect effort toward other components (image encoder, fusion, aggregation).

Evidence: config_002 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.5856), and config_019 (scgpt, same other settings) scored lower (0.5200), confirming pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer is a strong backbone. Uncertainty: the fusion mechanism (weighted vs. concat) is the one component of this best config not yet varied in isolation. This experiment tests whether concat fusion can match or beat weighted fusion while keeping all other settings identical to the current best. It is the best use of experiment 4 because it is a single-variable exploitation of the top configuration, giving a clean, interpretable signal about fusion design before spending remaining budget on broader exploration (e.g., different image encoders or RNA encoders).

Evidence: The best config so far (config_038, acc=0.5988) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat. We have shown pca_n2000 > scgpt (0.5856 vs 0.5199), but scvi_n200 remains completely untested. Question: Does the variational scvi_n200 RNA encoder outperform or match pca_n2000 under the best-known pipeline (imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion, multiprofile)? This is a clean single-variable change from the current best, isolating the RNA encoder effect. Why: With 5 experiments left, resolving the RNA encoder question is the highest-value uncertainty. If scvi_n200 is competitive, it opens a new optimization axis; if not, we can confidently lock in pca_n2000 and spend remaining budget fine-tuning aggregation/fusion or image encoder. This is the most informative next step before committing to exploitation of the current best.

Evidence: config_031 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved 0.7207 accuracy, far surpassing all other configs. The RNA encoder (scvi_n200) was the dominant factor, but the image encoder dimension has not yet been explored with scvi_n200. All top configs used imagenet_vit_l, and the image-only baseline (config_013) was very low (0.2596), suggesting the image branch contributes differently depending on the encoder. Question: Does resnet50 complement scvi_n200 better than imagenet_vit_l, potentially yielding a higher accuracy? This is the most impactful unexplored axis for our best-performing RNA encoder. Why this experiment: With 4 experiments remaining, testing a new image encoder paired with the clearly superior scvi_n200 + transformer + concat stack offers the highest potential upside to beat 0.7207, while keeping all other variables (aggregation, fusion, profile) fixed at their best-known values. It reduces uncertainty about whether the current 0.7207 is near-optimal or whether a different visual backbone could push performance higher.

The strongest evidence points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the optimal backbone (config_031: 0.7207 acc). The only untested dimension within this exact backbone is the fusion method: config_031 used concat, while weighted fusion remains untested with this combination. With pca_n2000, concat slightly outperformed weighted (0.5988 vs 0.5856), but the gap was small and scvi_n200 may interact differently with weighted fusion. Testing config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is a minimal, high-information experiment: it either discovers a new best or confirms concat is optimal for the top backbone. With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, exploiting the strongest direction while resolving the last untested hyperparameter is the best use of the budget.

Evidence: The top two results (config_039: 0.7250, config_031: 0.7207) both use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer, with weighted fusion marginally ahead of concat. All top performers use multiprofile and transformer aggregation. The only untested aggregation within this strongest encoder combination is avgpool. Question: Does avgpool aggregation with the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion setup match or exceed the transformer-based result of 0.7250? Why this experiment: It is the single remaining untested variation in the most promising design space (best RNA encoder + best image encoder + best fusion), and with only 2 experiments left, testing the one unexplored axis (aggregation) within the proven top combination is the highest-information, highest-upside choice. If avgpool underperforms, it confirms transformer as optimal and we can confidently lock in config_039 as the final answer.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer+weighted advantage is specific to imagenet_vit_l or generalizable. Config_047 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) is the only untested configuration that isolates the image encoder variable while holding the best aggregation and fusion fixed. It completes the critical 2x2 comparison for the top-performing architecture family. Even though resnet50 has underperformed vit_l in prior tests (0.6878 vs 0.7207 with concat), testing it with the stronger weighted fusion may reveal whether the gap narrows. This is the best use of the penultimate experiment because it either confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential (guiding the final experiment toward other untested dimensions) or reveals a competitive alternative, reducing uncertainty before the last experiment.

Evidence: The top-performing configurations consistently use scvi_n200 (RNA) + imagenet_vit_l (image) as encoders, with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion yielding the best result (config_039: 0.7250). Among untested configs, config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the only remaining multiprofile combination using both best-performing encoders. It tests whether the avgpool+concat pairing, while individually slightly weaker than transformer+weighted, might interact favorably with these strong encoders. This is the last experiment (0 remaining), so the goal is to maximize the probability of exceeding the current best of 0.7250. Config_032 has the highest expected accuracy among all untested options since it retains the two strongest encoders; all other untested scvi_n200 configs either swap to resnet50 (costing ~0.012) or use singleprofile (likely a larger drop). While the expected performance (~0.70-0.71) is unlikely to surpass 0.725, it is the best remaining bet to potentially improve the final result.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should test the core multimodal hypothesis with a well-motivated strong configuration to establish a performance baseline and reduce uncertainty about whether combining modalities is beneficial. config_007 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) uses the most powerful available encoders (scGPT for RNA captures biological structure; ViT-L for images) and multiprofile to maximize information from each modality. Transformer aggregation provides flexible cross-profile integration, and concat fusion is a simple, robust baseline that avoids potential issues with learned weighting in an unexplored space. If this performs well, we gain a strong candidate to refine over the remaining 9 experiments (varying fusion, encoders, aggregation). If it underperforms, the result diagnoses whether the bottleneck is in multimodal fusion, a specific encoder, or the architecture, guiding targeted follow-up experiments. Starting with the most promising configuration is the best use of experiment 1 because it either immediately identifies a high-accuracy candidate or provides a clear anchor for decomposition in subsequent trials.

With only one completed experiment (config_007: multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/ViT-L/transformer/concat at 50.7% acc), evidence is sparse and the most important uncertainty is whether the complex transformer aggregation over cells is actually contributing or introducing overfitting/noise. Config_009 changes exactly one variable—aggregation from transformer to avgpool—while keeping scgpt, ViT-L, multiprofile, and concat fusion identical to config_007. This clean A/B test will clarify whether the attention-based aggregation is a meaningful driver of the current performance or whether a simpler mean-pooling suffices. If avgpool matches or beats transformer, it frees us to focus budget on RNA/image encoder choices; if it is substantially worse, it confirms transformer aggregation as a key component. This is the highest-information single-variable probe available at experiment 2, reducing uncertainty about a high-impact architectural choice before committing remaining budget to other dimensions.

Evidence: config_009 (avgpool, concat) outperforms config_007 (transformer, concat) by ~1% acc and ~3% F1 with all other settings identical (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l), suggesting avgpool is the better aggregation. Uncertainty: we have not yet tested whether weighted fusion can further improve over concat fusion under the same avgpool aggregation. This experiment (config_003) tests that single variable change (concat → weighted) while holding the best-performing aggregation and all other settings constant. It is the best use of this slot because it is a minimal, controlled extension of the current best result, directly reducing uncertainty about the fusion strategy before we invest remaining budget in exploring other axes (RNA encoder, image encoder, modality ablations).

All three completed experiments share the same backbone (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile) and only vary aggregation/fusion, with avgpool+weighted (config_003, acc=0.542) clearly best. The major untested variable is the RNA encoder: we have only tried scgpt. Config_031 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) keeps all other settings at their best-known values while swapping in a simpler, high-dimensional PCA representation. This directly tests whether scgpt's learned representation is actually contributing or whether a standard linear projection suffices. If PCA matches or beats scgpt, it frees us to explore other dimensions; if it falls well short, it confirms scgpt is important and we should focus remaining budget on image encoder or profile setting. With 6 experiments left, resolving this core architectural question early maximizes the information gained per experiment.

The current best (config_031, acc=0.635) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. With scgpt, avgpool consistently outperformed transformer (0.518 vs 0.507), but pca_n2000 produces fundamentally different (linear, low-dim) representations that may interact differently with transformer aggregation. Config_012 is a clean single-variable test (avgpool→transformer, all else held at known-best) that clarifies whether the aggregation choice is robust or whether the PCA representation unlocks a benefit from attention-based aggregation. This is the highest-information next step: if transformer matches or beats avgpool, it opens a new direction; if it confirms avgpool, we can confidently lock that choice and spend remaining budget on the image encoder or fusion variable.

The best result so far is config_031 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.635 accuracy, and the evidence strongly supports pca_n2000 + avgpool + weighted as the optimal architecture. However, the image encoder dimension is unexplored for this strong combination—we've only tested imagenet_vit_l. Config_020 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable change that tests whether resnet50 could outperform or match imagenet_vit_l. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve: if resnet50 is comparable or better, it opens a new direction; if clearly worse, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is optimal and lets us focus remaining budget on other levers (e.g., profile setting or fusion). With 4 experiments left, efficiently confirming or ruling out the image encoder choice is critical before committing to fine-tuning.

The evidence strongly favors pca_n2000 + avgpool + weighted (config_020: 0.639, config_031: 0.635), and avgpool consistently outperforms transformer while weighted outperforms concat across all tested pairs. However, scvi_n2000 has never been tested in this proven-best architecture. Config_028 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) isolates the RNA encoder variable within the confirmed optimal aggregation/fusion/image-encoder setting. This is the highest-information experiment: if scvi_n2000 is competitive, it opens a new exploration axis for the remaining 3 experiments; if not, it confirms pca_n2000 is the optimal RNA encoder and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning around config_020. Testing transformer or concat variants would be low-value given their consistent underperformance, making this the best use of experiment 7.

The current best (config_028: scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.678) clearly establishes scvi_n200 as the superior RNA encoder and avgpool+weighted as the best aggregation/fusion pair. The key remaining uncertainty is the image encoder choice: resnet50 has only 2 data points (0.639, 0.678) vs. imagenet_vit_l with 5 (0.507–0.635). Config_036 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted + multiprofile) directly tests whether the larger ViT-L image encoder, when paired with the best RNA encoder and proven aggregation/fusion, can match or exceed resnet50. This is the highest-impact untested combination: if imagenet_vit_l performs comparably or better, it opens a new optimization axis; if it underperforms, it confirms resnet50 is optimal and the last 2 experiments can focus on fine-tuning around the resnet50+scvi_n200 core. This single test resolves the most important remaining design uncertainty before the budget ends.

The current best (config_036, scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, 0.706) has strong evidence for its encoder choices, but the aggregation choice with this specific encoder pair remains untested. Prior evidence shows avgpool > transformer by ~5% with pca_n2000 (config_031 vs 012) and ~3.5% with scgpt (config_003 vs 007), but scvi_n200 produces learned latent representations that may interact differently with attention-based aggregation. Config_038 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) directly tests whether transformer aggregation can match or exceed avgpool with the strongest encoder combination. If it underperforms as expected, it confirms the current best architecture is near-optimal, giving confidence to accept 0.706 in the final experiment. If it surprisingly performs well, it could push past 0.706. This is the highest-information experiment among the remaining options, as it resolves the last major architectural uncertainty in the neighborhood of the best configuration with only 1 experiment left in the budget.

The current best (config_038: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) establishes that scvi_n200, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion are the strongest components. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation benefit is specific to imagenet_vit_l or generalizable across image encoders. config_045 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) isolates this interaction: we know scvi_n200+resnet50+avgpool+weighted=0.678 (config_028), and transformer gave +0.019 over avgpool with imagenet_vit_l (0.706→0.725). If transformer aggregation also helps resnet50 comparably, this could reach ~0.697–0.71; if the interaction is synergistic, it could approach or exceed 0.725. Among all untested configs, this is the closest logical extension of the best configuration (only one component changed) and directly tests the one remaining design-space question near the optimum. As the final experiment, it maximizes the probability of either discovering a new best or confirming the current best is robust.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong, central baseline to anchor the search. config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) combines the most capable and standard choices across all design axes: it uses all modalities, the richer multiprofile setting, a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200), the stronger image backbone (ViT-L), a simple and robust aggregation (avgpool), and a flexible weighted fusion. This configuration has the highest prior probability of performing well and serves as a natural hub: every other multimodal configuration differs from it by only one or two factors, making it ideal for interpreting subsequent single-factor comparisons. Testing it first maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-run budget.

With only one data point (config_009: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted → 0.706 acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion actually adds value over the RNA modality alone. Config_035 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean ablation of config_009 that holds the RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation constant while removing the image branch. If config_035 performs comparably to 0.706, the image modality is not contributing meaningfully and I should redirect my remaining 8 experiments toward optimizing the RNA-only pipeline. If config_035 is substantially lower, it confirms multimodal fusion is valuable and I can exploit that by testing fusion/aggregation variations (e.g., config_012, config_041) in subsequent experiments. This single comparison resolves the highest-impact design question with minimal confounding, making it the best use of experiment 2 under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_009 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieved the best accuracy (0.706) and significantly outperformed the rna_only baseline (config_035, 0.650), confirming multimodal fusion is beneficial. Uncertainty: whether the simple avgpool aggregation is the bottleneck in the multiprofile setting, where multiple profiles must be combined into a single representation. Question: does upgrading aggregation to a transformer (which can model interactions across profiles) improve accuracy while keeping the proven weighted fusion and encoder choices fixed? This is a clean single-variable change from the current best. Rationale: with 7 experiments remaining, testing the aggregation mechanism is high-value because (a) it directly addresses the multiprofile aggregation challenge, (b) if transformer aggregation helps, it validates a direction extendable to other encoder/fusion combinations, and (c) it reduces uncertainty about whether the current 0.706 ceiling is due to a limited aggregation strategy rather than the encoders or fusion method.

The current best (config_041, acc=0.725) uses transformer aggregation + weighted fusion with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l. The avgpool→transformer switch gave ~2% gain, confirming that aggregation architecture matters. The next most informative one-variable change is testing concat fusion (config_025) in place of weighted fusion, holding all else constant. This directly tests whether the transformer-aggregated multimodal features benefit from a different fusion mechanism. It is the cleanest exploitation step from the current best, reducing uncertainty about the fusion design choice before branching into RNA encoder or image encoder variations in subsequent experiments.

The best result so far (config_041, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. The only RNA encoder tested across all 4 experiments is scvi_n200, making the RNA encoder the largest unexplored design axis. Config_019 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is a direct swap of the RNA encoder to scgpt while holding all other parameters at their best-known values. This tests whether a different learned single-cell encoder (scgpt vs. scvi) can push accuracy beyond 0.725. Given 5 remaining experiments, identifying whether the RNA encoder is a lever for improvement (or a near-irrelevant choice) is the highest-information experiment: if scgpt matches scvi_n200, we can deprioritize the encoder axis and focus on image encoder or profile setting; if it outperforms, we have a concrete new best to exploit in subsequent runs.

The best result so far is config_041 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc=0.725). The evidence clearly shows transformer aggregation > avgpool (+0.019) and scvi_n200 >> scgpt (+0.205), confirming the current best configuration. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation benefit is specific to the ViT-L image encoder or generalizable. Config_015 changes only the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) while holding all other proven-optimal settings (scvi_n200, transformer, weighted, multiprofile, multimodal) constant. This single-variable test will clarify whether the image encoder choice is a critical factor or whether the transformer aggregation provides robust gains across encoders. If resnet50 performs comparably, it broadens the search; if it drops significantly, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning around the config_041 neighborhood. With 4 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information single step that reduces uncertainty about an important design axis without abandoning the proven direction.

The current best (config_041, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. We have strong evidence that scgpt is a poor RNA encoder (0.520 vs 0.725), but pca_n2000—a fundamentally different linear method—has never been tested with this best architecture. Config_039 isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding all other settings at their empirically optimal values. This reduces uncertainty about whether scvi_n200's advantage is specific to deep generative encoding or whether a simpler linear projection could match/exceed it. If pca_n2000 performs comparably, it suggests the bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g., fusion or image encoder) and guides the remaining 3 experiments toward those dimensions. If it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 is locked in and we can exploit the remaining budget on finer architectural tweaks. This is the highest-information experiment given the sparse evidence on pca_n2000 in the best-architecture regime.

Evidence: The best config so far is config_041 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) at 0.7250 acc. All 7 completed experiments used multiprofile; the singleprofile dimension is entirely untested. Within multiprofile, transformer > avgpool and weighted > concat, and scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l is the dominant encoder pair. Question: config_004 tests whether the singleprofile architecture (no aggregation, direct fusion) with the proven best encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) and best fusion (weighted) can match or exceed the multiprofile + transformer pipeline. Rationale: With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, I need to either confirm the current best or find a competitive alternative. Singleprofile is the largest unexplored axis, and if it performs comparably or better, it opens a new exploitation direction for the final 2 runs. Choosing weighted over concat (config_002) is consistent with the small but consistent edge weighted has shown (0.7250 vs 0.7207).

The top-3 configurations (config_041: 0.725, config_025: 0.721, config_015: 0.713) all share scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, confirming these as the optimal backbone. The remaining uncertainty is the image-encoder × fusion interaction: imagenet_vit_l+weighted (0.725), imagenet_vit_l+concat (0.721), and resnet50+weighted (0.713) are tested, but resnet50+concat (config_049) is the only untested cell in this 2×2 grid. Testing it completes the picture of whether concat fusion might partially offset resnet50's slight disadvantage, or confirms that config_041's combination is the ceiling. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, resolving this last cell lets the final run either exploit a surprise winner or lock in the best-known configuration with confidence.

The best configuration found is config_041 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. All four combinations of {imagenet_vit_l, resnet50} × {weighted, concat} with transformer aggregation and scvi_n200/multiprofile have been tested, confirming transformer > avgpool and imagenet_vit_l ≥ resnet50. The remaining untested scvi_n200 + multiprofile configs all use avgpool, which has been consistently ~2% worse than transformer. Config_001 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the highest-expected-performance option among remaining untested configs, as it retains the proven best RNA encoder, multiprofile setting, and weighted fusion. While unlikely to surpass 0.7250, it is the best use of the final experiment slot: it confirms the avgpool penalty with resnet50 (complementing the imagenet_vit_l+avgpool result from config_009 at 0.7062) and solidifies the conclusion that transformer aggregation is the critical design choice, leaving no ambiguity in the final report.

With no prior evidence, I need to establish a strong baseline while testing the most impactful design axes simultaneously. Config_050 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) combines the strongest prior choices: scgpt (purpose-built single-cell foundation model for RNA), imagenet_vit_l (state-of-the-art vision encoder), transformer aggregation (most expressive for multiprofile), and weighted fusion (learnable combination of modalities). This tests whether the full multimodal pipeline with top-tier encoders and expressive aggregation/fusion can achieve high validation accuracy. If it performs well, it sets a strong bar and I can ablate components in later experiments. If it underperforms, subsequent experiments can isolate which component (encoder choice, aggregation, fusion) is the bottleneck. Given only 10 experiments for 51 configs, starting with the highest-prior configuration maximizes the chance of finding a strong solution early while still providing diagnostic information about the design space.

Evidence: config_050 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 52.0% accuracy / 47.9% F1, but with only one data point I cannot tell whether the image modality, the transformer aggregation, or the weighted fusion is actually contributing beyond what the RNA encoder alone provides. Question: config_010 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) is the cleanest single-variable ablation of config_050—it keeps the same RNA encoder (scgpt), same profile setting (multiprofile), and same aggregation (transformer), removing only the image branch. Why this is the best next experiment: establishing the RNA-only baseline is the highest-information experiment at this stage. If RNA alone approaches ~52%, the remaining 8 experiments should focus on RNA encoder/aggregation improvements and the image modality is deprioritized. If RNA alone is substantially lower (e.g., <45%), multimodal fusion is confirmed as a key lever and I should invest remaining budget in fusion strategies and image encoder choices. This single comparison partitions the search space efficiently and prevents wasting experiments on a modality combination that may not be the bottleneck.

The two completed experiments (config_050: multimodal/weighted, acc=0.520; config_010: RNA-only, acc=0.514) show only a marginal accuracy gain from adding the image modality, while F1 actually drops, suggesting the fusion strategy may be suboptimal. Config_040 is identical to config_050 except it uses concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, providing a clean single-variable ablation. This directly tests whether the weighted fusion is the bottleneck or whether a simple concatenation of modality representations performs comparably or better. Resolving this question early is critical: if concat outperforms weighted, it opens a clear exploitation path across other encoders; if they are similar, the fusion choice is not the limiting factor and I should pivot to testing alternative RNA encoders (pca_n2000, scvi_n200) in the remaining budget. With 7 experiments left, isolating this one variable now maximizes information per experiment.

The current best (config_050, acc=0.520) uses transformer aggregation with weighted fusion, scgpt, and imagenet_vit_l. The only other aggregation tested (in config_040) was also transformer with concat fusion, which underperformed. We have no evidence yet about whether avgpool aggregation could match or beat transformer in the multimodal multiprofile setting. config_019 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable comparison to the current best, changing only aggregation from transformer to avgpool. This is the best use of the next experiment because: (1) it directly tests a fundamental architectural choice with minimal confounding, (2) if avgpool performs comparably, it validates a simpler/faster architecture and frees later experiments to explore other dimensions (RNA encoder, image encoder), and (3) if it underperforms, it confirms transformer aggregation is critical and we can focus remaining budget on encoder and profile choices. With 6 experiments left, reducing uncertainty on this core design axis early is more valuable than jumping to a less-tested dimension.

The best result so far is config_019 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.542 accuracy, clearly establishing that avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion outperform transformer/concat for this multimodal setup. The remaining uncertainty is whether the specific RNA encoder (scgpt) is optimal for complementing the image features, or whether a different encoder like SCVI (a VAE-based latent representation) would interact more effectively with the imagenet_vit_l image features. Config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) holds the three best-performing design choices (avgpool, weighted, imagenet_vit_l) constant while swapping the RNA encoder to SCVI, which captures a fundamentally different latent space (variational posterior) than scgpt (generative model). This is the most informative single-variable extension of the current best: if SCVI matches or exceeds scgpt, it opens a new direction; if it falls short, it confirms scgpt as the preferred RNA encoder and lets us focus remaining budget on other axes. With 5 experiments left, this targeted test maximizes information gain about the RNA encoder dimension without risking the already-validated aggregation/fusion/image-encoder choices.

The dominant finding is that switching the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 (config_026 vs config_019, all else identical) produced a massive accuracy jump from 0.542 to 0.706, making scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted the clear best configuration. The most important untested dimension for this winning combination is the aggregation strategy: avgpool vs. transformer. With scgpt, avgpool was marginally better (0.542 vs 0.520), but the scvi_n200 latent representation may interact differently with transformer attention, potentially capturing cross-profile dependencies that simple pooling misses. config_027 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a single-variable change from the current best, directly testing whether transformer aggregation can push accuracy beyond 0.706. This is the highest-value experiment because it either confirms avgpool as optimal (reducing uncertainty and focusing remaining budget on other axes) or discovers a new best configuration, and it is the most natural logical extension of the strongest evidence in the search.

The strongest evidence shows scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_027, 0.725 acc) is the best configuration so far. With scgpt, weighted fusion consistently outperformed concat (0.520 vs 0.507 for transformer; similar gap expected for avgpool). However, the scgpt→scvi_n200 shift was so large (~0.20 acc) that the relative ranking of fusion strategies could plausibly differ. Config_017 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) is the single most direct exploitation of the best config, testing whether concat fusion might match or exceed weighted in the scvi_n200 regime. If it does, it opens a new direction; if not, it confirms weighted is optimal and lets us redirect remaining budget to image encoder (resnet50) or profile setting. With 3 experiments left after this, resolving the fusion question early maximizes the information value of the remaining trials.

The strongest evidence shows scvi_n200 as the dominant RNA encoder (0.725 vs ~0.52 for scgpt), with transformer+weighted as the best aggregation/fusion pair (0.7250 for config_027). The one major untested variable in this top region is the image encoder: all top results use imagenet_vit_l, but resnet50 has never been paired with scvi_n200. Config_015 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) directly tests whether the image encoder choice meaningfully affects performance when the RNA encoder and architecture are already optimal. If resnet50 matches imagenet_vit_l, it confirms we've found the plateau and the final experiment can focus on fine-tuning; if it lags significantly, it validates imagenet_vit_l as essential and rules out that direction. With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information experiment: it either confirms the current best is near-optimal or opens a new avenue, making it the best use of the next slot.

Evidence: The top-4 results are all scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with config_027 (vit_l, weighted) at 0.7250 as the best. Notably, config_015 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest F1 (0.6945) despite lower accuracy (0.7131), suggesting resnet50 captures complementary information. The one untested combination in this proven region is resnet50 + transformer + concat (config_021). This tests whether concat fusion interacts differently with resnet50 than weighted does, potentially closing the accuracy gap to vit_l. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, this is the highest-EV exploitation: it stays in the best-performing architecture family, tests a genuinely new interaction (resnet50×concat), and if it underperforms, the last experiment can pivot to an alternative (e.g., config_034 or a singleprofile variant) with clearer information about which axis to explore.

The strongest evidence shows scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile is the dominant combination (best: config_027 at 0.725). We have three of four cells in the aggregation×fusion 2×2 matrix for this combination: transformer+weighted (0.725), transformer+concat (0.721), avgpool+weighted (0.706). Config_034 (avgpool+concat) completes this matrix, clarifying whether the interaction between aggregation and fusion is purely additive or if there's a specific synergy. While it is unlikely to surpass 0.725, it is the most logically informative remaining test within the proven best-encoder regime, and as the final experiment it closes the design gap with minimal risk of wasting budget on a structurally inferior setting (e.g., singleprofile or pca_n2000).

With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether a full multimodal pipeline with strong encoders and expressive aggregation can achieve high validation accuracy. Config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) tests the most capable combination of encoders with a standard, well-understood fusion strategy. Choosing the highest-capacity multimodal setup first maximizes the chance of establishing a high accuracy floor early in the budget, while the transformer aggregation and concat fusion keep the design interpretable for follow-up ablations.

With only one completed experiment (config_008: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat → 0.7207 acc), evidence is extremely sparse and the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually contributing meaningful signal over a single-modality baseline. If RNA alone approaches 0.72, the image modality and its associated complexity (image encoder, fusion) are not adding value, and we should redirect remaining budget toward optimizing the RNA path or a different image encoder.
