This single experiment resolves the highest-impact architectural question with minimal confounding, making it the best use of experiment 2 under the limited 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved the best accuracy (0.7207), substantially outperforming the RNA-only baseline (0.6530), confirming that the multimodal architecture with these encoders is the right direction. Uncertainty: the only untested dimension within this exact backbone is the fusion strategy—concat vs. weighted. Question: Does weighted fusion improve over simple concatenation when combining the two modality representations? This is a clean single-variable change (only fusion differs from config_008), so any accuracy shift can be attributed to the fusion method. With 7 experiments remaining, this low-risk exploitation step either confirms concat is optimal (freeing us to explore other dimensions) or yields an immediate improvement to build upon, making it the highest-information-per-experiment choice right now.

Evidence: The top-3 experiments all use multimodal + multiprofile + imagenet_vit_l + transformer, with weighted fusion (config_029, 0.7250) slightly edging out concat (config_008, 0.7207). RNA-only (config_001, 0.6530) confirms multimodal is essential. The current best uses scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, but no alternative RNA encoder has been tested in this strong multimodal setting. Question: config_010 swaps only the RNA encoder to scgpt while keeping imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion fixed, directly testing whether a different RNA representation can push accuracy above 0.725. Why: With 6 experiments remaining, identifying the best RNA encoder in the proven multimodal/transformer/weighted pipeline is the highest-leverage single-variable exploration; it either confirms scvi_n200 is optimal (allowing exploitation of other axes) or reveals a new best encoder to build on.

Evidence: The best config so far is config_029 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.7250. The only image encoder tested in multimodal settings is imagenet_vit_l; resnet50 remains untested. scgpt was clearly inferior to scvi_n200 (0.52 vs 0.72), confirming scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder to use. Question: Does the image encoder choice (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) materially affect performance? config_023 is a clean single-variable comparison to config_029 (only image encoder differs: resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l, all else identical: scvi_n200, transformer, weighted, multiprofile). Why this is the best use of the experiment: Resolving the image encoder question is the highest-uncertainty architectural decision remaining. If resnet50 is competitive, it opens many more combinations; if it is significantly worse, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is critical and we can focus remaining budget on aggregation and profile-setting refinements. With 5 experiments left, resolving this binary choice first maximizes information for subsequent decisions.

The best result so far is config_029 (scvi_n200 + vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250), with config_008 (same but concat) close behind at 0.7207. The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 over scgpt and multimodal over RNA-only. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation could match or exceed it when paired with the best fusion (weighted) and best encoders (scvi_n200 + vit_l). Config_042 isolates this single variable (aggregation: transformer→avgpool) while holding all other components at their empirically best settings. This is a minimal, high-information experiment: if avgpool performs comparably, it confirms the architecture is robust; if it underperforms, it confirms transformer aggregation is a critical component. With 4 experiments remaining after this, establishing whether aggregation matters is essential before committing to further refinements.

Evidence: The top configuration (config_029, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. RNA encoder choice has been the most impactful variable (scvi_n200 at 0.725 vs scgpt at 0.520), but pca_n2000—a linear, non-learned dimensionality reduction—has not been tested in any multimodal setting. Uncertainty: It is unclear whether the learned latent space of scvi_n200 is truly necessary or whether a simpler linear projection (pca_n2000) could perform comparably when paired with the strong image encoder and transformer aggregation. This experiment isolically tests the RNA encoder variable within the best-known architecture (multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted), making it a clean single-factor comparison to config_029. If pca_n2000 matches or approaches scvi_n200, it reveals the RNA signal is relatively low-dimensional and the architecture is robust; if it falls well below, it confirms the learned representation is essential and focuses remaining budget on image-encoder or profile-setting refinements. With 3 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information experiment to either confirm or rule out a major design axis before final exploitation.

The current best is config_029 (0.7250 acc) with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile. All top performers use multiprofile with transformer aggregation, but the singleprofile + None aggregation combination remains entirely untested with the best-known encoders. config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, None aggregation, weighted fusion, singleprofile) isolates whether the profile/aggregation axis can yield a different (potentially better) operating point while keeping the three strongest components fixed. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve with 2 experiments left: if singleprofile + None matches or beats 0.7250, the final experiment can exploit that direction; if it falls short, we confirm multiprofile + transformer is optimal and the final experiment can focus on fine-tuning within that proven region (e.g., testing config_022 or config_043 as a last check).

The top-3 results (config_029: 0.7250, config_008: 0.7207, config_023: 0.7131) all share scvi_n200 + transformer + multiprofile + multimodal, with variation only in image encoder and fusion. Notably, config_023 (resnet50, weighted) achieves the highest F1 (0.6945) despite slightly lower accuracy, suggesting resnet50 captures complementary information. config_022 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the only untested configuration that preserves all four winning attributes while testing the resnet50+concat pairing. This clarifies whether the resnet50 F1 advantage is fusion-specific or general, and whether concat might better exploit resnet50's feature space. With only one experiment remaining after this, this is the highest-value exploration in the immediate neighborhood of the current best, as all other untested configs deviate more substantially (worse RNA encoder, avgpool, or singleprofile) and are unlikely to surpass 0.7250.

The best result so far is config_029 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). Evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 as RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as image encoder, multiprofile, and transformer aggregation over avgpool (0.7250 vs 0.7062). Since this is the final experiment, I select config_005 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) as the highest-expected-value untested option: it retains the two best-performing encoders and multiprofile, testing only the aggregation/fusion axis. While transformer+weighted is favored, the small gap between weighted and concat (0.7250 vs 0.7207) means config_005 has a non-trivial chance of being competitive, and it is the closest untested configuration to the known optimum. No other untested config maintains both top encoders with multiprofile.

With no prior evidence, the goal is to establish a strong baseline while gaining information about multiple key design dimensions simultaneously. config_048 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) combines the strongest available components: a purpose-built single-cell foundation model (scgpt) for RNA, a large pretrained ViT-L for images, transformer-based aggregation for expressive multi-profile integration, and weighted fusion to let the model learn modality importance. If this performs well, it confirms the multimodal + strong-encoder direction and I can ablate individual components in later experiments. If it underperforms, it signals that complexity (transformer aggregation, ViT-L, or weighted fusion) may be harmful, directing exploration toward simpler alternatives. This single experiment reduces uncertainty across four major design axes (model type, encoder quality, aggregation, fusion) and sets a high bar for the remaining 9 experiments.

With only one completed experiment (config_048: multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → acc 0.520), the largest remaining uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion actually adds value over a strong unimodal baseline. Config_022 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) is a clean ablation: it keeps the same image encoder and aggregation strategy as config_048, removing only the RNA modality and fusion step. If image-only performs comparably (~0.52), the RNA contribution is marginal and I should redirect remaining budget toward unimodal optimization or simpler multimodal variants. If image-only is substantially worse, it confirms that multimodal fusion is worth pursuing and justifies investing the remaining 7 experiments in refining the multimodal configuration (encoder choices, aggregation, fusion). This single experiment resolves the highest-impact design question before committing further budget.

Evidence: config_048 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.520), while image-only (config_022) was weak (0.260), confirming that the multimodal scgpt+ViT-L backbone with transformer aggregation is the strongest direction. Uncertainty: we have not tested whether the weighted fusion is optimal or whether simple concatenation (concat) of the two modal embeddings could yield a stronger signal. This experiment (config_015) isolates exactly one variable—fusion strategy (weighted → concat)—while holding all other components at their known-best settings. It is the best next experiment because it is a clean, minimal ablation of the highest-leverage architectural choice in the current best config, and the result will directly inform whether to exploit the weighted-fusion path or pivot to concat-fusion for the remaining 7 experiments.

The current best (config_048, acc=0.520) uses scgpt as the RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. The image-only baseline (0.260) confirms multimodal fusion is critical, and weighted fusion slightly edges out concat (0.520 vs 0.507). However, we have no evidence on whether scgpt is the optimal RNA encoder. config_003 is a clean single-variable swap: it replaces scgpt with scvi_n200 while keeping all other settings identical to the current best (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile, multimodal). This directly tests whether the learned generative RNA representation (scgpt) is meaningfully superior to the variational autoencoder (scvi_n200), reducing uncertainty on a fundamental architectural choice before committing remaining budget to fine-tuning aggregation or image encoder variants.

Evidence: config_003 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 acc, far outperforming scgpt-based configs (~0.52). The only other tested fusion variant (config_015, scgpt+concat) was ~1.3 pts below its weighted counterpart (config_048), suggesting weighted fusion may be important but the gap was small. Question: Does the fusion method (weighted vs concat) matter when paired with the superior scvi_n200 encoder? config_046 changes only fusion from weighted to concat while keeping all other settings identical to the current best (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, multiprofile). This is the cleanest single-variable ablation against the best config, giving unambiguous evidence about whether weighted fusion is a meaningful lever or whether concat is equally effective. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving this design choice early informs whether to focus subsequent budget on image encoder or aggregation variations.

Evidence: config_003 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.7250), and the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) is clearly the dominant factor (~0.21 gap). Fusion method (weighted vs concat) shows only a marginal difference (0.7250 vs 0.7207). The image encoder dimension remains unexplored for the top-performing RNA encoder. Question: Does resnet50 match or exceed imagenet_vit_l when paired with scvi_n200, transformer, and weighted fusion? This is a clean single-variable change from the best config. Why this is the best use of experiment 6: It reduces uncertainty on the second-most-important design axis (image encoder) while keeping all proven settings fixed. If resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the current config is near-optimal and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning; if it underperforms significantly, it validates imagenet_vit_l and narrows the search space for experiments 7-10.

The evidence strongly establishes scvi_n200 as the dominant RNA encoder (0.71–0.73 vs 0.51–0.52 for scgpt), and the current best (config_003, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. However, all scvi_n200 experiments to date have used transformer aggregation; no avgpool variant has been tested with this encoder. Config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is a clean, single-variable change from the current best, directly testing whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler pooling strategy matches or exceeds it. If avgpool performs comparably, it confirms robustness and frees a later experiment for finer-tuning; if it underperforms, it confirms transformer is critical and narrows the search. With 3 experiments remaining after this one, reducing uncertainty on the aggregation dimension—while holding the other three parameters at their best-known values—is the highest-information use of this slot.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_003) is the current best at 0.725 acc, and all tested multiprofile scvi_n200 variants cluster around 0.71–0.725, suggesting we are near the ceiling of the multiprofile architecture. The singleprofile setting (aggregation=None) has never been tested with the top-performing encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l). This experiment tests whether the singleprofile architecture, which bypasses the transformer/avgpool aggregation step, can either match or exceed the multiprofile best by handling the two modalities differently. Choosing weighted fusion (config_051) over concat is supported by the consistent (if small) edge of weighted over concat in multiprofile (0.725 vs 0.721). With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information test: if singleprofile beats 0.725, we find a new best; if it doesn't, we confirm multiprofile is optimal and can spend the final experiment on a minor multiprofile refinement rather than chasing a dead end.

The best result so far is config_003 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. All tested scvi_n200 variants confirm this architecture is near-optimal, but pca_n2000 has never been tested in the multimodal setting with the best image encoder, aggregation, and fusion. Config_043 isolates the RNA encoder variable (pca_n2000 vs scvi_n200) while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values, directly testing whether a simpler linear projection could match or exceed the learned scvi representation. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, this is the highest-information experiment: if pca_n2000 performs comparably, the last experiment can explore a further refinement; if it underperforms significantly, it confirms config_003 as the optimal configuration and the final experiment can be used for a minor perturbation around it.

Evidence: The top-4 experiments all use scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with config_003 (scvi_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 being the best. The consistent pattern shows scvi_n200 >> scgpt/pca, transformer > avgpool, and ViT-L ≥ resnet50. Uncertainty: We have not tested the scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat combination, which is the closest untested variant in the best-performing family. This experiment tests whether the concat fusion with resnet50 under transformer aggregation can approach the 0.71–0.72 range established by config_012 (weighted, 0.713). As the final experiment, config_025 has the highest expected accuracy among all remaining untested configurations (~0.70–0.71), making it the best use of the last budget slot to either confirm the ceiling or provide a small improvement over the current best.

With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether a strong multimodal fusion architecture can achieve high validation accuracy, and which encoder combination is most effective. This experiment tests the core multimodal hypothesis using the strongest available pre-trained encoders (scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for images) with multiprofile input, avgpool aggregation (simpler and less overfitting-prone than transformer for a first test), and weighted fusion (more flexible than concat for combining heterogeneous modalities). If this performs well, it establishes a strong baseline and direction for exploitation; if it underperforms, it signals that one or more components (encoder choice, fusion strategy, or multimodal integration itself) need simplification, guiding subsequent ablation experiments within the remaining 9-experiment budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_016: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc≈0.542), evidence is very sparse. The most impactful architectural uncertainty is whether the simple avgpool aggregation is sufficient or whether a transformer-based aggregation would better capture inter-feature relationships in the multimodal representation. config_048 changes exactly one factor from config_016 (aggregation: avgpool → transformer) while holding all other settings constant (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion, multiprofile, multimodal). This clean single-factor comparison will isolate the effect of aggregation strategy, which is likely a high-leverage design choice. If transformer aggregation improves accuracy, it opens a strong exploitation path for subsequent experiments; if not, it confirms avgpool is adequate and redirects budget toward other factors (RNA encoder, image encoder, fusion). This is the best use of experiment 2 under limited budget because it reduces uncertainty on a high-impact dimension with minimal confounding.

Evidence: Two experiments (config_016, config_048) show that scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + weighted fusion yields ~0.52-0.54 accuracy, with avgpool slightly outperforming transformer. The evidence is sparse (n=2), so we need to reduce uncertainty on key design axes. Question: Does the fusion method (weighted vs concat) materially affect performance when all other hyperparameters are held at the best-known settings (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, multiprofile)? config_011 is a clean single-variable change from the current best (config_016), isolating the fusion method. Why best use of budget: With 7 experiments left, resolving whether concat can beat weighted is a high-value binary decision that either confirms our exploitation path or opens a superior branch. It avoids confounding multiple changes and gives a direct, interpretable comparison against our current best.

The three completed experiments (config_016, config_048, config_011) all use scgpt + imagenet_vit_l, varying only aggregation and fusion. The best so far is config_016 (avgpool + weighted, acc=0.542), but the image encoder dimension (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) remains completely untested. Config_014 (scgpt + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) isolates the image encoder as a single variable change from the current best, directly testing whether a CNN backbone (ResNet50) can match or beat the ViT-L encoder for cellular image features. This is the highest-uncertainty design choice left unexplored, and resolving it early with 6 experiments remaining will guide whether to invest further in ViT-based or CNN-based image encoders for the rest of the budget.

The best result so far is config_016 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.542), and all four completed experiments use scgpt as the RNA encoder, leaving the RNA encoder dimension completely unexplored. Config_045 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) holds the three settings that produced the best result fixed and tests only the RNA encoder, isolating whether a different learned RNA representation (scvi_n200) can match or beat scgpt. This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact design choice remaining. With 5 experiments left, resolving whether the RNA encoder is a meaningful lever (or whether scgpt is already near-optimal) is critical: if scvi_n200 performs comparably, we can explore other dimensions; if it is clearly worse, we can confidently lock in scgpt and focus remaining budget on fine-tuning image encoder or fusion details around the current best.

The dominant finding from the 5 completed experiments is that scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder dramatically outperforms scgpt (0.706 vs ~0.52-0.54), making it the clear direction to exploit. The best config (config_045: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706) leaves the aggregation method as an important untested variable for this RNA encoder. For scgpt, avgpool slightly beat transformer (0.542 vs 0.520), but scvi_n200 produces a fundamentally different latent representation that may interact differently with transformer-based aggregation. Config_021 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is a clean single-variable change from the best config, testing whether transformer aggregation can push accuracy beyond 0.706. This is the highest-value next experiment: it either confirms avgpool is optimal (focusing remaining budget on other levers) or discovers a further improvement in the most promising configuration family.

Evidence: scvi_n200 dramatically outperforms scgpt (~0.71-0.73 vs ~0.52-0.54), and within scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation (0.725) beats avgpool (0.706) with weighted fusion. The current best is config_021 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, acc=0.725). Question: config_031 tests whether concat fusion can outperform weighted fusion when paired with transformer aggregation in the scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l family. While scgpt data suggests weighted>concat, the interaction with transformer aggregation and the much richer scvi_n200 representations may differ. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the clearly dominant direction (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer) while resolving the one remaining untested fusion variant in that family, directly targeting a potential improvement over the current best with 3 experiments still remaining.

Evidence: The strongest results (0.725 acc, 0.685 F1) come from scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_021), with transformer+concat (0.721) and avgpool+weighted (0.706) close behind. The scgpt encoder is clearly inferior (~0.52-0.54). Within the multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l space, we've tested 3 of 4 aggregation/fusion combos and the gains from further variation are marginal. Key uncertainty: whether the multiprofile setting is actually beneficial or whether a simpler singleprofile architecture with the same strong encoders could reduce overfitting and improve validation accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted fusion, isolating the profile-setting design choice while keeping the proven best encoders and fusion strategy. With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information test: if singleprofile matches or exceeds 0.725, it opens a simpler, potentially more generalizable direction for the final experiment; if it underperforms, it confirms multiprofile is essential and we can focus the last experiment on fine-tuning within the multiprofile space.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the dominant configuration family (0.706–0.725 accuracy vs. 0.52–0.54 for all other RNA/image combinations). Within this family, we have tested three of four aggregation×fusion combinations: avgpool+weighted (0.706), transformer+weighted (0.725), and transformer+concat (0.721). The only remaining cell is avgpool+concat (config_034). Testing it completes the 2×2 matrix, confirming whether transformer+weighted is truly optimal or whether a different combination might edge above 0.725. With only one experiment remaining after this, confirming the optimal aggregation/fusion pairing for the best RNA+image setup is the highest-value use of this slot: if config_034 underperforms (as expected), the final experiment can be a targeted fine-tune or a confirmation run; if it unexpectedly outperforms, we immediately identify a new best. No other untested configuration has a realistic chance of exceeding 0.725 given the large gaps observed across RNA encoders and image backbones.

The strongest evidence across 9 experiments clearly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + weighted (config_021, acc=0.7250) as the best configuration. The only untested variable within this top-performing family is the image encoder: all scvi_n200 multiprofile results used imagenet_vit_l, while resnet50 has only been tested with the much weaker scgpt encoder. Config_025 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted) directly tests whether swapping the image encoder to resnet50 could improve upon 0.7250 or confirm imagenet_vit_l as optimal. As the final experiment, this is the highest-value exploitation step: it keeps every other hyperparameter at its empirically best setting and probes the one remaining axis of variation, giving the clearest signal about whether the current best is truly at a local optimum or whether a different backbone could push accuracy higher.

With no prior evidence (experiment 1 of 10), the priority is to establish a strong reference point for the multimodal setting, which is the natural target for 'multimodal cellular profiling.' Config_010 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt + resnet50, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) is a well-balanced, canonical multimodal configuration: scgpt provides an expressive learned RNA representation, resnet50 is a reliable pretrained image encoder, transformer aggregation captures inter-cell interactions, and concat fusion is simple and robust. Testing this first tells us (1) whether the multimodal combination is viable and at what performance level, (2) whether the chosen encoders and aggregation are adequate, and (3) gives a concrete baseline to guide ablation (e.g., swap to imagenet_vit_l, try weighted fusion, or test single-modality baselines) in subsequent experiments. It is the highest-information single experiment to anchor the remaining 9 trials.

With only one data point (config_010: multimodal, scgpt+resnet50, transformer, concat → 47.1% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion is actually contributing or whether one modality dominates. Config_001 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) is the cleanest single-modality baseline matching the RNA side of config_010 exactly. If RNA-only approaches 47%, the image modality adds little value and future effort should focus on RNA encoder/aggregation improvements. If RNA-only is substantially lower, image is critical and we should prioritize image encoder and fusion strategy experiments. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental architectural question (is multimodal worth it?) before committing remaining budget to specific improvements.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, scgpt, transformer) achieved 0.514 acc, outperforming config_010 (multimodal, scgpt, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.471 acc. The 4.3-point drop when adding the image modality via concat fusion suggests the combination strategy may be the bottleneck rather than the image features themselves. Question: Does switching from concat to weighted fusion (config_038) recover multimodal performance, isolating whether the fusion mechanism is the issue while keeping all other settings (scgpt, resnet50, transformer, multiprofile) identical to config_010? Why this is the best next step: It is a clean single-variable comparison with config_010, directly testing the most likely cause of the multimodal underperformance. If weighted fusion helps, it opens a promising multimodal direction for exploitation in remaining experiments; if it does not, it strengthens the case that resnet50 image features are uninformative here, redirecting effort toward RNA-only improvements or a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) in subsequent trials.

Evidence: RNA-only with scgpt+transformer (config_001, acc=0.514) outperforms both multimodal+resnet50 experiments (config_010 concat=0.471, config_038 weighted=0.494), suggesting ResNet50 image features are not complementing scgpt RNA features under transformer aggregation. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the image modality can add value with a different encoder, or whether the bottleneck is specifically ResNet50's feature representation. This experiment tests scgpt + imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the image encoder as the variable while keeping the best-performing RNA encoder and aggregation. If ViT also underperforms RNA-only, we gain strong evidence to pivot fully toward RNA-only optimization with the remaining 6 experiments. If it succeeds, it identifies a promising multimodal direction to exploit. This is the highest-information experiment for the central question of whether multimodal fusion can beat the current best.

The best result so far is RNA-only scgpt+transformer (0.514), while the best multimodal config is scgpt+imagenet_vit_l+transformer+concat (0.507). For the weaker resnet50 encoder, weighted fusion (0.494) outperformed concat (0.471), suggesting fusion strategy matters. Config_027 tests whether weighted fusion with the stronger ViT-L image encoder + transformer aggregation can close or close the gap to the RNA-only baseline. This is a single-variable extension (concat→weighted) of the best multimodal result, directly testing whether improved fusion can make the multimodal model competitive or superior, which is critical for exploiting the remaining 5 experiments toward the highest accuracy.

The current best is config_027 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc 0.5200). All top-performing multimodal configs used transformer aggregation, so it's unclear whether the transformer is genuinely contributing or whether the gains come solely from the image encoder and weighted fusion. Config_035 is a clean single-variable change (transformer → avgpool) from the best config, directly testing whether attention-based aggregation adds value over simpler pooling. If avgpool performs comparably, it confirms the architecture is robust and frees remaining budget to explore other dimensions (RNA encoder, profile setting). If transformer clearly wins, we've locked in the aggregation choice and can focus remaining experiments on RNA encoder or profile variations. This is the highest-information single step to reduce architectural uncertainty before committing the last 4 experiments to exploitation.

The current best (config_035, acc=0.5420) uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. Across all completed experiments, imagenet_vit_l consistently outperforms resnet50, avgpool outperforms transformer, and weighted outperforms concat. The image-side pipeline (imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) appears robust. The main untested lever is the RNA encoder: all multimodal experiments so far used scgpt, but scvi_n200 has not been paired with this winning image pipeline. Config_019 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) directly tests whether a learned generative RNA encoder can surpass scgpt while holding the strongest image-side configuration fixed. This is the highest-value experiment because it either identifies a new best configuration or confirms scgpt as optimal, reducing uncertainty on the most impactful remaining design axis with 3 experiments still in budget.

The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted (config_019) achieved 0.706, far exceeding all scgpt-based configs (~0.54 best). With only 2 experiments remaining, I want to test the most direct single-variable extension of this best config: replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping all other settings identical. Evidence from scgpt experiments (config_027 vs config_035) showed avgpool slightly outperformed transformer, but scvi_n200's richer latent representations may interact differently with transformer's token-mixing capacity. This experiment directly reduces uncertainty about whether aggregation architecture can further improve on the 0.706 result, and if it fails, confirms avgpool is optimal, allowing the final experiment to focus on a different axis (e.g., fusion type or profile setting).

Evidence: config_031 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.725) is the clear best, and all comparisons show weighted fusion outperforms concat (e.g., 0.725 vs 0.706 for transformer, 0.520 vs 0.507 for scgpt+vit). Question: config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) is the only untested variant that retains all three top-performing components (strong RNA encoder, strong image encoder, transformer aggregation) while isolating the fusion method. Why: With only 1 experiment remaining, this is the most informative test near the optimum—it confirms whether the weighted-fusion advantage persists with the much stronger scvi_n200 signal or whether concat becomes competitive, reducing residual uncertainty about the design space around the best configuration. No other untested config plausibly beats 0.725, so this is the best use of the penultimate slot.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoder pair (0.706–0.725 vs. 0.47–0.54 for alternatives), and weighted fusion as slightly superior to concat. All top-3 results use multiprofile + transformer/avgpool aggregation. However, singleprofile with the best encoders has never been tested. config_043 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) tests whether removing the multiprofile aggregation complexity (which introduces an additional modeling step) could improve generalization while retaining the proven best encoders and fusion. As the final experiment, this is the highest-value untested combination: it pairs the two clearly superior encoders with the preferred fusion strategy while exploring the one remaining architectural dimension (profile setting) that could plausibly shift performance. If it underperforms, config_031 (0.725) remains the best result.

With no prior evidence, the goal is to establish a strong, well-motivated multimodal baseline that reduces uncertainty about the core design space. config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) uses two well-established encoders (scVI for scRNA-seq, ResNet50 for images) combined with a principled multi-profile aggregation (transformer) and a simple, interpretable fusion (weighted). This configuration sits near the 'center of mass' of the design space: it is complex enough to be competitive but relies on robust, validated components so that any failure signals a structural issue rather than an encoder choice. Performance here gives a strong reference point: if it is competitive, subsequent experiments can explore scgpt/ViT-L upgrades and alternative fusion; if it underperforms, I can ablate to identify whether multiprofile+transformer or the specific encoder pair is the bottleneck. With 9 experiments remaining, this single informative anchor maximally guides the next 9 choices.

Evidence: config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved 71.3% accuracy / 69.5% F1, establishing a working multimodal baseline. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether the relatively modest ResNet50 image encoder is a bottleneck compared to the more powerful ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L. This experiment (config_033) makes a single clean change—swapping image_encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l—while holding the RNA encoder (scvi_n200), aggregation (transformer), fusion (weighted), and profile setting (multiprofile) constant. This directly tests whether a stronger visual backbone translates into higher validation accuracy within the same architectural framework. It is the best use of experiment 2 because: (1) it is a minimal, interpretable ablation that isolates one high-impact variable, (2) if ViT-L helps, it unlocks a family of promising configs (017, 042, 051, etc.) for the remaining 8 experiments, and (3) with only one prior data point, a targeted exploitation of the proven architecture is more informative than a broad exploration or a baseline that would not change the multimodal search trajectory.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_004 and config_033) differ only in image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l), with ViT giving ~1.2% higher accuracy (0.725 vs 0.713) but slightly lower F1. Both use scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, so we have zero information about whether a different RNA encoder (scgpt) could improve performance with the best image encoder. Question: Does scgpt, a generative RNA encoder with a different inductive bias than the variational scvi_n200, complement the ViT image features better or worse under the same transformer+weighted fusion setup? Why this is the best next step: With only 2 data points and both sharing the same RNA encoder, the RNA encoder dimension is completely unexplored. Testing scgpt with the best-performing image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and the same aggregation/fusion (transformer/weighted) isolates the RNA encoder effect. If scgpt improves accuracy, it opens a high-value direction for the remaining 7 experiments; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 is the right choice and can focus exploitation on fusion/aggregation variations. This is the highest-information experiment to reduce uncertainty on a core design axis.

The current best is config_033 (scvi_n200 + ViT-L + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725). Evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 over scgpt (~20pt gap) and ViT-L over ResNet50 (~1.2pt gain). The key remaining uncertainty within this promising direction is the fusion strategy: weighted vs. concat. Config_017 is a clean single-variable ablation of config_033 (only fusion changes from weighted to concat), isolating whether the learned weighted combination adds value over simple concatenation. This is the best use of the next slot because it directly exploits the strongest configuration while resolving a high-impact design question, and with 6 experiments remaining, we can then test aggregation (avgpool vs. transformer) and profile setting in subsequent runs.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_033 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725), with config_017 (same but concat fusion, acc=0.721) close behind. Both use transformer aggregation. scvi_n200 clearly dominates scgpt (0.725 vs 0.520), and imagenet_vit_l edges out resnet50. Uncertainty: It is unclear whether the transformer aggregation is genuinely contributing to performance or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation would perform comparably, which would simplify the architecture without cost. This experiment (config_042: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) directly tests aggregation method while holding the best encoder and fusion choices constant. If avgpool matches transformer, we gain architectural simplicity; if it falls short, we confirm transformer's value and can focus remaining budget on other levers (e.g., singleprofile vs multiprofile or fusion tuning). This is the highest-information single test given 5 remaining experiments.

Evidence: All 5 completed experiments used multiprofile, and the current best (config_033: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) is multiprofile. The only major untested architectural dimension is profile_setting. Question: config_021 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) directly tests whether the multiprofile + transformer aggregation complexity is actually contributing to performance or whether a simpler singleprofile pipeline with the same strong encoders is competitive. Why this is the best next experiment: With 4 experiments remaining, resolving this fundamental design choice is high-value. If singleprofile matches or beats 0.725, it opens a simpler, potentially more tunable path. If it falls short, it confirms multiprofile + transformer is essential and the remaining budget should focus on fine-tuning within that space (e.g., fusion or aggregation variants). This reduces the largest remaining uncertainty before committing the final experiments to exploitation.

Evidence: The best config (config_033, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile. scgpt was clearly inferior (0.520), and scvi_n200 consistently outperforms across tested settings. However, pca_n2000 has never been tested in the optimal multimodal configuration space. This experiment (config_011: pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) is a clean single-variable swap of the RNA encoder, isolating whether the learned scvi representation is truly necessary or whether a simpler linear PCA projection suffices. If pca_n2000 is competitive, it confirms the bottleneck is elsewhere and frees future experiments to explore other dimensions; if it is substantially worse, it firmly validates scvi_n200 and lets us focus the remaining 3 experiments on confirming the best config's robustness or testing marginal variants. With only 3 experiments left after this one, reducing uncertainty on the most impactful untested variable (RNA encoder) in the top-performing configuration is the highest-value use of this slot.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile is clearly the best sub-space (0.725 for transformer+weighted, 0.721 for transformer+concat, 0.706 for avgpool+weighted). The only untested combination in this top sub-space is avgpool+concat (config_051). This experiment completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the best encoder pair, clarifying whether there is a non-additive interaction that could unexpectedly boost performance. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, it is the most informative remaining test within the proven-best architecture family. With only 2 experiments left after this, confirming the interaction structure (or ruling out a surprise) is the best use of budget before finalizing the winner as config_033.

The best config so far (config_033: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.725) has all four of its direct single-parameter neighbors already tested (transformer+concat=0.721, avgpool+weighted=0.706, avgpool+concat=0.715, resnet50+transformer+weighted=0.713). The only remaining untested variant in the high-performing scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer region is config_024 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat). While resnet50 is ~1.2% below vit_l and concat is ~0.4% below weighted for transformer aggregation, this experiment tests whether the interaction of concat fusion with transformer aggregation on the weaker image encoder produces any unexpected synergy. Given that only 1 experiment remains after this one and all other untested configurations involve clearly inferior components (scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, or unimodal baselines), config_024 is the highest-probability candidate to approach or exceed the current best, and it provides the most informative data point to guide the final experiment.

The current best is config_033 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725), and all four aggregation×fusion combinations for that exact encoder pair have been tested. The strongest remaining untested combination uses the proven-best RNA encoder (scvi_n200), multiprofile setting, and weighted fusion (which showed a particularly large advantage over concat for resnet50: 0.713 vs 0.688), paired with the second-best image encoder (resnet50) and avgpool aggregation. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, config_048 represents the highest-prior untested configuration given the evidence: weighted fusion is critical for resnet50, and this is the last experiment in the budget, so exploiting the most validated component choices in an untested pairing is the most rational final probe.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a clear, interpretable baseline for the multimodal pipeline. config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the most standard 'vanilla' multimodal configuration: it combines both modalities, uses a learned RNA latent (scvi_n200) with a conventional CNN (resnet50), and applies the simplest aggregation (avgpool) and fusion (concat). This anchors the search at a reasonable performance level and, crucially, isolates the contribution of each design axis—subsequent experiments can then systematically upgrade the image encoder (to imagenet_vit_l), the RNA encoder (to pca_n2000 or scgpt), the aggregation (to transformer), or the fusion (to weighted) to determine which changes yield the largest gains. Starting here maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-run budget by giving a clean reference point against which all component upgrades can be measured.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieved 63.2% accuracy, giving a single baseline. The most uncertain and potentially high-impact design choice is the image encoder: ResNet50 is a relatively modest CNN, while ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L is substantially more expressive and better suited for cellular morphology. Question: config_042 changes only the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while holding all other variables (scvi_n200, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) constant, giving a clean single-variable test of whether a stronger image encoder lifts validation accuracy. Why this is the best next experiment: with 8 experiments remaining, identifying whether the image encoder is a critical bottleneck determines whether subsequent experiments should prioritize ViT-based configurations. A large gain would justify exploring ViT + transformer aggregation + scgpt combinations; a small gain would redirect effort toward RNA encoder or aggregation choices. This single-variable comparison maximizes information per experiment under the limited budget.

The two completed experiments show that switching the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l yielded a large +8.3% accuracy gain (0.632→0.715), establishing config_042 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) as the current best. The next most impactful untested dimension is the aggregation method: avgpool is a simple mean that discards spatial/positional structure, while transformer aggregation can capture richer cross-modal interactions and per-token relationships. Config_018 is a clean single-variable change from config_042 (only aggregation changes from avgpool→transformer), so any performance delta is directly attributable to the aggregation choice. With 7 experiments remaining, testing this high-leverage architectural component early will either confirm a new best to build on or rule out transformer aggregation, reducing uncertainty before committing further budget to RNA-encoder or fusion variants.

Evidence: The image encoder (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) showed the largest performance gain (+8.3% acc), and transformer aggregation gave a small additional edge over avgpool (0.7207 vs 0.7150). The current best (config_018) uses scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, but we have not yet tested whether an alternative learned RNA encoder (scgpt) could improve further while keeping the proven image encoder and aggregation fixed. Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder when paired with imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation? This is a clean single-variable comparison against the current best. Why: With 6 experiments remaining, reducing uncertainty on the RNA encoder dimension is critical—if scgpt helps, it opens a new exploitation path; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 is optimal and can pivot to fusion or profile-setting refinements. This is the highest-information experiment available that directly extends the current best configuration.

The current best is config_018 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.7207. The evidence strongly favors: (1) imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (~8.4% gain), (2) scvi_n200 over scgpt (~21% gain), and (3) transformer over avgpool (small but consistent gain). The only untested dimension on this best-known backbone is the fusion method (concat vs. weighted). config_044 tests weighted fusion with the exact same encoders and aggregation as config_018, directly exploiting the strongest evidence while resolving the remaining uncertainty about whether learned modality weighting can push accuracy above 0.72. With 5 experiments left, this is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step: if weighted fusion helps, it confirms a direction for further refinement; if not, we can pivot to exploring pca_n2000 or singleprofile variants with the remaining budget.

The current best (config_044: scvi_n200 + ViT-L + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250) has established that a strong image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion are the key components. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the learned scvi_n200 RNA representations are truly necessary or whether a higher-dimensional linear projection (PCA_n2000) suffices when paired with the best image encoder and fusion. Config_041 isolates this single variable (RNA encoder: scvi_n200 → pca_n2000) while keeping all other settings at their proven-best values. If PCA performs comparably, it confirms the image modality dominates and frees us to explore other dimensions; if it drops significantly (as scgpt did, 0.507), it confirms learned RNA representations are essential and we should exploit the scvi_n200 + ViT-L + transformer + weighted neighborhood in the remaining 4 experiments. This single-variable test from the current best is the most interpretable and budget-efficient next step.

The top three experiments (config_044: transformer+weighted=0.725, config_018: transformer+concat=0.721, config_042: avgpool+concat=0.715) all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, confirming this encoder pair as the strongest combination. The only untested cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for this pair is avgpool+weighted (config_040). Testing it completes the grid, clarifying whether the small gains from transformer aggregation (+0.005) and weighted fusion (+0.004) are independent or interacting, and establishes the ceiling of this configuration space. With 3 experiments remaining after this one, confirming the local optimum here (or finding a slight improvement) lets the final experiments be directed toward the next most promising unexplored axis (e.g., singleprofile) with full information about the multiprofile ceiling.

The multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l space is fully explored (best: config_044 at 0.7250 with transformer+weighted). The remaining key architectural question is whether singleprofile (no aggregation step) with the same top encoders and weighted fusion can be competitive or surpass the multiprofile pipeline. config_028 (singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted) directly tests this with the strongest encoder pair and the fusion strategy that showed a slight edge in the multiprofile space (weighted > concat). This is the highest-information untested configuration: if it matches or beats 0.7250, it opens a simpler architecture; if it falls well short, it confirms the multiprofile aggregation step is essential, and we can confidently exploit the known best (config_044) in the final experiments. With only 2 experiments left, resolving this architectural question is the best use of the next slot.

The top 4 experiments (config_044: 0.7250, config_018: 0.7207, config_042: 0.7150, config_040: 0.7062) all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile, and all four aggregation×fusion combinations have been tested. The clear winner is transformer+weighted (config_044). With only 1 experiment remaining after this one, I need to either find a marginal improvement or confirm the ceiling. Config_049 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is the closest untested variant to the best configuration—it preserves the best RNA encoder, best aggregation, best fusion, and multiprofile, swapping only the image encoder. This tests whether the transformer+weighted architecture's advantage is robust to the image backbone or strictly dependent on imagenet_vit_l. If it approaches 0.72, it suggests architectural choices matter more than the specific encoder, opening interpretation for the final experiment; if it drops significantly, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential and the search has effectively converged on config_044 as the best achievable within this design space.

The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 (RNA), multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and imagenet_vit_l (image) as the top-performing combination, with config_044 (vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 being the current best. The only untested configuration in this high-performing region is config_038 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat). While imagenet_vit_l generally edges out resnet50, config_049 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.713 accuracy with the best F1 (0.695) of all experiments, suggesting resnet50+transformer is competitive. Testing config_038 completes the 2×2 grid of (resnet50, transformer) × (concat, weighted) and clarifies whether concat fusion with transformer aggregation on resnet50 could match or exceed the weighted variant. As the final experiment, this is the best exploitation choice: it uses the two strongest settings (scvi_n200, transformer) and tests the last unexplored fusion variant in the top-performing design space, maximizing the chance of finding a configuration that rivals or exceeds 0.725.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment must establish a strong multimodal anchor to calibrate the search. config_021 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) combines a well-established RNA encoder (scvi_n200), a powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), the more informative multiprofile setting, an expressive transformer aggregation, and a simple/robust concat fusion. This tests the core hypothesis that multimodal fusion with strong per-modality encoders yields high accuracy, while keeping the fusion strategy simple to isolate encoder and aggregation contributions. It provides a high-quality reference point: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can exploit by swapping individual components (e.g., scgpt, weighted fusion); if it underperforms, we learn which component to simplify. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-experiment budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_021: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat → 72.1% acc), evidence is sparse. The most informative next step is a single-variable ablation from the current best to isolate the impact of one design choice. Config_039 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, keeping all other settings identical. This directly tests whether adaptive weighted combination of RNA and image features (vs. simple concatenation) improves accuracy, which is a fundamental multimodal design decision. If weighted fusion helps, it confirms that modality weighting matters and opens a productive exploitation direction (e.g., weighted fusion combined with other changes). If it doesn't, we confirm concat is sufficient and can redirect exploration toward RNA encoder or aggregation choices. Under the 8-experiment remaining budget, this clean comparison maximizes information gain per experiment.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_021, config_039) establish that multimodal + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer achieves ~72.1-72.5% accuracy, with weighted fusion marginally preferred over concat. However, the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) remains a major untested axis that could significantly shift performance. Question: config_007 tests scgpt as the RNA encoder while holding the other components at their best-known settings (imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile). This directly isolates the effect of a more specialized single-cell foundation model on the RNA side. If scgpt improves accuracy, it opens a promising sub-space (e.g., config_014, config_023); if not, we confirm scvi_n200 and pivot to image-encoder or aggregation variations. This single experiment reduces the largest remaining source of uncertainty in the design space.

The current best (config_039, acc=0.7250) uses transformer aggregation with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion. We have only tested transformer aggregation so far; the effect of aggregation method is an important untested design axis. config_004 is a clean ablation: it holds all other settings at their best-known values (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, weighted fusion) and swaps transformer for avgpool. This directly tests whether the more complex transformer aggregation is contributing meaningfully or whether a simpler pooling suffices. Under a 6-experiment remaining budget, resolving this architectural question is high-value: if avgpool matches transformer, it confirms a simpler direction to exploit; if it lags, it validates transformer and narrows the search space, freeing later experiments to focus on image encoder or profile setting.

Evidence: The best config so far (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. All four completed experiments used imagenet_vit_l, so the image encoder dimension is completely unexplored. The RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) showed a massive gap (~0.20 acc), indicating encoder architecture is a high-impact choice. Question: Does resnet50 as the image encoder perform comparably or better than imagenet_vit_l when all other parameters are held at their best-known values? Why this is the best next experiment: config_013 differs from config_039 only in image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l), giving a clean single-variable comparison on the most important untested design axis. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving whether the image encoder is a binding constraint (or flexible) is critical for guiding the remaining budget efficiently.

Evidence: The top-5 experiments all use multiprofile, with config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) leading at 0.7250 acc. scvi_n200 is clearly the best RNA encoder (0.72 vs 0.52 for scgpt), imagenet_vit_l edges out resnet50 on accuracy, transformer beats avgpool, and weighted slightly beats concat. However, the profile setting (multiprofile vs singleprofile) is a major architectural dimension that has been completely untested. Question: config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted) is a clean ablation of config_039 with only the profile setting changed, directly testing whether the multiprofile + transformer aggregation pipeline is essential or whether a simpler single-profile fusion can match or exceed it. Why this is the best next experiment: With 4 experiments remaining, resolving whether singleprofile is competitive is critical—if it is, it opens a new search axis; if not, we can confidently commit remaining budget to refining the multiprofile + transformer + weighted pipeline. It retains all the individually validated best components (top RNA encoder, top image encoder, best fusion) while probing the single largest untested design choice.

The evidence strongly identifies the optimal architecture as multimodal/multiprofile/transformer/weighted with imagenet_vit_l (config_039, acc 0.7250), and scvi_n200 clearly outperforms scgpt (0.72+ vs 0.52). However, pca_n2000 as an RNA encoder has never been tested in the multimodal setting, leaving an important uncertainty: whether a simpler linear representation could match or complement the learned scvi_n200 embedding when fused with the image modality. Config_029 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) isolates this single variable within the best-known architecture. If it underperforms scvi_n200 (likely), it confirms scvi_n200 is the right choice and we can confidently exploit the config_039 neighborhood in the remaining 3 experiments. If it performs comparably or better, it reveals a new direction. With only 3 experiments left, resolving this last major encoder uncertainty is the highest-value use of experiment 7 before committing the final budget to exploitation.

Evidence: The top-3 configurations all use scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with accuracy ranging 0.713–0.725. The current best (config_039: imagenet_vit_l, weighted) scores 0.725. Notably, config_013 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved the highest F1 (0.6945) despite lower accuracy, suggesting resnet50 captures complementary features. The only untested pairing of these proven-best components is resnet50 + concat fusion (config_001). This experiment tests whether the interaction between resnet50's feature space and concat fusion yields a synergistic gain over the current best. With only 2 experiments remaining after this, exploiting the strongest evidence (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) while filling the last gap in the 2×2 image-encoder × fusion grid is the highest-value use of this slot; if it underperforms, the remaining 2 experiments can confirm the ceiling or probe a different axis.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the best-performing region (config_039: 0.7250, config_021: 0.7207, config_004: 0.7062). The only untested configuration in this top region is config_017 (avgpool + concat), which completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid. While transformer+weighted is already the best, testing this remaining cell reduces residual uncertainty about whether the aggregation-fusion interaction could yield an unexpected result. Given that all other untested configs involve clearly inferior components (scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, or image/rna-only), config_017 is the highest-value use of experiment 9: it either confirms the current best (config_039) or, in a small-probability case, reveals a new best for the final experiment to build upon.

The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 + multiprofile + multimodal as the best-performing family, with config_039 (imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) at 0.7250 as the current best. The only remaining untested configuration within this top family is config_027 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted). While avgpool has underperformed transformer for scvi_n200 (config_004: 0.7062 vs config_039: 0.7250), and resnet50 has been slightly weaker than imagenet_vit_l in accuracy (config_013: 0.7131), the weighted fusion consistently helps and resnet50 showed the highest F1 (0.6945) in the set, suggesting complementary discriminative strength. As the final experiment, config_027 completes the scvi_n200 multimodal multiprofile grid, provides the last opportunity to potentially exceed 0.7250 within the most promising design space, and confirms whether the imagenet_vit_l + transformer combination is truly optimal or whether a different pairing could marginally improve performance. All other untested configs involve scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, or unimodal settings, all of which have shown substantially lower performance.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong reference point by testing the most complete multimodal configuration. config_039 combines all the most expressive components: multimodal fusion (leveraging both RNA and image), multiprofile (richer cellular representation), scgpt (learned context-aware RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (strong pretrained vision encoder), transformer aggregation (most flexible multi-profile combination), and weighted fusion (learned modality balancing). This tests whether the full pipeline yields high validation accuracy, giving me a strong baseline to compare against. In subsequent experiments, I can systematically ablate individual components (e.g., swap scgpt→pca, imagenet_vit_l→resnet50, transformer→avgpool, or drop to single-modality) to identify which design choices drive performance. Starting here maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-run budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_039: multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → acc 0.52), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually contributing meaningful signal over a single-modality baseline. Config_001 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) is the natural RNA-only counterpart that keeps the same RNA encoder and aggregation strategy, isolating the effect of the image modality. If RNA alone performs comparably (~0.50-0.52), the search can focus on refining the RNA pipeline or testing simpler image encoders; if it performs substantially worse, it confirms the value of multimodal fusion and justifies further exploration of fusion strategies and image encoders. This is the highest-information experiment at this stage because it partitions the 8 remaining experiments between two very different search strategies (optimize multimodal fusion vs. optimize single-modality model), and the answer is unlikely to be resolved by tweaking secondary knobs like fusion type or aggregation.

Evidence: The best multimodal config (config_039: scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves only 0.520 accuracy vs 0.514 for RNA-only, and notably has a worse F1 (0.479 vs 0.498), suggesting the weighted fusion may be diluting useful RNA signal with image noise. Question: config_009 is a single-variable ablation of config_039, changing only fusion from weighted to concat while keeping scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, and multiprofile fixed. This directly tests whether the fusion mechanism is the bottleneck preventing the image modality from contributing meaningfully. Why this is the best next experiment: With only 2 data points and a very small accuracy gap, the highest-priority uncertainty is whether the current multimodal pipeline can be made to clearly outperform the RNA-only baseline. Isolating the fusion choice (the most tunable hyperparameter in the fusion step) is the most information-dense single experiment. If concat improves accuracy and F1, it validates the multimodal direction and guides remaining budget toward concat-based variants; if it doesn't, it shifts focus to image encoder or RNA encoder choices.

Evidence: config_039 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is the best at 0.5200 acc, but we have only tested one RNA encoder (scgpt). The RNA encoder is a fundamental representation choice that could significantly impact downstream fusion quality. Question: Does scvi_n200 (a learned VAE-based representation) perform comparably to or better than scgpt when paired with the same imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted pipeline? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable ablation of the best configuration, directly reducing uncertainty about whether the scgpt encoder is specifically critical or whether any strong learned RNA representation works. With 6 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out the RNA encoder choice early will focus subsequent experiments on the remaining high-impact dimensions (image encoder, aggregation) rather than wasting budget on a suboptimal RNA representation.

The dominant finding is that swapping the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 (config_039→config_014) produced a massive ~20-point accuracy jump (0.520→0.725) while keeping imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion constant. This strongly implicates scvi_n200 as the key driver. The next logical exploitation step is to test whether the image encoder also matters: config_032 keeps the proven scvi_n200 + transformer + weighted stack but swaps imagenet_vit_l for resnet50. This single-variable change will clarify whether the 0.725 is robust to image encoder choice or whether imagenet_vit_l is specifically synergistic with scvi_n200. If resnet50 performs comparably, we gain flexibility for future experiments; if it degrades significantly, we confirm imagenet_vit_l is critical and should focus remaining budget on aggregation/fusion variants around the config_014 core. With 5 experiments left, this targeted test maximizes information gain while staying in the high-performing region.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_014, acc=0.725) is the best configuration by a wide margin over all scgpt-based runs (~0.52). The top performer is config_014 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy, with config_036 (same but concat fusion) at 0.7207 and config_032 (resnet50, weighted) at 0.7131. The best result so far is config_014 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. Evidence: scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation is the dominant high-performing combination (0.725, 0.721, 0.713 across tested image/fusion pairings). With no prior evidence (experiment 1 of 10), the goal is to establish a strong performance reference and reduce uncertainty about whether the most expressive architecture is near-optimal. Evidence: Only one experiment is complete (config_003: multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/weighted, acc≈0.52), leaving major uncertainty about whether the multimodal combination is actually outperforming a single-modality baseline. Question: How well does the image modality alone (imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool) perform? This directly isolates the contribution of the RNA branch. Evidence: config_003 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) achieved 0.52 accuracy, far above the image-only baseline (0.33), confirming multimodal fusion is essential. Evidence: config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 acc, dramatically outperforming config_003 (scgpt, same other settings) at 0.520, strongly establishing scvi_n200 as the superior RNA encoder. config_013 (image_only) at 0.332 confirms multimodal is essential. Uncertainty: within the best config, it is unclear whether the transformer aggregation over profiles is genuinely contributing to the 0.725 performance or whether a simpler avgpool would suffice. Evidence: config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) achieved the best accuracy at 0.725, and config_030 (same but avgpool) scored 0.706, confirming transformer aggregation is slightly better. The scvi_n200 RNA encoder is clearly superior to scgpt (0.725 vs 0.520). Question: Does concat fusion outperform weighted fusion when paired with the proven-best RNA encoder, image encoder, and transformer aggregation? This is the only untested dimension in the top-performing configuration. If concat improves on 0.725, it opens a new promising axis; if weighted is confirmed, we can confidently pivot to testing alternative image encoders (resnet50) or profile settings in subsequent runs, maximizing information gain per experiment.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the dominant RNA encoder (0.725 vs 0.520 for scgpt), and within scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile, transformer+weighted is the best combo (0.725). However, the image encoder dimension (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) remains completely untested with scvi_n200. It is the best use of this slot because it probes the largest unexplored architectural axis; if resnet50 is competitive, it opens alternative paths for the remaining 4 experiments, and if it underperforms, we can confidently lock in imagenet_vit_l and focus remaining budget on fine-grained fusion/aggregation or profile-setting variations.

The top-4 experiments all use scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, and scgpt performed poorly (0.520), but pca_n2000 has never been tested in the multimodal setting. If pca_n2000 approaches 0.72, it confirms the architecture is the key driver and opens up many more viable configurations for the remaining 3 experiments. With 3 experiments left, resolving this uncertainty about the most important design axis is the highest-value use of the next slot.

Evidence: The best result (0.725, config_007) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile. Evidence: config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is the best at 0.7250. The top performers all share scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation. The two remaining unexplored axes in this high-performing neighborhood are the image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) and fusion (concat vs weighted) in combination. config_031 showed resnet50 + transformer + weighted = 0.7131 (with notably higher F1 of 0.6945 than config_007's 0.6847), and config_036 showed imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat = 0.7207. The interaction of resnet50 with concat fusion (config_050) is untested and is the closest untested variant to the current best. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, this is the highest-expected-value test: it either finds a marginal improvement or definitively confirms config_007 as the search-space optimum, allowing the final experiment to be a targeted refinement.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile is clearly the dominant design space (config_007: 0.725, config_036: 0.721, config_030: 0.706). The 2x2 grid of aggregation (transformer/avgpool) × fusion (weighted/concat) for this encoder pair is nearly complete—only avgpool+concat remains untested. Question: Does the avgpool+concat combination for scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l yield a competitive result, or does it confirm that both transformer and weighted are individually necessary for peak performance? Why this is the best last experiment: It completes the critical ablation grid in the proven-best encoder space, uses the two strongest individual components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l), and is the only remaining multiprofile scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l config. While it is unlikely to surpass 0.725 given that both avgpool and concat are individually suboptimal, it is the highest-value remaining test for confirming the design landscape and cannot be beaten by any other untested configuration (all others use weaker encoders like scgpt or pca_n2000, or drop to singleprofile).

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong reference point in the most promising region of the design space. config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) represents the most complete multimodal architecture: it pairs the most advanced RNA encoder (scgpt, a generative pre-trained single-cell model) with the strongest image encoder (ViT-L), uses multiprofile with transformer aggregation to capture multi-view information, and applies weighted fusion. This tests the central hypothesis that a full multimodal pipeline outperforms simpler variants. If it performs well, it sets a high ceiling and I can ablate components in subsequent experiments. If it underperforms, it signals that one or more of the complex components (scgpt, ViT-L, transformer aggregation) may be suboptimal, guiding targeted simplification. As experiment 1 of 10, this maximizes information gain by anchoring the search in the highest-capability region before exploring trade-offs.

The sole data point (config_018: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.520) is a 'maximally complex' multimodal setup, leaving major uncertainty about which components actually drive performance. The RNA encoder is a high-impact design choice: scgpt is a learned generative encoder that may overfit or fail to capture discriminative features, while pca_n2000 is a simple linear projection. Evidence: config_004 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.586 acc / 0.574 F1, substantially outperforming config_018 (scgpt, same other settings) at 0.520 acc. Evidence: The RNA encoder is the most impactful variable tested so far — pca_n2000 (0.5988) vastly outperforms scgpt (0.5199) in the same multimodal/multiprofile/transformer setup, a ~8-point gap. Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder (0.713–0.725 accuracy), and config_040 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is the current best at 0.725. The current best is config_040 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc=0.725). The current best (config_040: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted = 0.725) is strongly supported by consistent evidence: scvi_n200 dominates other RNA encoders, imagenet_vit_l slightly edges resnet50, transformer beats avgpool, and weighted fusion slightly beats concat. The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_040, acc=0.7250) as the best configuration. While transformer has consistently outperformed avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706 for weighted), testing the concat fusion with avgpool completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the best encoder pair and rules out any interaction effect where concat might partially compensate for avgpool's weaker aggregation. As the final experiment with no remaining budget, this is the highest-expected-accuracy untested option in the primary multimodal design space and provides the most definitive characterization of whether the current best (config_040) is truly the ceiling for this encoder combination.

With no prior evidence, the highest-uncertainty question is whether a multimodal fusion of the two strongest encoders (scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for image) yields a meaningful accuracy gain over unimodal baselines. config_001 tests this in the simplest multimodal setup (singleprofile, concat fusion), establishing a strong reference point. With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, ViT-L, concat → 43.5% acc), evidence is very sparse and the baseline accuracy is low.
