This is the best next experiment because: (1) it directly extends the only data point we have, making results interpretable; (2) multiprofile+aggregation is a major design axis that could unlock significant gains; (3) with 8 experiments remaining, establishing whether this architectural upgrade helps early will guide whether to invest further in multiprofile variants or pivot toward encoder/fusion changes.

Evidence: config_006 (multiprofile, avgpool, concat, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l) achieved 0.5176 accuracy, substantially outperforming config_001 (singleprofile, no aggregation, same encoders) at 0.4348. If weighted fusion helps, it strengthens the base for subsequent experiments; if not, we rule out that direction and can pivot to aggregation or encoder changes.

The current best (config_013, acc=0.5420) uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted in a multiprofile setting. This is the highest-value experiment because the RNA modality likely carries the most discriminative signal for cell-type classification, and confirming or refuting scgpt's superiority narrows the search space for the remaining 5 experiments.

The dominant finding from 5 experiments is that scvi_n200 as RNA encoder (config_021, acc=0.706) vastly outperforms scgpt (~0.52-0.54), and avgpool+weighted fusion is the best aggregation/fusion combination tested. However, all scvi_n200 experiments so far use imagenet_vit_l; the image encoder dimension is completely unexplored for this strong RNA encoder. config_041 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable test that changes only the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 while keeping all other parameters at their best-known settings. This directly tests whether the image encoder is a bottleneck or whether imagenet_vit_l is already near-optimal. The strongest evidence points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion as the best combination (config_021: 0.706 acc). The only untested aggregation with this exact encoder/fusion pairing is transformer. With scgpt, avgpool and transformer were close (0.542 vs 0.520), but scvi_n200 produces richer latent representations where a transformer aggregator could better capture inter-profile interactions. With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, exploiting the strongest known direction while resolving the key remaining uncertainty (aggregation method with the best encoders) is the highest-value use of this slot.

The current best is config_024 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. Evidence consistently shows weighted > concat (scgpt+avgpool: 0.542 vs 0.518), but this comparison was made with avgpool aggregation. With transformer aggregation, the attention mechanism may already perform implicit feature weighting, potentially reducing the advantage of explicit weighted fusion. Config_044 is the only untested variant sharing three of four key parameters with the current best (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer), differing only in fusion (concat vs weighted). This is the most direct exploitation test: if concat+transformer is competitive, it could reveal an interaction effect; if not, it confirms config_024 as the local optimum and frees the final experiment for a different exploration direction. The current best is config_024 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725. The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 over scgpt, multiprofile over singleprofile, and transformer over avgpool aggregation. The remaining uncertainty is whether the image encoder choice interacts with transformer aggregation in a non-additive way: imagenet_vit_l has beaten resnet50 in avgpool settings (0.706 vs 0.678), but transformer aggregation changes the feature interaction dynamics. config_022 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is the closest untested variant to the best config, isolating only the image encoder. It is the best use of experiment 9 because it either confirms imagenet_vit_l's dominance (giving confidence to lock in the best config for the final experiment) or reveals a surprising interaction that could push accuracy above 0.725, directly informing the last remaining experiment.

Evidence: The top-performing region is clearly scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation, with config_024 (imagenet_vit_l, weighted) at 0.725 as the current best. config_022 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.713, and config_044 (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved 0.721. This experiment tests whether concat fusion with resnet50+transformer can match or exceed the weighted variant (config_022 at 0.713), and whether the small concat-vs-weighted gap seen with imagenet_vit_l (0.721 vs 0.725) holds for resnet50. As the final experiment, this is the best exploitation choice: it probes the last untested cell in the highest-performing configuration space, maximizing the chance of a small improvement over 0.725 while confirming the optimal architecture.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong baseline using the most promising combination of design choices to set a high reference point for the remaining 9 experiments. config_050 combines multimodal (both RNA and image), multiprofile (more data per cell), a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200), a powerful image backbone (imagenet_vit_l), transformer aggregation (most expressive for multi-profile integration), and concat fusion (simple, less prone to overfitting than learned weights). This 'all-strong-ingredients' configuration is the most likely to perform well, giving me a high bar to beat. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components (e.g., swap to scgpt, try weighted fusion, test singleprofile) to identify which dimensions matter most. If it underperforms, the result will immediately signal which component is the bottleneck, focusing exploration efficiently within the limited budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_050: multimodal/multiprofile/scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/concat at 72.1% acc), the evidence is sparse and we need to reduce uncertainty about which design choices are most impactful. Config_010 is a minimal, controlled change from config_050—only the fusion strategy shifts from concat to weighted—while keeping all other components identical. This directly tests whether weighted fusion can outperform simple concatenation for combining the transformer-aggregated RNA and image features. It is the best use of experiment 2 because it is low-risk (a small perturbation of the current best), provides a clean A/B comparison on one axis, and if weighted fusion improves accuracy, it opens a productive family of weighted-fusion configs to exploit in subsequent experiments; if it does not, we confirm concat is the right choice and can pivot to testing other axes (image encoder, aggregation, profile setting) with greater confidence.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_050, config_010) are nearly identical except for fusion (concat vs weighted), both using scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation, yielding ~0.72 accuracy. Weighted fusion is marginally better (0.7250 vs 0.7207). This gives us almost no information about whether the RNA encoder choice is a bottleneck. Question: config_038 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable swap of the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while keeping the best-performing fusion and aggregation. This tests whether a more biologically contextual RNA representation (scgpt) can push accuracy beyond the current ~0.72 plateau. Why this is the best next step: With only 2 data points and 7 experiments remaining, we must identify which axis (RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation) offers the largest headroom. The image encoder (ViT-L) is already a very strong pretrained model, making the RNA encoder the most likely source of improvement. A positive result opens a new high-performing direction; a negative result confirms scvi_n200 is optimal and lets us focus remaining budget on other axes.

Evidence: The best result so far (config_010, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, and scgpt is clearly inferior (config_038, acc=0.52). All three experiments used imagenet_vit_l, so the image encoder dimension remains unexplored. Question: Does resnet50 perform comparably to imagenet_vit_l when paired with the proven-best RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion? This is a single-variable change (image encoder only) from the current best config, making the result cleanly interpretable. Why now: With 6 experiments left, clarifying whether the image encoder is a critical bottleneck or interchangeable will determine whether future experiments should focus on aggregation/fusion refinements around imagenet_vit_l or explore a broader design space. This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact untested dimension given current evidence.

The current best (config_010: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, acc=0.7250) and all top-4 experiments use transformer aggregation, so we have no evidence about whether avgpool could match or exceed it. config_041 is a single-variable extension of the best config, swapping only transformer→avgpool while keeping the proven scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted combination. This directly tests whether the more complex transformer aggregation is necessary or whether a simpler pooling strategy could improve accuracy (perhaps by reducing overfitting or better preserving spatial information). With 5 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out avgpool as a viable aggregation for the top encoder pair is the highest-information next step: if it helps, it opens a new optimization axis; if not, we consolidate around transformer and focus remaining budget on other variables (e.g., PCA encoder, singleprofile).

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_010 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. scvi_n200 strongly outperforms scgpt (0.72+ vs 0.52), and imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted is the best-known combination for image encoder, aggregation, and fusion. However, pca_n2000 as an RNA encoder has not been tested in this optimal multimodal/multiprofile setting. Question: This experiment tests whether the simpler, non-generative pca_n2000 RNA encoder can match or exceed scvi_n200 when paired with the best image encoder, aggregation, and fusion. Why: With 4 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out the RNA encoder as a potential improvement axis is critical. If pca_n2000 matches scvi_n200, the RNA encoder is not the bottleneck and remaining budget should target other dimensions (e.g., profile setting). If it underperforms, scvi_n200 is confirmed optimal and we can exploit the remaining budget on the best known configuration neighborhood. This is a clean single-variable test in the highest-performing region, making it the most informative use of experiment 6.

Evidence: All 6 completed experiments used multiprofile with aggregation (transformer or avgpool). The best result (config_010, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. scvi_n200 is clearly the best RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l the best image encoder, transformer the best aggregation, and weighted the best fusion. However, the profile_setting dimension (singleprofile vs multiprofile) is completely untested. Question: config_003 tests whether a singleprofile architecture (no aggregation step) with the best-known encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) and best fusion (weighted) can match or exceed the multiprofile pipeline. This is the largest unexplored design axis. Rationale: With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, resolving whether the multiprofile+aggregation pipeline is actually necessary (vs. a simpler singleprofile approach) is the highest-information experiment. If singleprofile is competitive, it opens a new search direction; if not, it confirms we should exploit the multiprofile+transformer+weighted cluster in the final experiments. All other untested configs are small perturbations of already-explored settings unlikely to beat 0.7250.

The top-performing family is clearly scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with config_010 (vit_l, weighted) at 0.7250 and config_050 (vit_l, concat) at 0.7207. Config_020 (resnet50, weighted) scored 0.7131 accuracy but notably the highest F1 (0.6945), suggesting resnet50 captures complementary class-discriminative features. Config_007 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the only untested corner of the image_encoder × fusion 2×2 grid within this proven high-performing family. With only 2 experiments remaining, staying within the validated architecture is essential; this experiment tests whether the concat fusion (which slightly underperformed weighted with vit_l) might interact favorably with resnet50's feature space, potentially yielding a configuration that exceeds 0.7250. It is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step given the strong evidence for this architectural core.

Evidence: The top performer is config_010 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc 0.7250), with config_050 (same but concat fusion, 0.7207) close behind. All other variations (resnet50, avgpool, singleprofile, pca_n2000, scgpt) have consistently underperformed. The only untested combination retaining both best encoders (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) with multiprofile is config_016 (avgpool + concat). Question: Does the avgpool+concat pairing, while individually slightly inferior to transformer+weighted, produce a different (possibly complementary) feature interaction that could match or exceed 0.7250? Why this experiment: It is the closest untested configuration to the current best, maintaining the two proven-best encoders. If it fails to beat 0.7250, it confirms that transformer+weighted is the optimal aggregation/fusion pairing, giving high confidence in the final answer before the last experiment. If it succeeds, it identifies a new optimum. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, confirming the ceiling of the best-known architecture is the highest-value use of this slot.

The best accuracy found (0.725, config_010: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) has already been identified, and all four combinations of {transformer, avgpool} × {weighted, concat} with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l have been tested. The remaining untested scvi_n200 multimodal configs use resnet50, which has shown ~1-2% lower accuracy (config_020: 0.713 vs config_010: 0.725). Config_030 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) completes the 2×2 architecture grid for the resnet50 encoder, confirming that the transformer + weighted + imagenet_vit_l combination is the optimal architecture. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, it is the highest-expected-value remaining test: it uses the proven-best RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and the slightly-better weighted fusion, and provides a clean confirmation that no untested architecture variant can outperform the already-identified best configuration, solidifying the final result for this search.

With no prior evidence (experiment 1 of 10), the priority is to establish a strong performance baseline while reducing uncertainty about the overall architecture. I select config_044 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) because it combines the most expressive choices across all design dimensions: both modalities (multimodal), multiple profiles per cell (multiprofile), a learned foundation-model RNA encoder (scgpt), the strongest image backbone (ViT-L), the most flexible aggregation (transformer), and a learnable fusion (weighted). If this configuration performs well, it gives a high bar to beat and I can ablate individual components in subsequent experiments to identify which choices drive performance. If it underperforms, it reveals that the combination of all 'maximal' choices is suboptimal, redirecting exploration toward simpler or alternative encoders/aggregations. This single experiment simultaneously tests the core hypothesis that multimodal + multiprofile + learned encoders + transformer aggregation is a strong regime, maximizing information gain per experiment under the tight 10-experiment budget.

The first experiment (config_044: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieved ~52% accuracy, which is modest. The most immediate uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation is actually contributing positively or introducing overfitting/instability relative to a simpler pooling strategy. Config_004 is a clean single-variable ablation (transformer → avgpool) holding all other settings identical (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion). If avgpool matches or exceeds the transformer result, it signals that the added complexity of transformer aggregation is not warranted and frees capacity to focus on other dimensions (fusion strategy, encoder choice). If the transformer clearly wins, it confirms that learned cross-profile attention is important and justifies keeping it in subsequent experiments. With 8 experiments remaining, resolving this architectural question early prevents wasting budget on variants built on a suboptimal aggregation backbone.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_044 and config_004) show that avgpool aggregation (0.542) outperforms transformer (0.520) when paired with scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion in a multimodal multiprofile setup. However, the RNA encoder dimension is completely unexplored—only scgpt has been tested. Question: config_047 tests scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder while holding all other settings at their current best-known values (multimodal, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted). This is a clean single-variable ablation that will reveal whether a different RNA representation (variational autoencoder-based, 200-dim) can improve upon scgpt. Why this is the best next experiment: The RNA encoder is a fundamental architectural choice that likely has a large impact on performance. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether scgpt is optimal or whether scvi_n200 offers gains is the highest-information experiment. If scvi_n200 matches or beats scgpt, it opens a new promising direction; if it underperforms, it confirms scgpt as the right encoder and lets us focus budget on other variables (image encoder, fusion, profile setting).

Evidence: config_047 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) achieved 0.706 accuracy, a dramatic jump over scgpt-based configs (~0.52-0.54), strongly indicating scvi_n200 is the superior RNA encoder. The only other variable tested within the scgpt+imagenet_vit_l+weighted family was aggregation (avgpool 0.542 vs transformer 0.520), a small difference. Question: Does transformer aggregation improve or degrade performance when paired with the much stronger scvi_n200 encoder? config_009 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is a single-variable change from the best config, directly testing whether the more expressive transformer aggregation can further boost accuracy or whether avgpool remains optimal. This is the best use of experiment 4 because it exploits the clearly promising scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l direction while reducing uncertainty about the aggregation choice with minimal confounding, leaving 6 experiments to explore fusion method, image encoder, and other refinements.

The evidence strongly points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the dominant configuration (0.706–0.725 acc vs 0.52–0.54 for scgpt). Within this strong family, transformer aggregation slightly edges out avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706), and weighted fusion is the current best. The key remaining uncertainty is whether concat fusion could outperform weighted fusion under the transformer aggregation. config_021 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) directly tests this. If concat matches or beats weighted, it opens additional combinations; if weighted holds, we confirm the fusion choice and can pivot to other dimensions (e.g., image encoder or profile setting) in the remaining 5 experiments. This is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step given the strong signal already established.

Evidence: scvi_n200 as RNA encoder dramatically outperforms scgpt (~0.72 vs ~0.53), and transformer+weighted is the best aggregation/fusion combo (0.725). However, all 5 experiments used imagenet_vit_l; the image encoder dimension is completely untested. Question: Does swapping to resnet50 with the proven scvi_n200+transformer+weighted stack improve or degrade performance? This is the largest untested design axis. Rationale: With only 4 experiments left, testing the image encoder is the highest-information experiment—if resnet50 is competitive, it opens a new direction; if it underperforms, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is critical and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning aggregation/fusion or profile settings. config_024 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) isolates the image encoder change while holding all other parameters at their known-best values.

The current best is config_009 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725). The evidence clearly shows scvi_n200 >> scgpt (~0.20 gap), transformer > avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706), and weighted ≈ concat (0.725 vs 0.721). Config_046 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the only untested combination in this best-performing subspace. With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, confirming the optimal configuration within the most promising subspace is the highest-value use of this slot—it reduces residual uncertainty before the final experiments and ensures the best configuration is correctly identified.

The current best (config_009, 0.725 acc) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. All multiprofile variants around this core have been explored (transformer/avgpool × weighted/concat), yielding a narrow 0.706–0.725 band. The singleprofile setting has not been tested at all, leaving an important design uncertainty: whether the aggregation step (transformer/avgpool) is genuinely adding signal or introducing noise that a direct weighted fusion of single-profile features could avoid. config_038 keeps the proven best RNA encoder (scvi_n200), best image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and best fusion (weighted) while removing aggregation, directly testing this question. With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information choice: if singleprofile matches or exceeds 0.725, the remaining budget can exploit a new design axis; if it falls short, it confirms the current best and validates the multiprofile+aggregation architecture, allowing the final experiments to focus on fine-grained perturbations of the known optimum.

The current best is config_009 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. All four aggregation×fusion combinations for scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l+multiprofile have been tested, and resnet50 variants are consistently ~1% lower. The major untested dimension is pca_n2000 in multiprofile mode with the best aggregation/fusion settings. This is the highest-information experiment remaining: it reduces uncertainty about the most impactful unexplored design choice before the final experiment.

The best accuracy so far is config_009 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725. All top performers use scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation. The one untested resnet50 variant (config_024: transformer+weighted) achieved the highest F1 (0.6945) of all experiments, suggesting resnet50+transformer has strong discriminative capacity. Config_028 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) tests whether concat fusion—competitive with weighted in the imagenet_vit_l setting (0.721 vs 0.725)—might complement resnet50's features differently. As the final experiment, this is the highest-expected-value remaining option among scvi_n200 multiprofile configurations, as it explores the only untested fusion×image-encoder pairing within the proven top-performing architecture family.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong multimodal baseline using the highest-capacity choices across all design dimensions: scgpt (pretrained single-cell foundation model) for RNA, imagenet_vit_l (largest image encoder) for images, transformer aggregation (most expressive for multiprofile), and weighted fusion (most flexible modality combining). This tests whether the full multimodal pipeline can achieve strong validation accuracy and provides a ceiling reference. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components (encoder, aggregation, fusion) to identify what drives performance. If it underperforms, it signals that complexity is a bottleneck and simpler alternatives (e.g., resnet50, avgpool, concat) should be explored. Evidence: Our only completed experiment (config_015) achieved ~52% accuracy with multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/weighted. This clean A/B test maximizes information gain per experiment under our tight budget.

Evidence: config_015 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.520 accuracy, and config_012 (same but resnet50) achieved 0.494, confirming that imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile is the strongest architecture so far. Uncertainty: we have only tested scgpt as the RNA encoder; scvi_n200 (a variational autoencoder) encodes RNA very differently and may capture complementary or superior biological signal. This experiment (config_026: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multimodal, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable swap against our current best, isolating the RNA encoder effect. It is the best use of experiment 3 because the RNA encoder is the highest-leverage untested design choice within the already-validated architecture, and resolving it early (with 7 experiments left) lets us commit the remaining budget to refining the winning combination rather than exploring a suboptimal RNA encoder.

Evidence: config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 accuracy, far surpassing scgpt-based configs (~0.50-0.52), establishing scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the strongest combination. Uncertainty: whether weighted fusion or concat fusion better leverages the strong scvi_n200 representations when combined with transformer aggregation. This experiment (config_016) tests concat fusion while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values, isolating the fusion mechanism as the single variable. It is the best next step because it is a minimal, clean ablation on the top-performing config—exploiting the strong evidence for scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer while resolving a key architectural uncertainty that could push accuracy above 0.725 in the remaining 6 experiments.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_026, acc=0.7250) is the best configuration, with concat fusion (config_016, acc=0.7207) nearly matching it. The only aggregation tested with this top encoder pair is 'transformer'. Config_047 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates the aggregation method while holding the best-known encoders and fusion fixed. This tells us whether the transformer aggregation is a critical contributor or whether a simpler avgpool suffices—reducing uncertainty about a key architectural dimension. Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the dominant RNA encoder (0.725 vs 0.520 for scgpt), and the current best (config_026: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) uses a large ViT image encoder. However, the image encoder gap was modest with scgpt (0.520 vs 0.494, only ~2.6 pts), so its contribution in the scvi_n200 regime is uncertain. This experiment (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) tests whether the smaller resnet50 image encoder is competitive when paired with the strong scvi_n200 RNA encoder. If resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the RNA encoder is the primary driver and we can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., singleprofile vs multiprofile, PCA). If it drops significantly, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential and we should lock in the current best architecture. This is the best use of experiment 6 because it directly reduces uncertainty about the second most important design variable in the context of the proven best RNA encoder, and it is a logical exploitation of the current leading direction before spending remaining budget on more speculative changes.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_026, acc=0.725) is the clear best, and all completed experiments use multiprofile. The singleprofile setting is completely unexplored, creating significant uncertainty about whether the multiprofile+transformer architecture is actually necessary or if a simpler single-profile model with the same encoders could match or exceed it. This experiment (config_017: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted) directly tests that hypothesis using the best-validated RNA and image encoders. It is the best use of this slot because: (1) it reduces uncertainty on a major untested architectural dimension, (2) if it performs comparably, it confirms a simpler viable path for remaining experiments, and (3) if it underperforms significantly, it confirms the multiprofile+transformer design is essential, allowing the final 3 experiments to focus purely on exploiting the multiprofile space (e.g., testing pca_n2000 as RNA encoder or fine-tuning fusion). No other untested configuration offers as much information per experiment under the remaining budget.

The current best (config_026: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile, acc=0.7250) has been identified, and all remaining scvi_n200 multimodal-multiprofile variants involve known-negative changes (avgpool, concat, resnet50, singleprofile) unlikely to exceed it. The key remaining uncertainty is whether pca_n2000, the only untested RNA encoder in the optimal multimodal-multiprofile setting, could be competitive. config_029 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) is a clean single-factor swap from config_026, directly testing whether the learned scvi representation is truly necessary or whether a linear PCA projection suffices. Given only 2 experiments remain, this is the highest-information experiment: if pca_n2000 is competitive (~0.70+), it reveals an alternative design axis for the final experiments; if it is substantially worse (as scgpt was at 0.52), it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and the current best is near-optimal, allowing the last two experiments to focus on fine-grained fusion/aggregation tweaks around the known optimum.

Evidence: config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the clear best at 0.7250, with config_016 (same but concat) at 0.7207 and config_010 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.7131. The top-performing region is firmly scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer. Question: config_032 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the last untested cell in the 2×2 image_encoder×fusion grid under transformer aggregation with scvi_n200. Testing it completes the picture of whether any transformer-aggregation variant could edge out config_026, or confirms it as the ceiling. Why this is best: With only 1 experiment remaining after this one, I need to either (a) discover a configuration that beats 0.7250 to guide the final experiment, or (b) confirm config_026 is optimal so the last experiment can be spent on a different exploratory axis. config_032 is the highest-information test within the proven high-performing region—any unexpected result would redirect the final experiment, while a confirmed lower result locks in config_026 as the answer and frees the last slot for broader exploration.

Evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the top-performing family (config_026: 0.7250, config_016: 0.7207, config_047: 0.7062). The 2x2 design over aggregation (transformer/avgpool) × fusion (weighted/concat) for this encoder pair is now fully tested except for avgpool+concat. With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong baseline for the full multimodal pipeline. config_020 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) combines the most expressive choices across all dimensions: a learned biological latent (scvi_n200), a strong pretrained vision backbone (imagenet_vit_l), the most flexible aggregation (transformer), and a learned fusion (weighted). With only one completed experiment (config_020: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → acc 0.725), the most critical uncertainty is whether the RNA modality actually contributes meaningful signal over the image alone. Evidence: config_020 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is the best at 0.725 acc, while config_045 (same but scgpt) drops to 0.520, confirming scvi_n200 is critical. config_004 (image_only) at 0.260 confirms multimodal fusion is essential. The best result so far (config_020, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted fusion. Evidence: config_020 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the clear best at 0.725 acc, with scvi_n200 strongly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.586) and scgpt (0.520), transformer beating avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706), and weighted ≈ concat (0.725 vs 0.721). Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder (0.725, 0.721, 0.713, 0.706 across configs), transformer is the best aggregation (0.725 vs 0.706 for avgpool), and the current best is config_020 (vit_l + weighted, acc 0.725). The current best is config_020 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether a multimodal fusion architecture with a learned RNA encoder can establish a strong performance baseline. This balances exploration of the most promising architectural hypothesis with practical robustness.

With only one completed experiment (config_002: multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/resnet50/transformer/weighted at 49.4% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually adding value over a single-modality baseline. config_001 (image_only, multiprofile, resnet50, transformer) is the cleanest ablation of config_002—it holds image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation identical, removing only the RNA branch. If image-only accuracy is close to 49.4%, RNA is not contributing and I should focus on image-side improvements; if it is substantially lower, the RNA signal is valuable and I should explore better RNA encoders and fusion strategies; if it is substantially higher, the RNA branch is hurting and I should pivot. Establishing this single-modality baseline is the highest-leverage uncertainty reduction with 8 experiments remaining, as it determines whether to invest in multimodal refinement or single-modality optimization for the rest of the budget.

Evidence: config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.494 acc, far exceeding image_only config_001 (0.224 acc), confirming multimodal fusion with scgpt is the strongest direction. Evidence: config_013 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) is the best result so far at 0.520 acc / 0.479 F1, outperforming config_002 (same but resnet50) at 0.494. Evidence: The current best is config_013 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.520), and image-only (config_001, acc=0.224) confirms RNA modality is critical. Question: Does a simpler, linear RNA representation (pca_n2000) perform comparably or differently when paired with the best image encoder and aggregation/fusion settings? This isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding all other parameters at their empirically best values (ViT-L, transformer, weighted, multiprofile). If PCA matches scGPT, it frees future experiments to explore other dimensions; if it lags, it confirms scGPT's importance and we can focus remaining budget on aggregation/fusion refinements with scGPT.

The best result so far is config_047 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.586). All completed multimodal experiments used transformer aggregation, so we have no evidence about whether a simpler aggregation (avgpool) could match or exceed it, especially with the simpler linear PCA representation. Config_041 isolates the aggregation variable (transformer→avgpool) while keeping the top-performing RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and fusion (weighted) fixed. This is the highest-value exploitation step: if avgpool performs comparably, we confirm the design is robust; if it underperforms, we confirm transformer is essential and can focus remaining budget on other axes. With 4 experiments left, reducing uncertainty on this untested structural choice is more informative than the smaller fusion variation (weighted vs concat) where we already have directional evidence.

The current best (config_041: pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.635) establishes that a simple PCA RNA encoder combined with a strong image encoder and avgpool aggregation is highly effective. The most impactful remaining design question is whether a learned RNA representation (scvi_n200) can outperform PCA in this same setting. config_049 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, and weighted fusion fixed, directly testing whether a biologically informed learned embedding adds value over the linear PCA baseline. This is the best use of the next slot because it (1) exploits the strongest configuration found so far, (2) reduces uncertainty on the RNA encoder axis—a major source of variance across experiments—and (3) if it improves, opens a new exploitation path for the remaining 3 experiments; if it does not, it confirms pca_n2000 as optimal and lets us focus remaining budget on fusion or other micro-variations around the known best.

The current best (config_049: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) achieves 0.706 accuracy. The evidence shows avgpool > transformer for pca_n2000 (0.635 vs 0.586), but scvi_n200 is a learned nonlinear representation that may interact differently with aggregation. config_050 tests whether transformer aggregation can outperform avgpool specifically with scvi_n200, keeping all other best-known settings (imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion, multiprofile). The current best (config_050: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) has been built up through clear evidence that scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 > scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l >> resnet50 for image, transformer > avgpool for aggregation, and weighted > concat for fusion. Config_048 is the only untested configuration sharing 4 of 5 key parameters with the current best (differing only in fusion: concat vs weighted). No other available configuration combines the proven-best RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation, making config_048 the highest-probability candidate to match or exceed the current best and the most informative use of this slot.

While it is unlikely to surpass config_050 given the observed ordering, it is the most principled final experiment: it exploits the strongest evidence (best encoders, multiprofile) while closing the last gap in the design space for the winning family. No other untested configuration (singleprofile variants, resnet50-based, or weaker RNA encoders) has a credible path to exceeding 0.725 based on the observed performance hierarchy.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong reference point for the core multimodal hypothesis. config_002 pairs the most expressive encoders in each modality (scgpt for RNA, ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L for images) with transformer-based aggregation (more expressive than avgpool for combining multiprofile outputs) and standard concat fusion. If it underperforms, it signals that complexity in one or more components is the bottleneck, guiding targeted follow-ups. This is the highest-information single experiment under a 10-run budget because it simultaneously validates the multimodal architecture, the encoder choices, and the aggregation strategy.

With only one data point (config_002: multimodal, scgpt+ViT-L, transformer+concat → acc 0.507, F1 0.455), the most critical uncertainty is whether multimodality is actually contributing value or whether a single modality can achieve comparable performance. Evidence: config_002 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) achieved 0.507 accuracy, far exceeding image-only config_014 (0.332), confirming multimodal fusion is essential. Evidence: The two best experiments (config_008: 0.725, config_019: 0.721) both use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation, with only a marginal difference between weighted and concat fusion. Why this is the best use: With 5 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out the image encoder as a performance lever is critical—if resnet50 matches or beats ViT-L, we gain flexibility for later fine-tuning; if it underperforms, we lock in imagenet_vit_l and can focus remaining budget on subtler hyperparameters (aggregation, fusion, profile setting).

The current best (config_008, 0.725 acc) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The best result so far is config_008 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725). With no prior experiments, there is no evidence to exploit, so the goal is to establish a strong multimodal baseline that reduces uncertainty about whether the full pipeline (learned RNA encoder + strong image encoder + expressive aggregation) is viable. config_005 combines the most powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), a learned RNA representation (scgpt), the most expressive aggregation (transformer), multiprofile (richer cellular information), and simple concat fusion (fewer hyperparameters to fail). With only one data point (config_005: multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/concat at 0.507 acc), the most fundamental uncertainty is whether the multimodal architecture is actually necessary or whether a single modality could be competitive. config_014 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) directly tests the contribution of the image modality while holding the RNA encoder (scgpt) and aggregation (transformer) constant. Evidence: config_045 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 accuracy, a massive jump over all scgpt-based configs (~0.50-0.52), strongly implicating the scvi_n200 RNA encoder as the critical factor. Evidence: The top-4 configs all use scvi_n200 + transformer + multiprofile, with imagenet_vit_l+weighted (config_045, acc=0.725) as the current best. However, config_047 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) achieved the highest F1 (0.695), suggesting resnet50 may pair well with certain fusion strategies.
