Testing it clarifies whether concat fusion rescues or improves upon resnet50's accuracy gap (0.713 vs 0.725), and whether the F1 advantage of resnet50 translates into an accuracy gain with a different fusion. This is the highest-value exploitation step: it completes the key comparison within the proven-best neighborhood, and with 4 experiments remaining, narrowing the optimal image-encoder/fusion pairing is essential before any fine-tuning.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. We've established that transformer aggregation + weighted fusion + imagenet_vit_l is the strongest architecture, and scvi_n200 >> scgpt as RNA encoder. The one untested RNA encoder in this proven architecture is pca_n2000. This experiment tests whether pca_n2000 can match or exceed scvi_n200 within the best-known architecture (transformer + weighted + imagenet_vit_l). It is the best use of this slot because it stays in the high-performing region (low risk of a large drop), reduces uncertainty about the RNA encoder choice, and if pca_n2000 performs comparably it opens flexibility for the remaining 3 experiments, while if it underperforms it firmly confirms scvi_n200 as the optimal encoder so remaining budget can focus on other refinements.

Evidence: The top-4 experiments all use scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation, with config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) leading at 0.725 accuracy. All tested configs use multiprofile, meaning the aggregation step is always present. Question: Does the singleprofile architecture (which removes the aggregation step entirely) with the best-known encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) and weighted fusion outperform or match the multiprofile pipeline? This is the most important untested architectural axis. Why this experiment: With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, I need to resolve uncertainty about a fundamental design choice (singleprofile vs multiprofile) using the strongest encoder combination. If config_020 performs comparably or better, it opens a new direction for the final experiment; if it underperforms, it confirms multiprofile is optimal and the remaining budget can be spent on minor refinements around the current best.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. All four scvi_n200+transformer+multiprofile combinations have been tested, confirming transformer aggregation provides a ~2% boost over avgpool and weighted fusion slightly outperforms concat. The remaining untested multimodal multiprofile configurations are dominated by scgpt or pca_n2000 RNA encoders, both of which showed substantially lower performance (0.542 and 0.586 respectively). Question: config_023 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) tests whether the transformer aggregation benefit generalizes across RNA encoders—i.e., whether scgpt's poor performance with avgpool (0.542) is partly due to the aggregation method rather than the encoder itself. Why this is the best use: Among all remaining untested configurations, config_023 has the highest potential ceiling (best image encoder + best aggregation method) and directly addresses the key architectural uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation is encoder-agnostic. While unlikely to surpass 0.725 given scgpt's large gap, it provides the most scientifically informative result with the final two experiments remaining, and no other untested configuration offers a more plausible path to improvement.

The best result so far is config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. Strong evidence across 9 experiments shows scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder, multiprofile far outperforms singleprofile, and transformer aggregation exceeds avgpool. The remaining untested scvi_n200/multiprofile/imagenet_vit_l configuration is config_015 (avgpool, concat), which is the closest untested variant to the best-performing setup. While transformer+weighted is clearly superior, testing avgpool+concat completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the top encoder pair, reducing residual uncertainty about whether any interaction between aggregation and fusion could shift performance. As the final experiment, this is the highest-expected-accuracy untested option and the most informative completion of the design space around the current best.

With no prior evidence, the most informative first experiment is to test the 'full-featured' multimodal hypothesis: combining RNA (scvi_n200, a learned deep representation) and image (imagenet_vit_l, the strongest available encoder) modalities with multiprofile data, transformer aggregation (most flexible for capturing cell-cell interactions), and weighted fusion (learned modality importance). This configuration sits at the intersection of the most promising choices across all design dimensions. If it performs well, it establishes a strong upper-bound reference and subsequent experiments can ablate individual components (encoder choice, aggregation, fusion) to identify what drives performance. If it underperforms, it signals that complexity or a specific component is the bottleneck, guiding simplification in later experiments. Testing this 'best-guess' configuration first maximizes information gain per experiment under the tight 10-experiment budget, as it simultaneously validates the multimodal approach, the multiprofile setting, and the most powerful encoders/architecture in a single data point.

With only one completed experiment (config_006: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → acc 0.725), evidence is extremely sparse. The most informative next step is a clean single-variable ablation to determine whether the fusion strategy (weighted vs. concat) is a meaningful design choice. Config_021 changes only the fusion from weighted to concat while holding all other settings identical to config_006. If concat outperforms weighted, it reveals that the interaction between modalities benefits from a richer (higher-dimensional) combination, guiding future experiments toward concat-based fusion. If weighted remains better or they are comparable, it tells us fusion strategy is not a major lever and we should prioritize encoder choices (RNA encoder, image encoder) in subsequent experiments. Under the limited budget of 8 remaining experiments, this minimal-change test maximizes information gain per experiment by isolating one critical design dimension without confounding other variables.

The two completed experiments (config_006 and config_021) establish that the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted/concat multimodal multiprofile setup achieves ~0.72-0.725 accuracy, with weighted fusion marginally better. The largest untested dimension is the RNA encoder: scgpt is a fundamentally different learned representation (generative) compared to scvi (variational), and could capture different biological structure. Config_028 changes only the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while holding all other variables (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) constant, making it a clean single-variable ablation. This is the best use of experiment 3 because it reduces uncertainty about whether the RNA encoder is a bottleneck or whether scvi_n200 is already near-optimal, and the result will strongly inform whether to invest remaining budget in scgpt-based or scvi-based configurations.

Evidence: config_006 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is the current best at 0.7250, and scvi_n200 is clearly superior to scgpt (0.725 vs 0.520). Weighted fusion edges out concat (0.725 vs 0.721). The largest untested architectural variable is the image encoder: all three completed experiments used imagenet_vit_l, so we have no evidence whether resnet50 might be competitive or superior. Question: config_038 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) is a clean single-variable A/B test against config_006, changing only the image encoder. This directly clarifies whether the larger ViT-L backbone is necessary or whether a lighter ResNet50 could match/exceed it, which would reshape the remaining 6-experiment search space. Rationale: With 6 experiments left, resolving the image encoder question now is the highest-information experiment—it either confirms imagenet_vit_l (letting us focus on aggregation/profile refinements) or reveals resnet50 as a better base (opening a new promising branch to exploit).

The best config so far (config_006: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) uses transformer aggregation, but we have no evidence yet on whether avgpool aggregation could match or exceed it. config_046 is a clean single-variable change (transformer→avgpool) from the current best, directly testing whether the more complex transformer aggregation is necessary or whether a simpler pooling strategy performs comparably. This is the best use of experiment 5 because: (1) it reduces uncertainty about an important architectural choice with minimal confounding, (2) if avgpool is competitive, it opens a broader set of configurations for the remaining 5 experiments, and (3) if transformer is clearly superior, we can confidently lock in that choice and focus remaining budget on other dimensions (e.g., profile setting, fusion strategy, or encoder alternatives like pca_n2000).

Evidence: All 5 completed experiments used multiprofile with transformer aggregation. scvi_n200 is clearly the best RNA encoder (0.71-0.72 vs scgpt's 0.52), imagenet_vit_l is the best image encoder (0.725 vs resnet50's 0.713), and weighted fusion slightly outperforms concat (0.725 vs 0.721). The single most important unexplored dimension is profile_setting (singleprofile vs multiprofile). This experiment (config_013: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted) tests whether removing the multiprofile/transformer aggregation step and using a single profile with the best-known encoders and fusion can match or exceed the current best (0.725). It is the best use of the next slot because it reduces uncertainty on the one major architectural axis not yet tested, uses all components with strong positive evidence, and with 4 experiments remaining after this one, confirming or ruling out singleprofile early will focus the remaining budget on the winning branch.

The best configuration so far is config_006 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). All major design axes have been explored in this pipeline except the RNA encoder alternative pca_n2000. We know scgpt is far inferior (0.52 vs 0.725), but pca_n2000 remains untested in the top pipeline. Config_042 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates this single variable change, directly testing whether a simpler linear projection can match or exceed the learned VAE representation. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve: if pca_n2000 performs comparably, it confirms the pipeline is robust to encoder choice and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and we lock in config_006's architecture for the final experiments. With only 3 experiments remaining, reducing uncertainty on the one untested core variable is the most efficient use of the next slot.

The current best is config_006 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc 0.7250). Evidence shows scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer is the strongest backbone, but the image encoder and fusion strategy still have unresolved trade-offs: resnet50 achieved lower accuracy (0.7131) yet notably higher F1 (0.6945 vs 0.6847) than imagenet_vit_l, suggesting it captures complementary features that a different fusion strategy might exploit. config_011 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the only untested combination that pairs the F1-strong resnet50 encoder with concat fusion while retaining the proven transformer aggregation. This tests whether the resnet50–RNA interaction benefits from a different fusion mechanism, potentially unlocking an accuracy gain over the current best. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, testing this high-potential variant is the best balance of exploiting the known strong backbone and exploring the one remaining untested pairing within it.

Evidence: The top configuration (config_006: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) and its three nearest variants have been tested (transformer+concat=0.721, avgpool+weighted=0.706). The 2×2 grid of aggregation×fusion for the best encoder pair is incomplete—only avgpool+concat (config_045) remains. Question: This tests whether the avgpool+concat combination, while expected to underperform transformer+weighted, might interact differently with the scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l pair to produce an unexpected result. Why this is the best use: With only 1 experiment remaining after this one, the search has essentially converged on the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile region. Completing this 2×2 grid is the most informative remaining experiment for the top configuration, ruling out any residual uncertainty about whether a different aggregation/fusion pairing could marginally improve on 0.725. All other untested configurations involve clearly inferior choices (scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, or single-modality) that the evidence strongly argues against.

Evidence: All top-performing configs (0.69–0.73 acc) use scvi_n200 + multiprofile, with transformer aggregation and weighted/concat fusion being the strongest. The current best is config_006 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.7250). The only remaining untested configurations in this high-performing family are config_040 and config_051 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool). Question: This tests whether the avgpool + resnet50 combination, paired with the best RNA encoder and weighted fusion, can approach or exceed the current best, and completes the full 2×2×2 grid for scvi_n200 + multiprofile. Why this is the best final experiment: Among all untested configs, config_051 retains the three strongest individual choices (scvi_n200, multiprofile, weighted fusion) and is the most likely remaining candidate to produce a competitive result. It also provides a clean ablation comparing resnet50+avgpool against imagenet_vit_l+avgpool (config_046, 0.7062) to isolate the image encoder's contribution under avgpool, which is valuable for the final report. All other untested configs (singleprofile, scgpt, pca_n2000, rna_only, image_only) show strong evidence of underperformance and are very unlikely to beat 0.7250.

With no prior evidence, the priority is to establish a strong multimodal baseline that tests the core hypothesis (does combining RNA + image modalities help?) while using well-established, low-risk components. config_001 pairs the strongest image encoder (ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L) with a simple, reliable RNA encoder (PCA-2000), standard avgpool aggregation, and straightforward concat fusion. This gives a high-probability-decent baseline: if it performs well, I can exploit by swapping in learned encoders (scGPT/scVI) or better fusion; if it underperforms, I can diagnose whether the bottleneck is the image encoder, RNA representation, or fusion strategy. Choosing this over a unimodal baseline (e.g., config_003) is justified because the study's goal is multimodal profiling, and a strong multimodal starting point lets me use subsequent experiments to ablate and improve rather than first confirming the obvious unimodal ceiling.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat → 0.6287 acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion actually adds value over a strong single-modality baseline. config_009 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool) is the cleanest ablation of config_001—it uses the same image encoder (ViT-L), same aggregation (avgpool), and same profile setting (multiprofile), differing only in the removal of the RNA branch. If image-only accuracy is close to 0.6287, the RNA signal contributes little and I should redirect budget toward image-centric or different-fusion strategies. If it is substantially lower, multimodal fusion is confirmed as the right direction and I can exploit that in subsequent experiments. This single comparison resolves the highest-impact design question early, making the best use of experiment 2 under a 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.629 acc, while image-only (config_009) is only 0.332, confirming RNA is critical. The single biggest untested lever is the RNA encoder: pca_n2000 is a linear projection that may discard nonlinear biological structure. Question: Does replacing pca_n2000 with the learned scgpt encoder (config_050) improve accuracy while keeping all other hyperparameters identical (imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, multiprofile)? This is the most controlled single-variable test of the highest-impact design choice. Why best use of experiment 3: With 7 experiments left, isolating the RNA encoder effect early will determine whether subsequent experiments should prioritize scgpt/scvi_n200 variants or focus on aggregation/fusion improvements, reducing uncertainty about the most important architectural axis.

Evidence: config_001 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat + multiprofile) is the best at 0.629 acc, and the image-only baseline (config_009, 0.332) is far weaker than the RNA signal, suggesting the fusion strategy is critical for balancing a strong RNA modality with a weaker image modality. Question: Does weighted fusion (config_020) outperform simple concat when combining these asymmetric modalities, allowing the model to learn optimal modality weights? Why this is the best next step: It is a single-variable change from the current best configuration, making the result cleanly interpretable. If weighted fusion improves accuracy, it validates a direction that can be combined with other untested dimensions (transformer aggregation, scvi_n200) in remaining experiments. If it does not, we confirm concat is sufficient and can pivot to testing aggregation or profile-setting changes, efficiently narrowing the search space with 6 experiments still available.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_020 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6352 acc / 0.6183 F1. PCA-based RNA encoding clearly outperforms scgpt (0.6287 vs 0.5176), multimodal far exceeds image-only (0.63 vs 0.33), and weighted fusion shows a modest edge over concat. Uncertainty: We have only tested avgpool aggregation with this top-performing RNA+image encoder pair; transformer aggregation is unexplored and could better capture inter-profile interactions in the multiprofile setting. This experiment (config_022) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the validated best components (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion), making it a clean, minimal exploitation step. With 5 experiments remaining, testing the single most impactful untested dimension (aggregation) on the proven-best backbone is the highest-value use of this slot, as a positive result would establish a new best config to build upon, while a null result would confirm avgpool sufficiency and free remaining budget for other axes (e.g., image encoder or profile setting).

Evidence: The best config so far is config_020 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, acc=0.6352). PCA (pca_n2000) outperforms scgpt (0.5176) by a wide margin, avgpool beats transformer (0.5856 vs 0.6352), and weighted fusion slightly edges concat. The one major untested RNA encoder with the best other settings is scvi_n200. Question: Can a learned variational autoencoder (scvi_n200) capture richer RNA structure than a fixed PCA projection while keeping all other components at their empirically best values (imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted)? Why this is the best use: It isolates the single highest-impact untested variable (RNA encoder type) while holding all other knobs at their known-optimal settings, maximizing the chance of either finding a new best or confirming PCA's sufficiency—critical information with only 4 experiments remaining.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted (config_007, acc=0.7062) dramatically outperforms all other tested configurations, with the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 >> pca_n2000 >> scgpt) being the dominant factor. However, we have only tested imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder with scvi_n200. Config_014 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) keeps the proven-best aggregation (avgpool) and fusion (weighted) while testing whether a different image encoder could further improve or at least match the current best. This is the best use of experiment 7 because: (1) it isolates the image encoder axis with all other parameters at their known-optimal values, (2) it reduces uncertainty about whether the 0.7062 result is specific to imagenet_vit_l or generalizable, and (3) with 3 experiments remaining, confirming or refuting the image encoder choice will guide whether to exploit the current best or explore alternative combinations in the final experiments.

The best result so far is config_007 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) at 0.706 accuracy. The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 as RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as image encoder, and avgpool over transformer. However, the fusion method (weighted vs concat) has only been tested with pca_n2000 (0.635 vs 0.629, a small gap). This experiment tests whether concat fusion is competitive with weighted fusion when paired with the superior scvi_n200 encoder. If concat performs comparably or better, it could reveal a different optimal configuration; if weighted is confirmed superior, it solidifies config_007 as the best and frees the remaining 2 experiments to explore other axes (e.g., singleprofile variants). This is the highest-information single test closest to the current best, making it the best use of experiment 8 with only 2 remaining.

The current best is config_034 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 acc. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l as the best image encoder, with concat slightly outperforming weighted fusion. The only untested dimension for this top combination is aggregation: transformer has not been tried with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l. While transformer underperformed avgpool with the weaker pca_n2000 encoder (0.586 vs 0.635), the richer scvi_n200 representations may interact differently with attention-based aggregation. config_033 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) is the direct, minimal extension of the best config, testing whether transformer aggregation can push accuracy above 0.715. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, exploiting the strongest known direction on its most uncertain axis is the highest-expected-value choice.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the dominant design space, with the top three results (0.721, 0.715, 0.706) all in this space. The 2×2 grid of aggregation (avgpool/transformer) × fusion (weighted/concat) has three corners tested: avgpool+weighted=0.706, avgpool+concat=0.715, transformer+concat=0.721. The only untested corner is transformer+weighted (config_015). Since transformer aggregation provided a ~0.5% boost over avgpool with concat, it is plausible that it also lifts the weighted fusion variant, potentially approaching or exceeding the current best of 0.721. As this is the final experiment, completing this grid is the highest-value exploitation move: it tests the one remaining combination in the proven best space and has the best prior probability of matching or beating the current champion. No other untested configuration (resnet50 variants, singleprofile, other RNA encoders) has evidence supporting performance above 0.70.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment must establish a meaningful baseline in the multimodal design space. I choose config_028 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, concat fusion) because: (1) it directly tests the core multimodal hypothesis with well-established, standard components (scgpt for RNA, ResNet-50 for images, simple concatenation for fusion), reducing the risk of confounding multiple novel choices; (2) singleprofile keeps the architecture simple, isolating the signal from modality combination rather than profile aggregation complexity; (3) concat is the most straightforward fusion, providing a clean reference point. This baseline will let me determine in subsequent experiments whether switching to multiprofile, a different RNA encoder (pca/scvi), a stronger image encoder (ViT-L), or a different fusion (weighted/transformer) yields meaningful gains, efficiently partitioning the 9 remaining experiments across the most impactful design axes.

Evidence: config_028 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, concat) achieved 42.7% accuracy, which is modest and suggests a bottleneck in one of the modalities. Uncertainty: it's unclear whether the image encoder (ResNet50) is a limiting factor compared to the RNA encoder or fusion strategy. This experiment (config_002) is a clean A/B test that changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while holding all other settings identical (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, no aggregation, concat fusion). ViT-L is a substantially stronger image backbone, so this directly tests whether image representation quality is the primary bottleneck. If accuracy improves meaningfully, we gain a strong direction to exploit in remaining experiments (e.g., adding multiprofile/transformer aggregation on top of ViT-L). If it does not improve, we learn the image modality is not the bottleneck and should pivot to RNA encoder or fusion strategy. With 8 experiments remaining, this single-variable test maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful design axis before committing to further structural changes.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_028, config_002) show that imagenet_vit_l slightly outperforms resnet50 (0.4348 vs 0.4275 acc) under the same multimodal/singleprofile/scgpt/concat setup, but the difference is small and based on only two data points. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether the fusion strategy (concat vs weighted) matters, which is a key design choice for combining two modalities. This experiment (config_017) tests weighted fusion while holding all other variables at the best-known settings (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, no aggregation). It is a single-variable change from the current best, making the result interpretable. If weighted fusion improves accuracy, it indicates the modalities have unequal contribution and we should explore weighting further; if not, we can rule out fusion as a lever and redirect budget toward profile setting or RNA encoder choices. With 7 experiments remaining, this targeted, low-risk test efficiently reduces uncertainty about an important architectural dimension before committing to larger structural changes.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_002 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + concat, singleprofile) at 0.4348 acc, with concat outperforming weighted fusion (0.4348 vs 0.4224). All three experiments used singleprofile, leaving the multiprofile dimension completely unexplored. Question: Does aggregating multiple profiles via avgpool improve over singleprofile while retaining the best-performing scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/concat combination? Why this is the best next experiment: config_016 is the most controlled extension of the current best, changing only the profile setting (single→multi) and adding a simple avgpool aggregation. This isolates the effect of multiprofile with minimal confounding (no complex transformer aggregation), giving a clear signal on whether multiprofile is a productive direction before committing remaining budget to more complex variants like transformer aggregation.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile + avgpool + imagenet_vit_l + scgpt + concat (config_016, acc=0.5176) dramatically outperforms all singleprofile configs (~0.42-0.43), indicating that multiprofile aggregation is the key lever. The next logical single-variable extension is to test whether a more expressive aggregation mechanism (transformer) can further improve over avgpool while keeping all other settings identical to the best config. This directly tests whether learned inter-profile interactions (transformer) add value beyond simple averaging, which is the most important remaining uncertainty about the aggregation design. From singleprofile evidence, concat fusion outperformed weighted fusion, so I keep concat. This is the highest-information experiment: if transformer aggregation helps, it opens a strong exploitation path; if it doesn't, it confirms avgpool is near-optimal and we can pivot to other variables (RNA encoder, image encoder) with the remaining 5 experiments.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat (config_016, acc=0.5176) is the best configuration, substantially outperforming all singleprofile variants (~0.43). Within this top setup, we have only tested scgpt as the RNA encoder. config_010 isolates the RNA encoder choice by swapping scgpt → scvi_n200 while holding all other hyperparameters (multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) constant. This is the cleanest A/B test to determine whether the RNA encoder is a bottleneck or whether the current 0.5176 ceiling is driven by the aggregation/fusion/image-encoder choices. If scvi_n200 matches or beats scgpt, it opens a new optimization axis; if it underperforms, it confirms scgpt's value and focuses remaining budget on fusion/aggregation refinements. With 4 experiments left, resolving this key design variable is the highest-information next step before committing to fine-tuning the best pipeline.

The strongest result so far is config_010 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy, which dwarfs all other configs. The key question is whether a more expressive aggregation strategy can push performance further. With scgpt, avgpool (0.518) marginally beat transformer (0.507), but that gap was small (~1%) and based on a much weaker RNA encoder. With scvi_n200 producing far richer profile representations, transformer aggregation could capture non-linear inter-profile interactions that simple averaging misses. Config_007 is a single-variable change from the best config (avgpool → transformer), keeping all other winning components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, concat). This is the most focused exploitation of the strongest evidence while testing the highest-impact remaining design choice. With 3 experiments left after this, a clear signal here would guide the final experiments toward either further refinement or confirming the optimum.

The strongest evidence points to multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the dominant configuration (config_007: 0.7207, config_010: 0.7150), with transformer aggregation slightly outperforming avgpool. The only untested variation within this proven space is fusion type: all top results used concat. Config_029 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) directly tests whether weighted fusion can improve upon concat in the best-performing setup. This is a minimal, targeted change that reduces uncertainty about the last remaining design dimension in the proven configuration. With only 2 experiments left after this, exploiting the strongest direction with a focused ablation is the highest-value use of experiment 8: if weighted fusion helps, we gain a new best; if not, we confirm concat is optimal and can use remaining budget on secondary variations (e.g., resnet50 with scvi_n200) without wasting an experiment on a clearly inferior direction.

The top three experiments (config_029: 0.7250, config_007: 0.7207, config_010: 0.7150) all share scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile, forming a 2x2 grid over aggregation (transformer/avgpool) and fusion (concat/weighted). Three cells are filled; config_048 (avgpool + weighted) is the only missing cell. Evidence shows weighted fusion improves over concat by ~0.4% with transformer (0.7250 vs 0.7207) and avgpool underperforms transformer by ~0.6% with concat (0.7150 vs 0.7207). Testing avgpool+weighted clarifies whether the weighted-fusion gain is aggregation-independent or specific to transformer. If it outperforms config_029, we find a new best; if not, we confirm transformer+weighted as the optimal combination in this dominant family. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, completing the grid in the highest-performing region is the most informative and highest-expected-value use of the budget.

The best configuration found (config_029: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250) has fully explored the optimal encoder/profile/aggregation/fusion space, with all four aggregation×fusion combinations tested. No remaining configuration is likely to exceed this. For this final experiment, config_031 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted) is the best choice because it retains the three strongest design choices (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer+weighted) and tests only the image encoder downgrade to resnet50. This isolates the marginal contribution of imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50 in the optimized pipeline, which is the most informative remaining question. The small resnet50 penalty observed in singleprofile (0.427 vs 0.435) suggests the gap may be modest, making this the highest-expected-accuracy untested configuration and the most logical exploitation of the strong transformer+weighted+scvi_n200 evidence.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment must establish a reliable baseline for the multimodal setting. config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) uses the most standard and well-validated components: ResNet50 as a robust image encoder, scVI-200 as a standard single-cell RNA encoder, multiprofile to leverage profile diversity, simple avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion to let the model learn modality importance. This 'central' configuration tests the core hypothesis that combining image and RNA modalities improves accuracy. Its result will anchor all subsequent comparisons: if it performs well, later experiments can exploit by swapping individual components (e.g., ViT-L, scGPT, transformer aggregation); if it underperforms, single-modality baselines (experiments 2-3) can isolate which component is the bottleneck. This maximizes information gain per experiment under a tight 10-experiment budget.

The sole data point (config_018: multimodal/multiprofile/scvi_n200/resnet50/avgpool/weighted → 0.678 acc) establishes a baseline but leaves the impact of the image encoder completely untested. Config_005 is a minimal, controlled change: it swaps resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l while holding every other variable (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool, weighted) constant. This directly tests whether a substantially more powerful image backbone can push accuracy higher, which is likely the single largest lever available. If ViT-L yields a clear gain, it re-centers the search around a stronger image encoder; if it does not, we learn ResNet50 is sufficient and can redirect effort toward RNA encoder, aggregation, or fusion choices. With 8 experiments remaining, this clean A/B comparison maximizes information per trial and avoids prematurely committing to a suboptimal image backbone.

Evidence: config_005 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.706 acc / 0.667 F1, outperforming config_018 (same but resnet50) by ~2.9% acc, establishing imagenet_vit_l as the stronger image encoder. Both experiments used avgpool aggregation, leaving the aggregation mechanism untested. Question: config_032 tests whether transformer aggregation (vs avgpool) further improves performance when paired with the stronger ViT-L encoder, while keeping all other settings identical to the current best. This is a clean single-variable change from config_005, isolating the effect of aggregation. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, reducing uncertainty about whether avgpool is a bottleneck for multimodal fusion is critical. Transformer aggregation is a more expressive way to combine multiprofile representations and could complement the attention-based ViT-L encoder. If it improves on 0.706, it opens a high-performing branch to further refine; if not, it confirms avgpool sufficiency and redirects budget toward RNA encoder or fusion strategy.

Evidence: Across 3 experiments, the best configuration (config_032, acc=0.7250) uses multimodal/multiprofile/scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/weighted. The image encoder (resnet50→ViT-L, +2.9pp) and aggregation (avgpool→transformer, +1.9pp) improvements are now well-established. The RNA encoder remains unexplored in this optimal setting. It directly extends the winning trajectory along the most impactful untested axis, and the result will inform whether to continue refining around scgpt or scvi_n200 for the remaining budget.

The best result so far (config_032, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion. All top configs use weighted fusion, so the fusion strategy is an unexplored axis with the strongest backbone. Config_029 isolates this one variable (weighted → concat) while keeping all other settings at their best-performing values. This is a low-risk, high-information experiment: if concat matches or exceeds weighted, it opens a new optimization direction; if not, it confirms weighted fusion is optimal for this architecture. With 5 experiments remaining, exploiting the proven backbone while testing the one untested fusion variant is the most efficient use of the next slot.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_032 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc=0.7250), with config_029 (concat fusion) very close at 0.7207. scgpt is clearly inferior (0.5200), and imagenet_vit_l + transformer dominates resnet50 + avgpool. However, the RNA encoder dimension remains underexplored—only scvi_n200 and scgpt have been tested. Question: config_047 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates the RNA encoder choice by swapping scvi_n200 for PCA while keeping all other parameters at their best-known values. Why this is the best use: With 4 experiments remaining, resolving whether PCA is competitive is the highest-information experiment—it either opens a new family of configurations to exploit or confirms scvi_n200 as essential, allowing the remaining budget to focus on fine-tuning the scvi_n200 + vit_l + transformer architecture (e.g., singleprofile variant, fusion ablation).

Evidence: All 6 completed experiments used multiprofile, and the best (config_032: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) reached 0.7250. The single-profile dimension is completely untested, creating significant uncertainty about whether multiprofile + transformer aggregation is truly superior or whether single profile with the same strong encoders could match or exceed it. This experiment (config_017: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) directly tests that question using the best-known RNA and image encoders with the slightly better fusion strategy. It is the best use of experiment 7 because: (1) it resolves a major unexplored design axis before committing the remaining 3 experiments to refinement, (2) it leverages the strongest components already validated, and (3) if single profile performs comparably, it opens a new search space; if it underperforms, it confirms multiprofile is essential and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning the multiprofile configuration.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the dominant combination (0.725 best vs. 0.52–0.68 for all other RNA/image/profile pairings). Within this top subspace, we have tested transformer+weighted (0.725), transformer+concat (0.721), and avgpool+weighted (0.706). Config_051 (avgpool+concat) is the only remaining untested configuration in this best-performing subspace, completing the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid. While transformer+weighted is expected to remain best, testing config_051 definitively closes the exploration of the most promising region with minimal budget waste. With only 2 experiments left after this one, spending them on clearly inferior combinations (different RNA encoders, resnet50, or singleprofile) would be low-value; confirming the landscape of the top subspace is the highest-information use of this slot.

The best result so far is config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile, acc=0.7250). All four aggregation×fusion combinations for the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile region have been tested, confirming transformer+weighted as the top configuration. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation benefit (+1.9% over avgpool with ViT-L) is generalizable or specific to the stronger image encoder. Config_014 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) fills the last missing cell in the resnet50 aggregation matrix (we only have avgpool+weighted=0.6776 from config_018). This clarifies whether the architectural gain from transformer aggregation is encoder-agnostic, which is important for understanding the design space. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, this is the highest-information experiment: if it approaches 0.70+, it confirms transformer aggregation is broadly beneficial; if it stays near 0.68, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is the critical factor. No untested configuration in the fully-explored best region can plausibly exceed 0.7250, so this exploratory test is the best use of the slot.

The best result so far is config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). All four aggregation×fusion combinations for that encoder pair have been tested. The next closest untested variant is config_043 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat, multiprofile). Evidence: config_014 (same but weighted fusion) achieved acc=0.7131 with the highest F1 (0.6945) of any tested config, suggesting strong class separation in this encoder pair. The pattern shows concat outperforms weighted with avgpool (0.715 vs 0.706 for ViT), so testing concat with transformer+resnet50 completes the 2×2 grid and probes whether the high-F1 signal in config_014 can be leveraged by a different fusion strategy. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability untested configuration to either match or exceed the current best, while also reducing residual uncertainty about the fusion choice for transformer aggregation.

With no prior experiments, I need to establish a strong reference point. Config_006 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) combines the most promising components in each design dimension: a learned single-cell RNA encoder (scgpt) over PCA, a large pretrained image encoder (ViT-L), the most expressive aggregation (transformer), and the richest data regime (multiprofile). Testing this 'full-power' multimodal configuration first establishes the performance ceiling of the approach. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components (e.g., swap scgpt→pca, ViT-L→ResNet50, transformer→avgpool) to identify which choices drive accuracy. If it underperforms, I learn early that the ceiling is low and can pivot to simpler or single-modality baselines. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-run budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_006: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted → 52.0% acc), we have very sparse evidence and high uncertainty about which architectural choices are driving performance. The most informative next step is a clean single-variable ablation: config_003 changes only the aggregation from transformer to avgpool while keeping the same RNA encoder (scgpt), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), profile setting (multiprofile), and fusion (weighted). This directly tests whether the more complex transformer aggregation is actually contributing meaningful gain over a simpler average-pooling strategy, or whether it is overfitting/underperforming. If avgpool matches or exceeds transformer, we can eliminate the transformer branch from further exploration and redirect remaining budget toward encoder and fusion choices. If transformer clearly wins, we gain confidence to build on that architecture. This is the best use of experiment 2 because it isolates one critical design variable with a direct comparison to our only data point, maximizing information gain per experiment under the 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_006 vs config_003) show that avgpool aggregation outperforms transformer by ~2.2% accuracy with scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion, establishing avgpool as the preferred aggregation. The current best (config_003, acc=0.542) uses scgpt as the RNA encoder, but we have no evidence yet about whether this complex learned representation actually adds value over a simpler PCA baseline. Question: config_002 is an exact A/B test against config_003, changing only the RNA encoder from scgpt to pca_n2000 while keeping imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, and multiprofile fixed. This isolates the RNA encoder's contribution. Why this is the best next step: With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether scgpt is genuinely superior to PCA is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact decision. If PCA matches or beats scgpt, it frees us from a potentially overfit encoder and redirects exploration; if scgpt clearly wins, we can confidently build further extensions around it. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty in the design space.

Evidence: config_002 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is the clear best at 0.635 acc, showing pca_n2000 substantially outperforms scgpt (~9 pt gap) and avgpool edges out transformer. Question: Does the image encoder choice (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) matter with the superior pca_n2000 RNA encoder? This is a single-variable change from the best config, isolating the image encoder effect. Why: The image encoder is a fundamental architectural decision that will guide the remaining 6 experiments. If resnet50 is competitive, it broadens the search space; if imagenet_vit_l is clearly superior, we can focus subsequent experiments on fusion and profile variations with that encoder. This reduces uncertainty on the most impactful untested dimension of the current best configuration.

The top two experiments (config_002: 0.635, config_041: 0.639) both use pca_n2000 + avgpool + weighted fusion, with the image encoder making negligible difference. The scgpt experiments (0.520-0.542) are far behind, confirming pca_n2000 is the critical choice. The most impactful untested variable within the best-performing sub-space is the fusion strategy: weighted vs concat. Config_010 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) is a single-variable change from the current best (config_041), cleanly isolating whether concat fusion—letting the model learn cross-modal interactions rather than relying on a fixed weighted sum—can push accuracy above 0.639. With 5 experiments remaining, this controlled test of a fundamental architectural choice is the highest-value next step before exploring profile setting or scvi_n200.

Evidence: The RNA encoder is the dominant factor (pca_n2000: ~0.635-0.639 vs scgpt: ~0.52-0.54), and the best config (config_041: pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted = 0.639) has not been tested with scvi_n200. Uncertainty: scvi_n200 is a learned 200-dim variational latent space, fundamentally different from both linear PCA and transformer-based scGPT; it may capture nonlinear cell-type structure that PCA misses. This experiment isolates the scvi_n200 encoder while holding all other components at their empirically best values (resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile), making it a clean single-variable test. It is the best use of this slot because the RNA encoder axis has the largest observed effect size, scvi_n200 is completely untested, and knowing whether it is competitive with PCA will determine how to allocate the remaining 4 experiments (exploit PCA further vs. pivot to scvi_n200 combinations).

Evidence: config_049 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.678) is the clear best, establishing scvi_n200 as the dominant RNA encoder and avgpool+weighted as the preferred architecture. The image encoder comparison (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) was only tested with pca_n2000 (0.639 vs 0.635, a small gap). Question: Does imagenet_vit_l match or exceed resnet50 when paired with the superior scvi_n200 encoder, holding the proven-best avgpool+weighted fixed? This is a clean single-variable test of the one remaining unexplored dimension in the top-performing region. Rationale: With 3 experiments left after this one, exploiting the strongest direction (scvi_n200) while resolving the image-encoder uncertainty is the highest-value move. If imagenet_vit_l performs comparably, it confirms resnet50's edge is minimal; if it underperforms, it locks in resnet50 and frees remaining budget for other refinements.

The current best (config_020: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706) strongly establishes scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoders. The one untested structural variable with this top combination is aggregation method: we know transformer underperformed avgpool with scgpt (0.520 vs 0.542), but scvi_n200 produces a learned variational latent that may interact differently with attention-based aggregation than scgpt's encoder output. Config_028 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) isolates this single variable. If transformer improves, we gain a new best; if not, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can spend the remaining 2 experiments testing concat fusion (config_036) or other refinements. This is the highest-information experiment for the most promising configuration family with 2 slots left.

The current best (config_028: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 accuracy. All evidence strongly supports this family: scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 > scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 for image, and transformer > avgpool for aggregation. The only untested variant in this top family is the fusion choice—config_008 tests concat fusion with transformer aggregation. While weighted has outperformed concat under avgpool (config_041 vs config_010), the interaction between transformer aggregation and concat fusion is untested and could theoretically capture complementary cross-modal interactions. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the last untried combination in the clearly dominant configuration family is the highest-value exploitation move, as it either confirms weighted is optimal or discovers a better fusion-aggregation synergy.

The best result so far is config_028 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725). The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 as RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as image encoder, and transformer aggregation over avgpool (~0.02 gain). The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation benefit is specific to ViT's patch structure or generalizable across image encoders. Config_024 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) directly tests this: we know scvi_n200+resnet50+avgpool+weighted gives 0.678, so if transformer adds a similar ~0.02 boost, we'd expect ~0.70. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, this is the most logical exploitation of the strongest evidence (scvi_n200 + transformer + weighted) and clarifies whether the top configuration's advantage is due to the ViT-transformer synergy or a more general transformer benefit—critical for confirming that 0.725 represents the true optimum of this design space with the final experiment.

With no prior evidence, the goal is to establish a strong reference point in the most promising region of the design space. Config_020 combines the strongest available components: multimodal (both RNA and image), multiprofile (richer per-cell information), scgpt (a powerful pretrained generative RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (a large ViT image encoder), transformer aggregation (the most expressive pooling strategy for multiple profiles), and concat fusion (information-preserving, letting the classifier learn the optimal combination). Testing this 'all-strong' configuration first will (1) establish an upper-bound baseline, (2) confirm whether the multimodal + multiprofile paradigm is beneficial, and (3) provide a reference against which subsequent ablations (e.g., swapping to resnet50, avgpool, weighted fusion, or singleprofile) can be interpreted. Under a tight 10-experiment budget, anchoring the search with the most capable configuration maximizes the chance that the best-so-far accuracy is already competitive, while still leaving 9 experiments to explore and refine.

With only one completed experiment (config_020: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat → acc 0.507), evidence is extremely sparse. The most informative next step is a single-variable A/B test on the fusion strategy, since fusion is the final integration step and likely has outsized impact on how well the two modalities are combined. config_032 is identical to config_020 except fusion changes from concat to weighted. This directly clarifies whether weighted fusion (which learns a scalar reweighting of the two modalities) outperforms simple concatenation under the same backbone. If weighted wins, we gain a strong signal to explore weighted-fusion variants across encoders; if concat wins or ties, we can rule out fusion as a bottleneck and pivot to testing aggregation (avgpool vs transformer) or RNA encoder choice. This minimal-change comparison maximally reduces uncertainty about a critical design axis with one experiment, preserving budget for subsequent exploitation.

This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the dominant RNA encoder (0.72 vs 0.51 for scgpt), and the current best config (config_012, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. If resnet50 is competitive, it broadens the search space; if not, it confirms imagenet_vit_l and lets us focus remaining budget on aggregation/fusion/profile refinements. This is a single-variable change from the current best, making the result interpretable.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the dominant RNA encoder (~0.72 vs ~0.51 for scgpt), imagenet_vit_l slightly edges resnet50 in accuracy, and weighted fusion is marginally better than concat. The current best (config_012: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) uses transformer aggregation. The one untested aggregation with this top combination is avgpool. Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant factor (0.71–0.725 vs ~0.52 for scgpt), and within scvi_n200 multimodal multiprofile configs, transformer aggregation and imagenet_vit_l are the strongest components. Evidence: scvi_n200 dramatically outperforms scgpt (0.725 vs 0.520) in the best multimodal setup (imagenet_vit_l + transformer), and weighted fusion edges out concat. Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (multiprofile) is the clear best at 0.725, and weighted fusion consistently outperforms concat across all tested pairings. The best configuration found is config_012 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong multimodal baseline using the most expressive components to set a high performance bar and reduce uncertainty about whether the full multimodal pipeline is viable. config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) combines a pretrained RNA foundation model (scgpt), the strongest image encoder (ViT-L), the most expressive aggregation (transformer), and a flexible learned fusion (weighted). With only one completed experiment (config_037: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion, acc≈0.52), the most important uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation layer is actually contributing meaningful performance over a simpler alternative. Evidence: Both completed experiments (config_037, config_016) share scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion + multiprofile, differing only in aggregation (transformer=0.520 vs avgpool=0.542), suggesting avgpool is preferable. However, we have zero information about whether the RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) materially affects performance. Question: config_045 keeps all best-known settings (avgpool, weighted, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile) and swaps scgpt for scvi_n200, isolating the RNA encoder as the single variable. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether a learned VAE (scvi_n200) can match or beat the generative pre-trained scgpt will either open a new promising branch or confirm scgpt as the anchor, allowing subsequent experiments to focus on image encoder, fusion, and profile-setting choices with higher confidence.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 as RNA encoder dramatically outperforms scgpt (0.706 vs ~0.52-0.54) with the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted). The current best (config_045) uses imagenet_vit_l, but we have no data on how the image encoder interacts with scvi_n200. config_007 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the cleanest single-variable test: it changes only the image encoder from the current best, isolating whether resnet50 provides complementary or superior visual features when paired with the scvi_n200 RNA representation. This is the highest-impact untested dimension (image encoder is more fundamental than aggregation, which showed only ~2% difference with scgpt), and resolving it early with 6 experiments remaining will guide the rest of the search toward the best image-RNA pairing.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the superior RNA encoder (0.706/0.678 vs 0.520/0.542 for scgpt), and imagenet_vit_l outperforms resnet50 with scvi_n200 (0.706 vs 0.678). The best config (config_045) uses avgpool+weighted. However, the avgpool>transformer finding was only observed with the weaker scgpt encoder; with scvi_n200's richer latent representations, transformer aggregation may better capture cross-modal interactions.
